12.s:
sukeśiruvāca /
karmaṇā narakānetān kena gacchanti vai katham /
etad vadantu viprendrāḥ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ mama //
12.d:
सुकेशिरुवाच ।
कर्मणा नरकानेतान् केन गच्छन्ति वै कथम् ।
एतद् वदन्तु विप्रेन्द्राः परं कौतूहलं मम ॥
12.m:
Sukeśin said:
By what action do they go to these hells, and how?
Let the best of Brahmins tell this; my curiosity is great.

12.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ /
karmaṇā yena yeneha yānti śālakaṭaṅkaṭa /
svakarmaphalabhogārthaṃ narakān me śṛṇuṣva tān //
12.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
कर्मणा येन येनेह यान्ति शालकटङ्कट ।
स्वकर्मफलभोगार्थं नरकान् मे शृणुष्व तान् ॥
12.m:
The sages said:
By whichever action here they go, O Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa,
to the hells to experience the fruit of their own deeds, hear that from me.

12.s:
vedavevadvijātīnāṃ yairnindā satataṃ kṛtā /
ye purāṇetihāsārthān nābhinandanti pāpinaḥ //
kurunindākarā ye ca sakhavighnakarāśca ye /
dāturnivārakāye ca teṣu te nipatanti hi / /
12.d:
वेदवेवद्विजातीनां यैर्निन्दा सततं कृता ।
ये पुराणेतिहासार्थान् नाभिनन्दन्ति पापिनः ॥
कुरुनिन्दाकरा ये च सखविघ्नकराश्च ये ।
दातुर्निवारकाये च तेषु ते निपतन्ति हि । ।
12.m:
Those by whom reviling of the Vedas, the gods, and the twice-born is constantly done,
and the sinners who do not welcome the truths of the Purāṇas and Itihāsas;

Those who revile the Kurus, and those who obstruct their friends,
and those who dissuade a giver—upon them indeed they fall.

12.s:
12.4 suhṛddampatisodaryasvāmibhṛtyapitāsutān /
yājyopādhyāyayoryaiśca kṛto bhedo 'dhamairmithaḥ //
12.d:
12.4 सुहृद्दम्पतिसोदर्यस्वामिभृत्यपितासुतान् ।
याज्योपाध्याययोर्यैश्च कृतो भेदो ऽधमैर्मिथः ॥
12.m:
Between friend and friend, husband and wife, brothers, master and servant, father and son,
and between patron and priest—those low men by whom division is created among them,

12.s:
kanyāmekasya dattvā ca dadatyanyasya ye 'dhamāḥ /
karapatreṇa pāṭyante te dvidhā yamakiṅkaraiḥ //
12.d:
कन्यामेकस्य दत्त्वा च ददत्यन्यस्य ये ऽधमाः ।
करपत्रेण पाट्यन्ते ते द्विधा यमकिङ्करैः ॥
12.m:
and the vile who, having promised a maiden to one, give her to another,
they are split in two with a saw by the servants of Yama.

12.s:
paropatāpajanakāścandanośīrahāriṇaḥ /
bālavyajanaharttāraḥ karambhasikatāśritāḥ //
12.d:
परोपतापजनकाश्चन्दनोशीरहारिणः ।
बालव्यजनहर्त्तारः करम्भसिकताश्रिताः ॥
12.m:
Those who cause torment to others, stealers of sandalwood and uśīra,
and stealers of horsehair whisks, dwell in Karambhasikatā.

12.s:
nimantrito 'nyato bhuṅkte śrāddhe daive sapaitṛke /
sa dvidhā kṛṣyate mūḍhastīkṣṇatuṇḍaiḥ khagottamaiḥ //
12.d:
निमन्त्रितो ऽन्यतो भुङ्क्ते श्राद्धे दैवे सपैतृके ।
स द्विधा कृष्यते मूढस्तीक्ष्णतुण्डैः खगोत्तमैः ॥
12.m:
When invited, one who dines elsewhere during a rite to the gods and ancestral śrāddha,
that fool is torn in two by the sharp-beaked foremost birds.

12.s:
marmāṇi yastu sādhūnāṃ tudan vāgbhirnikṛntati /
tasyopari tudantastu tuṇḍaistiṣṭhanti pattriṇaḥ //
12.d:
मर्माणि यस्तु साधूनां तुदन् वाग्भिर्निकृन्तति ।
तस्योपरि तुदन्तस्तु तुण्डैस्तिष्ठन्ति पत्त्रिणः ॥
12.m:
He who pierces the vitals of the virtuous, cutting [them] with his words,
upon him the birds stand, pecking with their beaks.

12.s:
yaḥ karoti ca paiśunyaṃ sādhūnāmanyathāmatiḥ /
vajratuṇḍanakhā jihvāmākarṣante 'sya vāyasāḥ //
12.d:
यः करोति च पैशुन्यं साधूनामन्यथामतिः ।
वज्रतुण्डनखा जिह्वामाकर्षन्ते ऽस्य वायसाः ॥
12.m:
And he of wicked mind who slanders the virtuous,
crows with vajra-like beaks and talons tear out his tongue.

12.s:
mātāpitṛgurūṇāṃ ca ye 'vajñāṃ cakruruddhatāḥ /
majjante pūyavimmūtre tpratiṣṭhe hyadhosukhāḥ //
12.d:
मातापितृगुरूणां च ये ऽवज्ञां चक्रुरुद्धताः ।
मज्जन्ते पूयविम्मूत्रे त्प्रतिष्ठे ह्यधोसुखाः ॥
12.m:
And those arrogant ones who showed contempt for mother, father, and teachers,
sink head-downward into pus, feces, and urine in Apratiṣṭha.

12.s:
devatātithibhūteṣu bhṛtyeṣvabhyāgateṣu ca /
abhuktavatsu ye 'śnanti bālapitragnimātṛṣu //
12.d:
देवतातिथिभूतेषु भृत्येष्वभ्यागतेषु च ।
अभुक्तवत्सु ये ऽश्नन्ति बालपित्रग्निमातृषु ॥
12.m:
When gods, guests, living beings, servants, and new arrivals,
children, fathers, the sacred fires, and mothers have not yet eaten, those who eat—

12.s:
duṣṭacāsṛkpūyaniryāsaṃ bhuñjate tvadhamā ime /
sūcīmukhāśca jāyante kṣudhārttā girivigrahāḥ //
12.d:
दुष्टचासृक्पूयनिर्यासं भुञ्जते त्वधमा इमे ।
सूचीमुखाश्च जायन्ते क्षुधार्त्ता गिरिविग्रहाः ॥
12.m:
these vile men consume vile blood and exudate of pus;
and with mouths like needles, afflicted with hunger, they become mountain-sized in body.

12.s:
ekapaṅktyupaviṣṭānāṃ viṣamaṃ bhojayanti ye /
viḍbhojanaṃ rākṣasendra narakaṃ te vrajanti ca //
12.d:
एकपङ्क्त्युपविष्टानां विषमं भोजयन्ति ये ।
विड्भोजनं राक्षसेन्द्र नरकं ते व्रजन्ति च ॥
12.m:
Those who feed unequally those seated in a single row,
they go, O king of rākṣasas, to the hell of eating feces.

12.s:
ekasārthaprayātaṃ ye paśyantaścārthinaṃ narāḥ /
asaṃvibhajya bhuñjanti te yānti śleṣmabhojanam //
12.d:
एकसार्थप्रयातं ये पश्यन्तश्चार्थिनं नराः ।
असंविभज्य भुञ्जन्ति ते यान्ति श्लेष्मभोजनम् ॥
12.m:
Men who see a beggar traveling in the same caravan,
and eat without sharing, go to the eating of phlegm.

12.s:
gobrāhṇaṇāgnayaḥ spṛṣṭā yairucchiṣṭaiḥ kṣapācara /
kṣipyante hi karāsteṣāṃ taptasumbhe sudāruṇe //
12.d:
गोब्राह्णणाग्नयः स्पृष्टा यैरुच्छिष्टैः क्षपाचर ।
क्षिप्यन्ते हि करास्तेषां तप्तसुम्भे सुदारुणे ॥
12.m:
By whom cows, Brahmins, and fires were touched while impure from eating, O night-wanderer,
their hands are cast into the most dreadful Taptakumbha.

12.s:
sūryendutārakā dṛṣṭā yairucchiṣṭaiśca kāmataḥ /
teṣāṃ netragato vahnirdhamyate yamakiṅkaraiḥ //
12.d:
सूर्येन्दुतारका दृष्टा यैरुच्छिष्टैश्च कामतः ।
तेषां नेत्रगतो वह्निर्धम्यते यमकिङ्करैः ॥
12.m:
By whom the sun, moon, and stars were looked upon willfully while impure from eating,
the fire in their eyes is blown into by the servants of Yama.

12.s:
mitrajāyātha jananī jyeṣṭho bhrātā pitā svasā /
jāmayo guravo vṛddhā yaiḥ saṃspṛṣṭāḥ padā nṛbhiḥ //
12.d:
मित्रजायाथ जननी ज्येष्ठो भ्राता पिता स्वसा ।
जामयो गुरवो वृद्धा यैः संस्पृष्टाः पदा नृभिः ॥
12.m:
A friend's wife, a mother, an elder brother, a father, a sister,
female relatives, teachers, and elders, who have been touched with the foot by men—

12.s:
baddhāṅghrayaste vigaḍairlohairvāhnipratāpitaiḥ /
kṣipyante raurave ghore hyājānuparidāhinaḥ //
12.d:
बद्धाङ्घ्रयस्ते विगडैर्लोहैर्वाह्निप्रतापितैः ।
क्षिप्यन्ते रौरवे घोरे ह्याजानुपरिदाहिनः ॥
12.m:
their feet bound with iron fetters heated by fire,
they are cast into the dreadful Raurava, burning up to their knees.

12.s:
pāyasaṃ kṛśaraṃ māṃsaṃ vṛthā bhuktāni yairnaraiḥ /
teṣāmayoguḍāstaptāḥ kṣipyante vadane 'dbhutāḥ //
12.d:
पायसं कृशरं मांसं वृथा भुक्तानि यैर्नरैः ।
तेषामयोगुडास्तप्ताः क्षिप्यन्ते वदने ऽद्भुताः ॥
12.m:
Pāyasa, kṛśara, and meat eaten in vain by men,
into their mouths terrifying, heated iron balls are cast.

12.s:
gurudevadvijātīnāṃ vedānāṃ ca narādhamaiḥ /
nindā niśāmitā yaistu pāpānāmiti kurvatām //
12.d:
गुरुदेवद्विजातीनां वेदानां च नराधमैः ।
निन्दा निशामिता यैस्तु पापानामिति कुर्वताम् ॥
12.m:
By the lowest of men, reviling of teachers, gods, the twice-born,
and the Vedas was listened to, while sinners were doing so—

12.s:
teṣāṃ lohamayāḥ kīlā vahnivarṇāḥ punaḥ punaḥ /
śravaṇeṣu nikhanyante dharmarājasya kiṅkaraiḥ //
12.d:
तेषां लोहमयाः कीला वह्निवर्णाः पुनः पुनः ।
श्रवणेषु निखन्यन्ते धर्मराजस्य किङ्करैः ॥
12.m:
iron spikes of the color of fire are driven again and again
into their ears by the servants of Dharmarāja.

12.s:
prapādevakulālāmān vipraveśmasabhāmaṭhān /
kūpavāpītaḍāgāṃśca bhaṅktvā vidhvaṃsayanti ye //
12.d:
प्रपादेवकुलालामान् विप्रवेश्मसभामठान् ।
कूपवापीतडागांश्च भङ्क्त्वा विध्वंसयन्ति ये ॥
12.m:
Water-booths, temples, gardens, Brahmin dwellings, assembly halls, monasteries,
and wells, tanks, and ponds—those who break and ruin them,

12.s:
teṣāṃ vilapatāṃ carma dehataḥ kriyate pṛthak /
karttikābhiḥ sutīkṣṇībhiḥ suraudrairyamakiṅkaraiḥ //
12.d:
तेषां विलपतां चर्म देहतः क्रियते पृथक् ।
कर्त्तिकाभिः सुतीक्ष्णीभिः सुरौद्रैर्यमकिङ्करैः ॥
12.m:
as they wail, the skin is severed from their bodies
with very sharp knives by the terrifying servants of Yama.

12.s:
gobrāhmaṇārkamagniṃ ca ye vai mehanti mānavāḥ /
teṣāṃ gudeva cāntrāṇi viniḥkṛntanti vāyasāḥ //
12.d:
गोब्राह्मणार्कमग्निं च ये वै मेहन्ति मानवाः ।
तेषां गुदेव चान्त्राणि विनिःकृन्तन्ति वायसाः ॥
12.m:
The men who urinate facing cows, Brahmins, the sun, and fire,
crows tear out their entrails right through the anus.

12.s:
svapoṣaṇaparo yastu parityajati mānavaḥ /
putrabhṛtyakalatrādibandhuvargamakiñcanam /
durbhikṣe saṃbhrame cāpi sa śvabhojye nipātyate //
12.d:
स्वपोषणपरो यस्तु परित्यजति मानवः ।
पुत्रभृत्यकलत्रादिबन्धुवर्गमकिञ्चनम् ।
दुर्भिक्षे संभ्रमे चापि स श्वभोज्ये निपात्यते ॥
12.m:
The man devoted only to feeding himself who abandons
his destitute family—sons, servants, wife, and kin—
in famine and in terror, he is cast into Śvabhojya.

12.s:
śaraṇāgataṃ ye tyajanti ye ca bandhanapālakāḥ /
patanti yantrapīḍe te tāḍya mānāstu kiṅkaraiḥ //
12.d:
शरणागतं ये त्यजन्ति ये च बन्धनपालकाः ।
पतन्ति यन्त्रपीडे ते ताड्य मानास्तु किङ्करैः ॥
12.m:
Those who abandon one who has sought refuge, and prison guards [who torment],
fall into Yantrapīḍa, being beaten by the servants.

12.s:
kleśayanti hi viprādīn ye hyakarmasu pāpinaḥ /
te piṣyante śilāpeṣe śoṣyanate 'pi ca śoṣakaiḥ //
12.d:
क्लेशयन्ति हि विप्रादीन् ये ह्यकर्मसु पापिनः ।
ते पिष्यन्ते शिलापेषे शोष्यनते ऽपि च शोषकैः ॥
12.m:
The sinners who afflict Brahmins and others during unrighteous tasks,
are crushed under a grinding stone and dried out by desiccators.

12.s:
nyāsāpahāriṇaḥ pāpā badhyante nigaḍairapi /
śrutkṣāmāḥ śuṣkatālvoṣṭhāḥ pātyante vṛścikāśane //
12.d:
न्यासापहारिणः पापा बध्यन्ते निगडैरपि ।
श्रुत्क्षामाः शुष्कताल्वोष्ठाः पात्यन्ते वृश्चिकाशने ॥
12.m:
Sinners who steal deposits are bound with chains,
and famished, their palates and lips dried up, they are cast into Vṛścikāśana.

12.s:
parvamaithuninaḥ pāpāḥ paradāraratāśca ye /
te vahnitaptāṃ kūṭāgrāmāliṅgante ca śālmalīm //
12.d:
पर्वमैथुनिनः पापाः परदाररताश्च ये ।
ते वह्नितप्तां कूटाग्रामालिङ्गन्ते च शाल्मलीम् ॥
12.m:
The sinners who copulate on forbidden lunar days, and those devoted to others' wives,
they embrace the fire-heated Kūṭaśālmalī tree with sharp points.

12.s:
upādhyāyamadhaḥkṛtya yairadhītaṃ dvijādhamaiḥ /
teṣāmadhyāpako yaśca sa śilāṃ śirasā vahet //
12.d:
उपाध्यायमधःकृत्य यैरधीतं द्विजाधमैः ।
तेषामध्यापको यश्च स शिलां शिरसा वहेत् ॥
12.m:
By which lowest of twice-born study was done having humiliated the preceptor,
and he who is their instructor, must carry a rock upon his head.

12.s:
mūtraśleṣmapurīṣāṇi yairutsṛṣṭāni vāriṇi /
te pātyante ca viṇmūtre durgandhe pūyapūrite //
12.d:
मूत्रश्लेष्मपुरीषाणि यैरुत्सृष्टानि वारिणि ।
ते पात्यन्ते च विण्मूत्रे दुर्गन्धे पूयपूरिते ॥
12.m:
Those by whom urine, phlegm, and feces were discharged into water,
they are cast into foul-smelling feces and urine, filled with pus.

12.s:
śrāddhātitheyamanyonyaṃ yairbhuktaṃ bhuvi mānavaiḥ /
parasparaṃ bhakṣayante māṃsāni svāni bāliśāḥ //
12.d:
श्राद्धातिथेयमन्योन्यं यैर्भुक्तं भुवि मानवैः ।
परस्परं भक्षयन्ते मांसानि स्वानि बालिशाः ॥
12.m:
Men on earth by whom śrāddha and guest offerings were mutually eaten,
those fools consume each other's flesh.

12.s: vedavahnigurutyāgī bhāryāpitrostathaiva ca/ giriśṛḍgādadhaḥpātaṃ pātyante yamakiṅkaraiḥ //
12.d: वेदवह्निगुरुत्यागी भार्यापित्रोस्तथैव च। गिरिशृड्गादधःपातं पात्यन्ते यमकिङ्करैः ॥
12.m:
One who abandons the Vedas, the sacred fire, his teacher, and likewise his wife and parents,
is thrown down from a mountain peak by the servants of Yama.

12.s:
punarbhūpatayo ye ca kanyāvidhvaṃsakāśca ye /
tadgarbhaśrāddhabhug yaśca kṛmīnbhakṣetpipīlikāḥ //
12.d:
पुनर्भूपतयो ये च कन्याविध्वंसकाश्च ये ।
तद्गर्भश्राद्धभुग् यश्च कृमीन्भक्षेत्पिपीलिकाः ॥
12.m:
The husbands of remarried women, and those who ruin maidens,
and he who eats the funeral feast of their fetus, must eat worms and ants.

12.s:
cāṇḍālādantyajādvāpi pratigṛhṇāti dakṣiṇām /
yājako yajamānaśca so 'smāntaḥ sthūlakīṭakaḥ //
12.d:
चाण्डालादन्त्यजाद्वापि प्रतिगृह्णाति दक्षिणाम् ।
याजको यजमानश्च सो ऽस्मान्तः स्थूलकीटकः ॥
12.m:
He who accepts a sacrificial fee from an outcaste or a low-born man,
both the priest and the patron, become fat worms inside a stone.

12.s:
pṛṣṭhamāṃsāśino mūḍhāstathaivotkocajīvinaḥ /
kṣipyante vṛkabhakṣe te narake rajanīcara //
12.d:
पृष्ठमांसाशिनो मूढास्तथैवोत्कोचजीविनः ।
क्षिप्यन्ते वृकभक्षे ते नरके रजनीचर ॥
12.m:
Fools who eat back-flesh (slanderers), and likewise those who live by bribes,
are cast into the Vṛkabhakṣa hell, O night-wanderer.

12.s:
svarṇasteyī ca brahmaghnaḥ surāpo gurulalpagaḥ /
tathā gobhūmiharttaro gostrībālahanāśca ye //
12.d:
स्वर्णस्तेयी च ब्रह्मघ्नः सुरापो गुरुलल्पगः ।
तथा गोभूमिहर्त्तरो गोस्त्रीबालहनाश्च ये ॥
12.m:
The thief of gold, the killer of a Brahmin, the drinker of liquor, the defiler of a guru's bed,
and likewise stealers of cows and land, and killers of cows, women, and children,

12.s:
eta narā dvijā ye ca goṣu vikrayiṇastathā /
somavikrayiṇo ye ca vedavikrayiṇastathā //
12.d:
एत नरा द्विजा ये च गोषु विक्रयिणस्तथा ।
सोमविक्रयिणो ये च वेदविक्रयिणस्तथा ॥
12.m:
these men; and those twice-born who are sellers of cattle,
those who are sellers of soma, and those who are sellers of the Vedas,

12.s:
kūṭasabhyāstvaśaucāśca nityanaimittanāśakāḥ /
kūṭasākṣyapradā ye ca te mahāraurave sthitāḥ //
12.d:
कूटसभ्यास्त्वशौचाश्च नित्यनैमित्तनाशकाः ।
कूटसाक्ष्यप्रदा ये च ते महारौरवे स्थिताः ॥
12.m:
deceitful assessors, the impure, destroyers of regular and occasional rites,
and those who give false testimony, abide in Mahāraurava.

12.s:
daśavarṣa sahasrāṇi tāvat tāmisrake sthitāḥ /
tāvaccaivāndhatāmisre asipatravane tataḥ //
12.d:
दशवर्ष सहस्राणि तावत् तामिस्रके स्थिताः ।
तावच्चैवान्धतामिस्रे असिपत्रवने ततः ॥
12.m:
For ten thousand years they stay in Tāmisra,
and for as long in Andhatāmisra, then in Asipatravana;

12.s:
tāvaccaiva ghaṭīyantre taptakumbhe tataḥ param /
prapāto bhavate teṣāṃ yairidaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam //
12.d:
तावच्चैव घटीयन्त्रे तप्तकुम्भे ततः परम् ।
प्रपातो भवते तेषां यैरिदं दुष्कृतं कृतम् ॥
12.m:
and for as long in Ghaṭīyantra, [and] after that in Taptakumbha
occurs the fall of those by whom this evil was committed.

12.s:
ye tvete narakā raudrā rauravādyāstavoditāḥ /
te sarve kramaśaḥ proktāḥ kṛtaghne lokanindite //
12.d:
ये त्वेते नरका रौद्रा रौरवाद्यास्तवोदिताः ।
ते सर्वे क्रमशः प्रोक्ताः कृतघ्ने लोकनिन्दिते ॥
12.m:
These terrible hells, beginning with Raurava, that have been described to you,
they have all been proclaimed in succession for the ungrateful person, who is blamed by the world.

12.s:
yathā surāṇāṃ pravaro janārdano yathā girīṇāmapi śaiśirādriḥ /
yathāyudhānāṃ pravaraṃ sudarśanaṃ yathā khagānāṃ vinatātanūjaḥ /
mahoragāṇāṃ pravaro 'pyananto yathā ca bhūteṣu mahī pradhānā //
12.d:
यथा सुराणां प्रवरो जनार्दनो यथा गिरीणामपि शैशिराद्रिः ।
यथायुधानां प्रवरं सुदर्शनं यथा खगानां विनतातनूजः ।
महोरगाणां प्रवरो ऽप्यनन्तो यथा च भूतेषु मही प्रधाना ॥
12.m:
Just as Janārdana is foremost among the gods, just as the snowy mountain [Himavat] is among mountains,
just as Sudarśana is foremost among weapons, just as the son of Vinatā [Garuḍa] is among birds,
just as Ananta is foremost among great serpents, and just as the earth is principal among beings,

12.s:
nadīṣu gaṅgā jalajeṣu padmaṃ surārimukhyeṣu harāṅghribhaktaḥ /
kṣetreṣu yadvatkurujaṅgalaṃ varaṃ tīrtheṣu yadvat pravaraṃ pṛthūdakam //
12.d:
नदीषु गङ्गा जलजेषु पद्मं सुरारिमुख्येषु हराङ्घ्रिभक्तः ।
क्षेत्रेषु यद्वत्कुरुजङ्गलं वरं तीर्थेषु यद्वत् प्रवरं पृथूदकम् ॥
12.m:
just as the Gaṅgā is [foremost] among rivers, the lotus among water-born flowers, the devotee of Hara's feet among the leaders of the gods' enemies,
just as Kurujaṅgala is best among holy realms, just as Pṛthūdaka is foremost among tīrthas,

12.s:
sarassu caivottaramānasaṃ yathā vaneṣu puṇyeṣu hi nandanaṃ yathā /
lokeṣu yadvatsadanaṃ viriñceḥ satyaṃ yathā dharmavidhikriyāsu //
12.d:
सरस्सु चैवोत्तरमानसं यथा वनेषु पुण्येषु हि नन्दनं यथा ।
लोकेषु यद्वत्सदनं विरिञ्चेः सत्यं यथा धर्मविधिक्रियासु ॥
12.m:
just as Uttaramānasa is [foremost] among lakes, just as Nandana is among sacred groves,
just as the abode of Viriñci [Brahmā] is among the worlds, just as truth is among the rites of dharma's injunctions,

12.s:
yathāśvamedhaḥ pravaraḥ kratūnāṃ putro yathā sparśavatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ /
tapodhanānāmapi sumbhayoniḥ śrutirvarā yadvadihāgameṣu //
12.d:
यथाश्वमेधः प्रवरः क्रतूनां पुत्रो यथा स्पर्शवतां वरिष्ठः ।
तपोधनानामपि सुम्भयोनिः श्रुतिर्वरा यद्वदिहागमेषु ॥
12.m:
just as the horse sacrifice is foremost among sacrifices, just as a son is best among things possessed of touch,
just as the jar-born [Agastya] is [foremost] among ascetics, just as the Veda is best among scriptures here,

12.s:
mukhyaḥ purāṇeṣu yathaiva mātsyaḥ svāyaṃbhuvoktistvapi saṃhitāsu /
manuḥ smṛtīnāṃ pravaro yathaiva tithīṣu darśā viṣuveṣu dānam //
12.d:
मुख्यः पुराणेषु यथैव मात्स्यः स्वायंभुवोक्तिस्त्वपि संहितासु ।
मनुः स्मृतीनां प्रवरो यथैव तिथीषु दर्शा विषुवेषु दानम् ॥
12.m:
just as the Matsya is principal among Purāṇas, and the text of Svayambhū among the collections,
just as Manu is foremost among the smṛtis, the new moon among lunar days, and gift-giving at the equinoxes,

12.s:
tejasvināṃ yadvadihārka ukto ṛkṣeṣu candro jaladhirhvadeṣu /
bhavān yathā rākṣasasattameṣu pāśeṣu nāgastimiteṣu bandhaḥ //
12.d:
तेजस्विनां यद्वदिहार्क उक्तो ऋक्षेषु चन्द्रो जलधिर्ह्वदेषु ।
भवान् यथा राक्षससत्तमेषु पाशेषु नागस्तिमितेषु बन्धः ॥
12.m:
just as the sun is said to be [foremost] among radiant bodies here, the moon among constellations, the ocean among reservoirs of water,
just as you are among the best of Rākṣasas, the serpent-noose among fetters, and arrest among fixed states,

12.s:
dhānyeṣu śalirdvipadeṣu vipraḥ catuṣpade gauḥ śvapadāṃ mṛgendraḥ /
puṣpeṣu jātī nagareṣu kāñcī nārīṣu rambhā śramīṇāṃ gṛhasthaḥ //
12.d:
धान्येषु शलिर्द्विपदेषु विप्रः चतुष्पदे गौः श्वपदां मृगेन्द्रः ।
पुष्पेषु जाती नगरेषु काञ्ची नारीषु रम्भा श्रमीणां गृहस्थः ॥
12.m:
just as winter rice is [foremost] among grains, the Brahmin among two-legged beings, the cow among quadrupeds, the lion among carnivores,
just as the jasmine is among flowers, Kāñcī among cities, Rambhā among women, and the householder among those in the stages of life,

12.s:
kuśasthalī śreṣṭhatamā pureṣu deśeṣu sarveṣu ca madhyadeśaḥ /
phaleṣu cūto mukuleṣvaśokaḥ sarvauṣadhīnāṃ pravarā ca pathyā //
12.d:
कुशस्थली श्रेष्ठतमा पुरेषु देशेषु सर्वेषु च मध्यदेशः ।
फलेषु चूतो मुकुलेष्वशोकः सर्वौषधीनां प्रवरा च पथ्या ॥
12.m:
just as Kuśasthalī is best among cities, and Madhyadeśa among all regions,
just as the mango is among fruits, the aśoka among blossoms, and the yellow myrobalan foremost among all medicinal plants,

12.s:
mūleṣu kandaḥ pravaro yathokto vyādhiṣvajīrṇaṃ kṣaṇadācarendra /
śveteṣu dugdhaṃ pravaraṃ yathaiva kārpāsikaṃ prāvaraṇeṣu yadvat //
12.d:
मूलेषु कन्दः प्रवरो यथोक्तो व्याधिष्वजीर्णं क्षणदाचरेन्द्र ।
श्वेतेषु दुग्धं प्रवरं यथैव कार्पासिकं प्रावरणेषु यद्वत् ॥
12.m:
just as the edible bulb is proclaimed foremost among roots, indigestion among diseases, O king of night-wanderers,
just as milk is foremost among white things, and just as cotton is among garments,

12.s:
kalāsu mukhyā gaṇitajñatā ca vijñānamukhyeṣu yathendrajālam /
śākeṣu mukhyā tvapi kākamācī raseṣu mukhyaṃ lavaṇaṃ yathaiva //
12.d:
कलासु मुख्या गणितज्ञता च विज्ञानमुख्येषु यथेन्द्रजालम् ।
शाकेषु मुख्या त्वपि काकमाची रसेषु मुख्यं लवणं यथैव ॥
12.m:
just as skill in mathematics is principal among the arts, just as sorcery is among sciences,
just as the black nightshade is principal among vegetables, and just as salt is principal among tastes,

12.s:
tuṅḍgeṣu tālo nalinīṣu pampā vanaukaseṣveva ca ṛkṣarājaḥ /
mahīruheṣveva yathā vaṭaśca yathā haro jñānavatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ //
12.d:
तुङ्ड्गेषु तालो नलिनीषु पम्पा वनौकसेष्वेव च ऋक्षराजः ।
महीरुहेष्वेव यथा वटश्च यथा हरो ज्ञानवतां वरिष्ठः ॥
12.m:
just as the palmyra palm is [foremost] among lofty things, Pampā among lotus-pools, the king of bears among forest-dwellers,
just as the banyan tree is among trees, and just as Hara is best among the wise,

12.s:
yathā satīnāṃ himavatsutā hi yathārjunīnāṃ kapilā variṣṭhā /
yathā vṛṣāṇāmapi nīlavarṇo yathaiva sarveṣvapi duḥsaheṣu /
durgeṣu raudreṣu niśācareśa nṛpātanaṃ vaitaraṇī pradhānā //
12.d:
यथा सतीनां हिमवत्सुता हि यथार्जुनीनां कपिला वरिष्ठा ।
यथा वृषाणामपि नीलवर्णो यथैव सर्वेष्वपि दुःसहेषु ।
दुर्गेषु रौद्रेषु निशाचरेश नृपातनं वैतरणी प्रधाना ॥
12.m:
just as the daughter of Himavat [Pārvatī] is indeed [foremost] among chaste wives, just as the brown cow is best among white ones,
just as the dark-colored one is among bulls, and just as among all unbearable,
terrible fortresses, O lord of night-wanderers, the Vaitaraṇī that casts down men is primary,

12.s:
pāpīyasāṃ tadvadiha kṛghnāḥ sarveṣu pāpeṣu vanaśācarendra /
brahmaghnagoghnādiṣu niṣkṛtirhi vidyetata naivāsya tu duṣṭacāriṇaḥ /
na niṣkṛtiścāsti kṛtaghnavṛtteḥ suhṛtkṛtaṃ nāśayato 'bdakoṭibhiḥ //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
12.d:
पापीयसां तद्वदिह कृघ्नाः सर्वेषु पापेषु वनशाचरेन्द्र ।
ब्रह्मघ्नगोघ्नादिषु निष्कृतिर्हि विद्येतत नैवास्य तु दुष्टचारिणः ।
न निष्कृतिश्चास्ति कृतघ्नवृत्तेः सुहृत्कृतं नाशयतो ऽब्दकोटिभिः ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे द्वादशो ऽध्यायः
12.m:
so the ungrateful are the most sinful among all sinners, O king of forest-wanderers!
For an expiation exists for killers of Brahmins, killers of cows, and the like, but none exists for this wrongdoer;
and there is no expiation even in ten million aeons for the conduct of an ungrateful person who destroys what a friend has done.

Thus ends the twelfth chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

13.s:
sukeśiruvāca /
bhavadbhiruditā ghorā puṣkaradvīpasaṃsthitiḥ /
jambūdvīpasya saṃsthānaṃ kathayantu maharṣayaḥ //
13.d:
सुकेशिरुवाच ।
भवद्भिरुदिता घोरा पुष्करद्वीपसंस्थितिः ।
जम्बूद्वीपस्य संस्थानं कथयन्तु महर्षयः ॥
13.m:
Sukeśin said:
"You have described the dread condition of Puṣkaradvīpa.
Let the great sages tell of the constitution of Jambūdvīpa!"

13.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ /
jambūdvīpasya saṃsthānaṃ kathyamānaṃ nisāmaya /
navabhedaṃ suvistīrṇaṃ svargasokṣaphalapradam //
13.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
जम्बूद्वीपस्य संस्थानं कथ्यमानं निसामय ।
नवभेदं सुविस्तीर्णं स्वर्गसोक्षफलप्रदम् ॥
13.m:
The sages said:
"Listen to the constitution of Jambūdvīpa as it is being told,
having nine divisions, very extensive, granting the fruits of heaven and liberation:

13.s:
madhye tvilāvṛto varṣo bhadraśvaḥ pūrvato 'dbhutaḥ /
pūrva uttarataścāpi hiraṇyo rākṣaseśvara //
13.d:
मध्ये त्विलावृतो वर्षो भद्रश्वः पूर्वतो ऽद्भुतः ।
पूर्व उत्तरतश्चापि हिरण्यो राक्षसेश्वर ॥
13.m:
In the middle is the realm of Ilāvṛta; wondrous Bhadrāśva is in the east;
in the north-east is Hiraṇya, O lord of Rākṣasas;

13.s:
pūrvadakṣiṇataścāpi kiṃnaro varṣa ucyate /
bhārato dakṣiṇe prokto harirdakṣiṇapaśacime //
13.d:
पूर्वदक्षिणतश्चापि किंनरो वर्ष उच्यते ।
भारतो दक्षिणे प्रोक्तो हरिर्दक्षिणपशचिमे ॥
13.m:
in the south-east is the realm called Kiṃnara;
Bhārata is declared in the south, and Hari in the south-west;

13.s:
paścime kekumālaśca ramyakaḥ paścimottare /
uttare ca kururvarṣaḥ kalpavṛkṣasamāvṛtaḥ //
13.d:
पश्चिमे केकुमालश्च रम्यकः पश्चिमोत्तरे ।
उत्तरे च कुरुर्वर्षः कल्पवृक्षसमावृतः ॥
13.m:
in the west is Ketumāla, and Ramyaka in the north-west;
and in the north is the realm of Kuru, filled with wish-fulfilling trees.

13.s:
puṇyā ramyā navaivaite varṣāḥ śālakaṭaṅkaṭa /
ilāvṛtādyā ye cāṣṭau varṣaṃ muktvaiva bhāratam //
13.d:
पुण्या रम्या नवैवैते वर्षाः शालकटङ्कट ।
इलावृताद्या ये चाष्टौ वर्षं मुक्त्वैव भारतम् ॥
13.m:
These nine realms alone are sacred and delightful, O Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa!
And as for the eight beginning with Ilāvṛta, leaving aside the realm of Bhārata,

13.s:
na teṣvasti yugāvasthā jarāmṛtyubhayaṃ na ca /
teṣāṃ svābhāvikī siddhiḥ sukhaprāyā hyatnataḥ /
viparyayo na teṣvasti nottamādhamamadhyamāḥ //
13.d:
न तेष्वस्ति युगावस्था जरामृत्युभयं न च ।
तेषां स्वाभाविकी सिद्धिः सुखप्राया ह्यत्नतः ।
विपर्ययो न तेष्वस्ति नोत्तमाधममध्यमाः ॥

13.s:
yadetad bhārataṃ varṣaṃ navadvīpaṃ nisācara /
sāgarāntaritāḥ sarve agamyāśca parasparam //
13.d:
यदेतद् भारतं वर्षं नवद्वीपं निसाचर ।
सागरान्तरिताः सर्वे अगम्याश्च परस्परम् ॥
13.m:
This realm of Bhārata, O night-wanderer, has nine regions;
they are all separated by the ocean, and inaccessible to one another:

13.s:
indrīpaḥ kaserumāṃstāmravarṇo gabhastimān /
nāgadvīpaḥ kaṭāhaśca siṃhalo vāruṇastathā //
13.d:
इन्द्रीपः कसेरुमांस्ताम्रवर्णो गभस्तिमान् ।
नागद्वीपः कटाहश्च सिंहलो वारुणस्तथा ॥
13.m:
Indradvīpa, Kaserumat, Tāmravarṇa, Gabhastimat,
Nāgadvīpa, Kaṭāha, Siṃhala, and Vāruṇa.

13.s:
ayaṃ tu navamasteṣāṃ dvīpaḥ sāgarasaṃvṛtaḥ /
kumārākhyaḥ parikhyāto dvīpo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇottaraḥ //
13.d:
अयं तु नवमस्तेषां द्वीपः सागरसंवृतः ।
कुमाराख्यः परिख्यातो द्वीपो ऽयं दक्षिणोत्तरः ॥
13.m:
And this ninth region of theirs is surrounded by the ocean;
known by the name of Kumāra, this region extends from south to north,

13.s:
pūrve kirātā yasyānte paścime yavanāḥ sthitāḥ /
āndhrā dakṣimate vīra turuṣkāstvapi cottare //
13.d:
पूर्वे किराता यस्यान्ते पश्चिमे यवनाः स्थिताः ।
आन्ध्रा दक्षिमते वीर तुरुष्कास्त्वपि चोत्तरे ॥
13.m:
at whose eastern end dwell the Kirātas, and in the west the Yavanas;
the Āndhras are in the south, O hero, and the Turuṣkas in the north.

13.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ sūdrāścāntaravāsinaḥ /
ijyāyuddhavaṇijyādyaiḥ karmabhiḥ kṛtapāvanāḥ //
teṣāṃ saṃvyavahāraśca ebhiḥ karmabhiriṣyate /
svargāpavargaprāptiśca puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ tathaiva ca / /
13.d:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः सूद्राश्चान्तरवासिनः ।
इज्यायुद्धवणिज्याद्यैः कर्मभिः कृतपावनाः ॥
तेषां संव्यवहारश्च एभिः कर्मभिरिष्यते ।
स्वर्गापवर्गप्राप्तिश्च पुण्यं पापं तथैव च । ।
13.m:
Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras dwell in the interior,
purified through their actions such as sacrifice, warfare, trade, and the like.

their lot is determined by these actions,
as are the attainment of heaven and liberation, and merit and sin likewise.

13.s:
13.13 mahendro malayaḥ sahyaḥ śuktimān ṛkṣaparvataḥ /
vindhyaśca pāriyātraśca saptātra kulaparvatāḥ //
13.d:
13.13 महेन्द्रो मलयः सह्यः शुक्तिमान् ऋक्षपर्वतः ।
विन्ध्यश्च पारियात्रश्च सप्तात्र कुलपर्वताः ॥
13.m:
Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śuktimān, Ṛkṣaparvata,
Vindhya, and Pāriyātra: these are the seven mountain ranges here.

13.s:
tathānye śatasāhasrā bhūdharā madhyavāsināḥ /
vistārocchrāyiṇo ramyā vipulāḥ śubhasānavaḥ //
13.d:
तथान्ये शतसाहस्रा भूधरा मध्यवासिनाः ।
विस्तारोच्छ्रायिणो रम्या विपुलाः शुभसानवः ॥
13.m:
Likewise, there are hundreds of thousands of other mountains dwelling in the interior,
extensive and lofty, lovely, broad, with auspicious peaks:

13.s:
kolāhalaḥ savaibhrājo mandaro durdarācalaḥ /
vātandhamo vaidyutaśca mainākaḥ sarasastathā //
13.d:
कोलाहलः सवैभ्राजो मन्दरो दुर्दराचलः ।
वातन्धमो वैद्युतश्च मैनाकः सरसस्तथा ॥
13.m:
Kolāhala, Vaibhrāja, Mandara, mount Dardura,
Vātandhama, Vaidyuta, Maināka, and Sarasa,

13.s:
tuṅgaprastho nāgagiristathā govardhanācalaḥ /
ujjāyanaḥ puṣpagirirarbudo raivatastathā //
13.d:
तुङ्गप्रस्थो नागगिरिस्तथा गोवर्धनाचलः ।
उज्जायनः पुष्पगिरिरर्बुदो रैवतस्तथा ॥
13.m:
Tuṅgaprastha, the Nāga mountain, mount Govardhana,
Ujjāyana, Puṣpagiri, Arbuda, and Raivata,

13.s:
ṛṣyamūkaḥ sagomantaścitrakūṭaḥ kṛtasmaraḥ /
śrīparvataḥ koṅgaṇaśca śataśa'nye 'pi parvatāḥ //
13.d:
ऋष्यमूकः सगोमन्तश्चित्रकूटः कृतस्मरः ।
श्रीपर्वतः कोङ्गणश्च शतशऽन्ये ऽपि पर्वताः ॥
13.m:
Ṛṣyamūka, Gomanta, Citrakūṭa, Kṛtasmara,
Śrīparvata, and Koṅgaṇa, and hundreds of other mountains.

13.s:
tairvimiśrā janapadā mlecchā āryāśca bhāgaśaḥ /
taiḥ pīyante saricchreṣṭhā yāstāḥ samyaṅ niśāmayaḥ //
13.d:
तैर्विमिश्रा जनपदा म्लेच्छा आर्याश्च भागशः ।
तैः पीयन्ते सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा यास्ताः सम्यङ् निशामयः ॥
13.m:
Mixed with them are realms of Mlecchas and Āryas, in their respective parts.
By them the best of rivers are drunk; hear of them accurately:

13.s:
sarasvatī pañcarūpā kālindī sahiraṇvatī /
śatadruścandrikā nīlā vitastairāvatī kuhūḥ //
13.d:
सरस्वती पञ्चरूपा कालिन्दी सहिरण्वती ।
शतद्रुश्चन्द्रिका नीला वितस्तैरावती कुहूः ॥
13.m:
Sarasvatī, Pañcarūpā, Kālindī, Hiraṇvatī,
Śatadru, Candrikā, Nīlā, Vitastā, Airāvatī, Kuhū,

13.s:
madhurā hārarāvī ca uśīrā dhātukī rasā /
gomatī dhūtapāpā ca bāhudā sadṛṣadvatī //
13.d:
मधुरा हाररावी च उशीरा धातुकी रसा ।
गोमती धूतपापा च बाहुदा सदृषद्वती ॥
13.m:
Madhurā, Hārarāvī, Uśīrā, Dhātukī, Rasā,
Gomatī, Dhūtapāpā, Bāhudā, and Dṛṣadvatī,

13.s:
niścirā gaṇḍakī citrā kauśikī ca vadhūsarā /
sarūśca salauhityā himavatpādaniḥsṛtāḥ //
13.d:
निश्चिरा गण्डकी चित्रा कौशिकी च वधूसरा ।
सरूश्च सलौहित्या हिमवत्पादनिःसृताः ॥
13.m:
Niścirā, Gaṇḍakī, Citrā, Kauśikī, Vadhūsarā,
Sarayū, and Lauhityā: these flow from the foot of Himavat.

13.s:
vedasmṛtirvedasinī vṛtraghnī sindhureva ca /
parṇāśā nandinī caiva pāvanī ca mahī tathā //
13.d:
वेदस्मृतिर्वेदसिनी वृत्रघ्नी सिन्धुरेव च ।
पर्णाशा नन्दिनी चैव पावनी च मही तथा ॥
13.m:
Vedasmṛti, Vedasinī, Vṛtraghnī, and the Sindhu,
Parṇāśā, Nandinī, Pāvanī, and Mahī,

13.s:
pārā carmaṇvatī lūpī vidiśā veṇumatyapi /
siprā hyavantī ca tathā pāriyātrāśrayāḥ smṛtāḥ //
13.d:
पारा चर्मण्वती लूपी विदिशा वेणुमत्यपि ।
सिप्रा ह्यवन्ती च तथा पारियात्राश्रयाः स्मृताः ॥
13.m:
Pārā, Carmaṇvatī, Lūpī, Vidiśā, Veṇumatī,
Siprā, and Avantī are recorded as originating from Pāriyātra.

13.s:
śoṇo mahānadaścaiva narmadā surasā kṛpā /
mandākinī daśārṇā ca citrakūṭāpavāhikā //
13.d:
शोणो महानदश्चैव नर्मदा सुरसा कृपा ।
मन्दाकिनी दशार्णा च चित्रकूटापवाहिका ॥
13.m:
The Śoṇa, the great river, Narmadā, Surasā, Kṛpā,
Mandākinī, Daśārṇā, and the stream of Citrakūṭā,

13.s:
citrotpalā vai tamasā karamodā piśācikā /
tathānyā pippalaśroṇī vipāśā vañjulāvatī //
13.d:
चित्रोत्पला वै तमसा करमोदा पिशाचिका ।
तथान्या पिप्पलश्रोणी विपाशा वञ्जुलावती ॥
13.m:
Citrotpalā, Tamasā, Karamodā, Piśācikā,
and another, Pippalaśroṇī, Vipāśā, and Vañjulāvatī,

13.s:
satsantajā śuktimatī mañjiṣṭhā kṛttisā vasuḥ /
ṛkṣapādaprasūtā ca tathānyā balavāhinī //
13.d:
सत्सन्तजा शुक्तिमती मञ्जिष्ठा कृत्तिसा वसुः ।
ऋक्षपादप्रसूता च तथान्या बलवाहिनी ॥
13.m: Satsantajā, Śuktimatī, Mañjiṣṭhā, Kṛttisā, Vasu, / and Balavāhinī are others born from the foot of Ṛkṣa.

13.s:
śivā payoṣṇī nirvindhyā tāpī saniṣadhāvatī /
veṇa vaitaraṇī caiva sinīvāhuḥ kumudvatī //
13.d:
शिवा पयोष्णी निर्विन्ध्या तापी सनिषधावती ।
वेण वैतरणी चैव सिनीवाहुः कुमुद्वती ॥
13.m: Śivā, Payoṣṇī, Nirvindhyā, Tāpī with Niṣadhāvatī, / Veṇā, Vaitaraṇī, Sinīvāhu, Kumudvatī,

13.s:
toyā caiva mahāgairī durgandhā vāśilāḥ tathā /
vindhyapādaprasūtāśca nadyaḥ puṇyajalāḥ śubhāḥ //
13.d:
तोया चैव महागैरी दुर्गन्धा वाशिलाः तथा ।
विन्ध्यपादप्रसूताश्च नद्यः पुण्यजलाः शुभाः ॥
13.m: Toyā, Mahāgairī, Durgandhā, and Vāśilā: / these are the rivers born from the foot of the Vindhya, auspicious, with holy waters.

13.s:
godāvarī bhīmarathī kṛṣṇā veṇā sarasvatī /
tuṅgabhadrā suprayogā vāhyā kāverireva ca //
13.d:
गोदावरी भीमरथी कृष्णा वेणा सरस्वती ।
तुङ्गभद्रा सुप्रयोगा वाह्या कावेरिरेव च ॥
13.m: Godāvarī, Bhīmarathī, Kṛṣṇā, Veṇā, Sarasvatī, / Tuṅgabhadrā, Suprayogā, Vāhyā, and Kāverī,

13.s:
dugdhodā nalinī reva vārisenā kalasvanā /
etāstvapi mahānadyaḥ sahyapādavinirgatāḥ //
13.d:
दुग्धोदा नलिनी रेव वारिसेना कलस्वना ।
एतास्त्वपि महानद्यः सह्यपादविनिर्गताः ॥
13.m: Dugdhodā, Nalinī, Revā, Vārisenā, Kalasvanā— / these great rivers, moreover, issue from the foot of the Sahya.

13.s:
kṛtamālā tāmrarṇī vaḍhjulā cotpalāvatī /
sinī caiva sudāmā ca śuktimatprabhavāstvimāḥ //
13.d:
कृतमाला ताम्रर्णी वढ्जुला चोत्पलावती ।
सिनी चैव सुदामा च शुक्तिमत्प्रभवास्त्विमाः ॥
13.m: Kṛtamālā, Tāmraparṇī, Vañjulā, Utpalāvatī, / Sinī, and Sudāmā: these originate from Śuktimat.

13.s:
sarvāḥ puṇyāḥ sarasvatyaḥ pāpapraśamanāstathā /
jagato mātaraḥ sarvāḥ sarvāḥ sāgarayoṣitaḥ //
13.d:
सर्वाः पुण्याः सरस्वत्यः पापप्रशमनास्तथा ।
जगतो मातरः सर्वाः सर्वाः सागरयोषितः ॥
13.m: All are holy Sarasvatīs, dispelling sin; / all are mothers of the world, all wives of the ocean.

13.s:
anyāḥ sahasraśaścātra kṣudranadyo hi rākṣasa /
sadākālavahāścānyāḥ pravṛṭkālavahāstathā /
udaṅmadhyodbhavā deśāḥ pibanti svecchayā śubhāḥ //
13.d:
अन्याः सहस्रशश्चात्र क्षुद्रनद्यो हि राक्षस ।
सदाकालवहाश्चान्याः प्रवृट्कालवहास्तथा ।
उदङ्मध्योद्भवा देशाः पिबन्ति स्वेच्छया शुभाः ॥
13.m: And there are thousands of other minor rivers here, O Rākṣasa, / some flowing at all times, and others flowing during the rains; / the auspicious lands born in the north and middle drink [them] at will.

13.s: matsyāḥ kuśaṭṭāḥ kuṇikuṇḍalāśca pāñjālakāśyāḥ saha kosalābhiḥ //
13.d: मत्स्याः कुशट्टाः कुणिकुण्डलाश्च पाञ्जालकाश्याः सह कोसलाभिः ॥
13.m: The Matsyas, Kuśaṭṭas, Kuṇikuṇḍalas, Pāñcālas, and Kāśis along with the Kosalas,

13.s:
vṛkāḥ śabarakauvīrāḥ sabhūliṅgā janāstvime /
śakāścaiva samaśakā madhyadeśya janāstvime //
13.d:
वृकाः शबरकौवीराः सभूलिङ्गा जनास्त्विमे ।
शकाश्चैव समशका मध्यदेश्य जनास्त्विमे ॥
13.m: Vṛkas, Śabaras, Kauvīras, these people with the Bhūliṅgas, / the Śakas and Samaśakas—these are people of the Middle Country.

13.s:
vāhlīkā vāṭadhānāśca ābhīrāḥ kālatoyakāḥ /
aparāntāstathā śūdrāḥ pahlāvāśca sakheṭakāḥ //
13.d:
वाह्लीका वाटधानाश्च आभीराः कालतोयकाः ।
अपरान्तास्तथा शूद्राः पह्लावाश्च सखेटकाः ॥
13.m: The Vāhlīkas, Vāṭadhānas, Ābhīras, Kālatoyakas, / the Aparāntas, Śūdras, and Pahlavas with the Kheṭakas,

13.s:
gāndhārā yavanāścaiva sindhusauvīramadrakāḥ /
śātadravā lalitthāśca pārāvatasamūṣakāḥ //
13.d:
गान्धारा यवनाश्चैव सिन्धुसौवीरमद्रकाः ।
शातद्रवा ललित्थाश्च पारावतसमूषकाः ॥
13.m: the Gāndhāras, Yavanas, Sindhus, Sauvīras, Madrakas, / the Śātadravas, Lalitthas, and Pārāvatasamūṣakas,

13.s:
māṭharodakadhārāścaja kaikaiyā daśamāstathā /
śratriyāḥ prativaiśyāśca vaiśyaśūdrakulāni ca //
13.d:
माठरोदकधाराश्चज कैकैया दशमास्तथा ।
श्रत्रियाः प्रतिवैश्याश्च वैश्यशूद्रकुलानि च ॥
13.m: the Māṭharas, Udakadhāras, Kaikeyas, and Daśamas, / the Kṣatriyas, Prativaiśyas, and families of Vaiśyas and Śūdras,

13.s:
kāmbojā daradāścaiva barbarā hyaṅgalaukikāḥ /
cīnāścaiva tuṣārāśca bahudhā bāhyatodarāḥ //
13.d:
काम्बोजा दरदाश्चैव बर्बरा ह्यङ्गलौकिकाः ।
चीनाश्चैव तुषाराश्च बहुधा बाह्यतोदराः ॥
13.m: the Kāmbojas, Daradas, Barbaras, and Aṅgalaukikas, / the Cīnas, Tuṣāras, and many external Toḍaras,

13.s:
ātreyāḥ sabharadvājāḥ prasthalāśca daśerakāḥ /
lampakāstāvakārāmāḥ śūlikāstaṅgaṇaiḥ sahā //
13.d:
आत्रेयाः सभरद्वाजाः प्रस्थलाश्च दशेरकाः ।
लम्पकास्तावकारामाः शूलिकास्तङ्गणैः सहा ॥
13.m: the Ātreyas with the Bharadvājas, the Prasthalas, Daśerakas, / the Lampākas, Tāvakārāmas, and Śūlikas along with the Taṅgaṇas,

13.s:
aurasāścālimadrāśca kirātānāṃ ca jātayaḥ /
tāmasāḥ kramamāsāśca supārśvāḥ puṇḍrakāstathā //
13.d:
औरसाश्चालिमद्राश्च किरातानां च जातयः ।
तामसाः क्रममासाश्च सुपार्श्वाः पुण्ड्रकास्तथा ॥
13.m: the Aurasas, Alimadras, and the tribes of Kirātas, / the Tāmasas, Kramamāsas, Supārśvas, and Puṇḍrakas,

13.s:
kulūtāḥ kuhukā ūrṇāstūṇīpādāḥ sukukkuṭāḥ /
māṇḍavyā mālavīyāśca uttarāpathavāsinaḥ //
13.d:
कुलूताः कुहुका ऊर्णास्तूणीपादाः सुकुक्कुटाः ।
माण्डव्या मालवीयाश्च उत्तरापथवासिनः ॥
13.m: the Kulūtas, Kuhukas, Ūrṇas, Tūṇīpādas, Sukukkuṭas, / the Māṇḍavyas, and Mālavīyas: these are dwellers of the Northern Path.

13.s:
aṅgā vaṅgā mudgaravāstvantargiribahirgirāḥ /
tathā pravaṅgā vāṅgeyā māṃsādā baladantikāḥ //
13.d:
अङ्गा वङ्गा मुद्गरवास्त्वन्तर्गिरिबहिर्गिराः ।
तथा प्रवङ्गा वाङ्गेया मांसादा बलदन्तिकाः ॥
13.m: The Aṅgas, Vaṅgas, Mudgaravas, Antargiris, Bahirgiris, / as well as the Pravaṅgas, Vāṅgeyas, the meat-eating Baladantikas,

13.s:
brahmottarā prāvijayā bhārgavāḥ keśavarrāḥ /
pragjyotiṣāśca śūdraśca videhāstāmraliptakāḥ //
13.d:
ब्रह्मोत्तरा प्राविजया भार्गवाः केशवर्राः ।
प्रग्ज्योतिषाश्च शूद्रश्च विदेहास्ताम्रलिप्तकाः ॥
13.m: the Brahmottaras, Prāvijayas, Bhārgavas, Keśavarras, / the Prāgjyotiṣas, Śūdras, Videhas, Tāmraliptakas,

13.s:
mālā magadhagonandāḥ prācya najapadāstvime /
puṇḍrāśca keralāścaiva cauḍāḥ kulyāśca rākṣasa //
13.d:
माला मगधगोनन्दाः प्राच्य नजपदास्त्विमे ।
पुण्ड्राश्च केरलाश्चैव चौडाः कुल्याश्च राक्षस ॥
13.m: the Mālas, Magadhas, and Gonandas: these are the eastern realms; / and the Puṇḍras, Keralas, Cauḍas, and Kulyas, O Rākṣasa,

13.s:
jātuṣā mūṣikādāśca kumārādā mahāśakāḥ /
mahārāṣṭrā māhiṣikāḥ kāliṅgāścaiva sarvaśaḥ //
13.d:
जातुषा मूषिकादाश्च कुमारादा महाशकाः ।
महाराष्ट्रा माहिषिकाः कालिङ्गाश्चैव सर्वशः ॥
13.m: the Jātuṣas, Mūṣikādas, Kumārādas, Mahāśakas, / the Mahārāṣṭras, Māhiṣikas, and Kāliṅgas on every side,

13.s:
ābhīrāḥ saha naiṣīkā āraṇyāḥ śabarāśca ye /
valindhyā vindhyamauleyā vaidarbhā daṇḍakaiḥ saha //
13.d:
आभीराः सह नैषीका आरण्याः शबराश्च ये ।
वलिन्ध्या विन्ध्यमौलेया वैदर्भा दण्डकैः सह ॥
13.m: the Ābhīras along with the Naiṣīkas, the forest-dwelling Śabaras, / the Valindhyas, Vindhyamauleyas, Vaidarbhas with the Daṇḍakas,

13.s:
paurikaḥ sauśikāścaiva aśmakā bhogavarddhanāḥ /
vaiṣikāḥ kundalā andhrā udbhidā nalakārakāḥ /
dākṣiṇātyā janapadāstvime śālakaṭaṅkaṭaḥ //
13.d:
पौरिकः सौशिकाश्चैव अश्मका भोगवर्द्धनाः ।
वैषिकाः कुन्दला अन्ध्रा उद्भिदा नलकारकाः ।
दाक्षिणात्या जनपदास्त्विमे शालकटङ्कटः ॥
13.m: the Paurikas, Sauśikas, Aśmakas, Bhogavardhanas, / Vaiṣikas, Kundalas, Andhras, Udbhidas, and Nalakārakas: / these are the southern realms, O Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa.

13.s:
sūrpārakā kārivanā durgāstālīkaṭaiḥ saha /
pulīyāḥ sasinīlāśca tāpasāstāmasāstathā //
13.d:
सूर्पारका कारिवना दुर्गास्तालीकटैः सह ।
पुलीयाः ससिनीलाश्च तापसास्तामसास्तथा ॥
13.m: The Śūrpārakas, Kārivanas, Durgas with the Tālīkaṭas, / the Pulīyas with the Sinīlas, the Tāpasas, and Tāmasas,

13.s:
kāraskarāstu ramino nāsikyāntaranarmadāḥ /
bhārakacchāḥ samāheyāḥ saha sārasvatairapi //
vātseyāśca surāṣṭrāśca āvantyāścārbudaiḥ saha /
ityete paścimāmāśāṃ sthitā jānapadā janāḥ /
//
13.d:
कारस्करास्तु रमिनो नासिक्यान्तरनर्मदाः ।
भारकच्छाः समाहेयाः सह सारस्वतैरपि ॥
वात्सेयाश्च सुराष्ट्राश्च आवन्त्याश्चार्बुदैः सह ।
इत्येते पश्चिमामाशां स्थिता जानपदा जनाः ।
॥
13.m:
the Kāraskaras, Raminas, Nāsikyas, Antarnarmadas, / Bhārakacchas, Māheyas, along with the Sārasvatas,

the Vātseyas, Surāṣṭras, and Āvantyas along with the Arbudas: / these people of the realms reside in the western quarter.

13.s:
13.52 kāruṣāścaikalavyāśca mekalāścotkalaiḥ saha /
uttamarṇā daśārṇāśca bhojāḥ kiṅkavaraiḥ saha //
13.d:
13.52 कारुषाश्चैकलव्याश्च मेकलाश्चोत्कलैः सह ।
उत्तमर्णा दशार्णाश्च भोजाः किङ्कवरैः सह ॥
13.m: The Kāruṣas, Ekalavyas, Mekalas along with the Utkalas, / Uttamarṇas, Daśārṇas, Bhojas with the Kiṅkavaras,

13.s:
tośalā kośalāścaiva traipurāścaillikāstathā /
turusāstumbarāścaiva vahanāḥ naiṣadhaiḥ saha //
13.d:
तोशला कोशलाश्चैव त्रैपुराश्चैल्लिकास्तथा ।
तुरुसास्तुम्बराश्चैव वहनाः नैषधैः सह ॥
13.m: the Tośalas, Kośalas, Traipuras, and Aillikas, / Turusas, Tumbaras, and Vahanas with the Naiṣadhas,

13.s:
anūpāstuṇḍikerāśca vītahotrāstvavantayaḥ /
sukeśe vandhyamūlasthastvime janapadāḥ smṛtāḥ //
13.d:
अनूपास्तुण्डिकेराश्च वीतहोत्रास्त्ववन्तयः ।
सुकेशे वन्ध्यमूलस्थस्त्विमे जनपदाः स्मृताः ॥
13.m: the Anūpas, Tuṇḍikeras, Vītahotras, and Avantīs: / these realms, O Sukeśin, are known to be situated at the foot of the Vindhya.

13.s:
atho deśān pravakṣyāmaḥ parvatāśrayiṇastu ye /
nirāhārā haṃsamārgāḥ kupathāstaṅgaṇāḥ khaśāḥ //
13.d:
अथो देशान् प्रवक्ष्यामः पर्वताश्रयिणस्तु ये ।
निराहारा हंसमार्गाः कुपथास्तङ्गणाः खशाः ॥
13.m: Now we shall speak of the lands that dwell in the mountains: / the Nirāhāras, Haṃsamārgas, Kupathas, Taṅgaṇas, Khaśas,

13.s:
kuthaprāvaraṇāścaiva ūrṇāḥ capuṇyāḥ sahūhukāḥ /
trigarttāśca kirātāśca tomarāḥ śiśirādrikāḥ //
13.d:
कुथप्रावरणाश्चैव ऊर्णाः चपुण्याः सहूहुकाः ।
त्रिगर्त्ताश्च किराताश्च तोमराः शिशिराद्रिकाः ॥
13.m: the Kuthaprāvaraṇas, Ūrṇas, Capuṇyas, Sahūhukas, / Trigartas, Kirātas, Tomaras, and Śiśirādrikas.

13.s:
ime tavoktā viṣayāḥ suvistarād dvipe kumāre rajanīcareśa /
eteṣu deśeṣu ca deśadharmān saṃkīrtyamānāñ śṛṇu tattvāto hi //
itī śrīvāmanapurāṇe trayodaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
13.d:
इमे तवोक्ता विषयाः सुविस्तराद् द्विपे कुमारे रजनीचरेश ।
एतेषु देशेषु च देशधर्मान् संकीर्त्यमानाञ् शृणु तत्त्वातो हि ॥
इती श्रीवामनपुराणे त्रयोदशो ऽध्यायः
13.m:
These regions in Kumāradvīpa have been described to you in detail, O lord of night-roamers; / hear in truth as the regional customs in these countries are recounted.

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

14.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ /
ahiṃsā satyamastaṃ dānaṃ kṣāntirdamaḥ śamaḥ /
akārpaṇyaṃ ca śaucaṃ ca tapaśca rajanīcara //
14.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तं दानं क्षान्तिर्दमः शमः ।
अकार्पण्यं च शौचं च तपश्च रजनीचर ॥
14.m: The ṛṣis said: / Non-violence, truth, non-stealing, charity, patience, restraint, tranquility, / generosity, purity, and asceticism, O night-roamer:

14.s:
daśāṅgo rākṣasaśreṣṭha dharmo 'sau sārvavarṇikaḥ /
brāhmaṇasyāpi vihitā cāturāśramyakalpanā //
14.d:
दशाङ्गो राक्षसश्रेष्ठ धर्मो ऽसौ सार्ववर्णिकः ।
ब्राह्मणस्यापि विहिता चातुराश्रम्यकल्पना ॥
14.m: this is the ten-fold dharma common to all classes, O best of Rākṣasas; / and the arrangement of the four stages of life is prescribed for the Brahmin.

14.s:
sukeśiruvāca /
viprāṇāṃ cāturāśramyaṃ vistarānme tapodhanāḥ /
ācakṣadhvaṃ na me tṛptiḥ śṛṇvataḥ pratipadyate //
14.d:
सुकेशिरुवाच ।
विप्राणां चातुराश्रम्यं विस्तरान्मे तपोधनाः ।
आचक्षध्वं न मे तृप्तिः शृण्वतः प्रतिपद्यते ॥
14.m: Sukeśin said: / O rich in asceticism, tell me in full / about the four stages of life of the Brahmins; as I listen, satisfaction is not reached.

14.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ /
kṛtopanayanaḥ samyag brahmacārī gurau vaset /
tatra dharmo 'sya yastaṃ ca kathyamānaṃ niśāmaya //
14.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
कृतोपनयनः सम्यग् ब्रह्मचारी गुरौ वसेत् ।
तत्र धर्मो ऽस्य यस्तं च कथ्यमानं निशामय ॥
14.m: The ṛṣis said: / Having properly undergone initiation, the celibate student should dwell with the guru; / hear what his duty is there as it is described.

14.s:
svādhyāyo 'thāgniśuśruṣā snānaṃ bhikṣāṭanaṃ tathā /
gurorniṃvedya taccādyamanujñātena sarvadā //
14.d:
स्वाध्यायो ऽथाग्निशुश्रुषा स्नानं भिक्षाटनं तथा ।
गुरोर्निंवेद्य तच्चाद्यमनुज्ञातेन सर्वदा ॥
14.m: Vedic recitation, service to the fire, bathing, and begging for alms: / offering that to the guru, he should eat, always permitted [by him].

14.s:
guroḥ karmaṇi sodyogaḥ samyakprītyupapādanam /
tenāhūtaḥ paṭheccaiva tatparo nānyamānasaḥ //
14.d:
गुरोः कर्मणि सोद्योगः सम्यक्प्रीत्युपपादनम् ।
तेनाहूतः पठेच्चैव तत्परो नान्यमानसः ॥
14.m: Zealous in the guru's work, bringing about his complete pleasure, / summoned by him, he should study, intent on that with no other thought in mind.

14.s:
ekaṃ dvau sakalān vāpi vedān prāpya surormukhāt /
anujñāto varaṃ dattvā gurave dakṣiṇāṃ tataḥ //
14.d:
एकं द्वौ सकलान् वापि वेदान् प्राप्य सुरोर्मुखात् ।
अनुज्ञातो वरं दत्त्वा गुरवे दक्षिणां ततः ॥
14.m: Having received one, two, or all the Vedas from the mouth of the guru, / granted permission after giving the guru a gift and honorarium,

14.s:
gārhasthyāśramakāmastu gārhasthyāśramamāvaset /
vānaprasthāśramaṃ vāpi caturthaṃ svecchayātmanaḥ //
14.d:
गार्हस्थ्याश्रमकामस्तु गार्हस्थ्याश्रममावसेत् ।
वानप्रस्थाश्रमं वापि चतुर्थं स्वेच्छयात्मनः ॥
14.m: if he desires the householder's stage of life, he should dwell in the householder's stage, / or in the forest-dweller's stage, or the fourth, according to his own wish.

14.s:
tatraiva vā gurorgehe dvijo niṣṭhāmavāpnuyāt /
gurorabhāve tatputre tacchiṣye tatsutaṃ vinā //
14.d:
तत्रैव वा गुरोर्गेहे द्विजो निष्ठामवाप्नुयात् ।
गुरोरभावे तत्पुत्रे तच्छिष्ये तत्सुतं विना ॥
14.m: Or the twice-born may attain his end right there in the guru's house; / in the absence of the guru, [he may dwell] with his son, or with his pupil, if he has no son.

14.s:
śuśrūṣan nirabhīmāno brahmacaryāśramaṃ vaset /
evaṃ jayati mṛtyuṃ sa dvijaḥ śālakaṭaṅkaṭa //
14.d:
शुश्रूषन् निरभीमानो ब्रह्मचर्याश्रमं वसेत् ।
एवं जयति मृत्युं स द्विजः शालकटङ्कट ॥
14.m: Serving without pride, he should live in the stage of celibate studenthood; / thus that twice-born conquers death, O Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa.

14.s:
upāvṛttastatastasmād gṛhasthāśramakāmyayā /
asamānarṣikulajāṃ kanyāmudvahed niśācara //
14.d:
उपावृत्तस्ततस्तस्माद् गृहस्थाश्रमकाम्यया ।
असमानर्षिकुलजां कन्यामुद्वहेद् निशाचर ॥
14.m: Having returned from that with the desire for the householder's stage, / he should marry a maiden born in a different ṛṣi lineage, O night-roamer.

14.s:
svakarmaṇā dhanaṃ labdhvā pitṛdevātithīnapi /
samyak saṃprīṇayed bhaktyā sadācārarato dvijaḥ //
14.d:
स्वकर्मणा धनं लब्ध्वा पितृदेवातिथीनपि ।
सम्यक् संप्रीणयेद् भक्त्या सदाचाररतो द्विजः ॥
14.m: Having gained wealth by his own occupation, / the twice-born devoted to proper conduct should fully please the ancestors, gods, and guests with devotion.

14.s:
sadācāro nigadito yuṣmābhirmama suvratāḥ /
lakṣaṇaṃ śrotumicḥāmi kathayadhvaṃ tamadya me //
14.d:
सदाचारो निगदितो युष्माभिर्मम सुव्रताः ।
लक्षणं श्रोतुमिच्ःआमि कथयध्वं तमद्य मे ॥
14.m: [Sukeśin said:] / Proper conduct has been mentioned by you to me, O you of noble vows; / I wish to hear its characteristics; explain it to me today.

14.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ /
sadācāro nigaditastava yo 'smābhirādarāt /
lakṣaṇaṃ tasya vakṣyāmastacchṛṇuṣva niśācara //
14.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
सदाचारो निगदितस्तव यो ऽस्माभिरादरात् ।
लक्षणं तस्य वक्ष्यामस्तच्छृणुष्व निशाचर ॥
14.m: The ṛṣis said: / That proper conduct which was mentioned to you by us with respect, / we shall state its characteristics; listen to that, O night-roamer.

14.s:
gṛhasthena sadā kāryamācāraparipālanam /
na hyācāravihinasya bhadramatra paratra ca //
14.d:
गृहस्थेन सदा कार्यमाचारपरिपालनम् ।
न ह्याचारविहिनस्य भद्रमत्र परत्र च ॥
14.m: The maintenance of conduct must always be observed by the householder; / for there is no well-being in this world or the next for one devoid of proper conduct.

14.s:
yajñadānatapāṃsīha puruṣasya na bhūtaye /
bhavanti yaḥ samullaṅghya sadācāraṃ pravartate //
14.d:
यज्ञदानतपांसीह पुरुषस्य न भूतये ।
भवन्ति यः समुल्लङ्घ्य सदाचारं प्रवर्तते ॥
14.m: Sacrifices, gifts, and austerities here do not bring prosperity to a man / who, having transgressed right conduct, proceeds otherwise.

14.s:
hurācāro hi puruṣo neha nāmutra nandate /
kāryo yatnaḥ sadācāre ācāro hantyalakṣaṇam //
14.d:
हुराचारो हि पुरुषो नेह नामुत्र नन्दते ।
कार्यो यत्नः सदाचारे आचारो हन्त्यलक्षणम् ॥
14.m: Indeed, a man of bad conduct rejoices neither here nor in the hereafter; / effort should be made in right conduct, for right conduct destroys inauspicious marks.

14.s:
tasya svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ sadācārasya rākṣasa /
śṛṇuṣvaikamanāstacca yadi śreyo 'bhivāñchasi //
14.d:
तस्य स्वरूपं वक्ष्यामः सदाचारस्य राक्षस ।
शृणुष्वैकमनास्तच्च यदि श्रेयो ऽभिवाञ्छसि ॥
14.m: We shall describe its true nature, that of right conduct, O Rākṣasa; / listen with one mind to it, if you desire your highest welfare.

14.s:
dharmo 'sya mūlaṃ dhanamasya śākhā puṣpaṃ ca kāmaḥ phalamasya mokṣaḥ /
asau sadācārataruḥ sukeśin saṃsevito yena sa puṇyabhokta //
14.d:
धर्मो ऽस्य मूलं धनमस्य शाखा पुष्पं च कामः फलमस्य मोक्षः ।
असौ सदाचारतरुः सुकेशिन् संसेवितो येन स पुण्यभोक्त ॥
14.m: Righteousness is its root, wealth is its branch, desire is its flower, and its fruit is liberation; / this is the tree of right conduct, O Sukeśin: he who attends upon it is an enjoyer of merit.

14.s:
brahmo muhūrte prathamaṃ vibudhyedanusmared devavarān maharṣīn /
prābhātikaṃ maṅgalameva vācyaṃ yaduktavān devapatistrinetraḥ //
14.d:
ब्रह्मो मुहूर्ते प्रथमं विबुध्येदनुस्मरेद् देववरान् महर्षीन् ।
प्राभातिकं मङ्गलमेव वाच्यं यदुक्तवान् देवपतिस्त्रिनेत्रः ॥
14.m: One should awake first at the hour of Brahma, and recall to mind the foremost gods and great sages; / only an auspicious morning greeting must be uttered, which the three-eyed Lord of gods spoke.

14.s:
sukeśiruvāca /
kiṃ taduktaṃ suprabhātaṃ śaṅkareṇa mahātmanā /
prabhāte yat paṭhan martyo mucyate pāpabandhanāt //
14.d:
सुकेशिरुवाच ।
किं तदुक्तं सुप्रभातं शङ्करेण महात्मना ।
प्रभाते यत् पठन् मर्त्यो मुच्यते पापबन्धनात् ॥
14.m: Sukeśin said: / What was that auspicious morning hymn uttered by the great-souled Śaṅkara, / by reciting which at dawn a mortal is freed from the bond of sins?

14.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ /
śrūyatāṃ rākṣasaśreṣṭha suprabhātaṃ haroditam /
śrutvā smṛtvā paṭhitvā ca sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
14.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
श्रूयतां राक्षसश्रेष्ठ सुप्रभातं हरोदितम् ।
श्रुत्वा स्मृत्वा पठित्वा च सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
14.m: The sages said: / Let it be heard, O foremost of Rākṣasas, the auspicious morning hymn proclaimed by Hara; / having heard, remembered, and recited it, one is completely freed from all sins.

14.s:
brahma murāristripurāntakārī bhānuḥ śaśī bhūmisuto budhaśca /
guruśca śukraḥ saha bhānujena kurvantu sarve mama suprabhātam //
14.d:
ब्रह्म मुरारिस्त्रिपुरान्तकारी भानुः शशी भूमिसुतो बुधश्च ।
गुरुश्च शुक्रः सह भानुजेन कुर्वन्तु सर्वे मम सुप्रभातम् ॥
14.m: May Brahmā, Murāri, the destroyer of Tripura, the sun, the moon, and the son of the earth (Mars), and Mercury, / and Jupiter, and Śukra, along with the son of the sun (Saturn)—may they all make my morning auspicious.

14.s:
bhṛgurvasiṣṭhaḥ kraturaṅgirāśca manuḥ pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ sagautamaḥ /
raibhyo marīciścyavano ṛbhuśca kurvantu sarve mama suprabhātam //
14.d:
भृगुर्वसिष्ठः क्रतुरङ्गिराश्च मनुः पुलस्त्यः पुलहः सगौतमः ।
रैभ्यो मरीचिश्च्यवनो ऋभुश्च कुर्वन्तु सर्वे मम सुप्रभातम् ॥
14.m: May Bhṛgu, Vasiṣṭha, Kratu, and Aṅgiras, Manu, Pulastya, Pulaha along with Gautama, / Raibhya, Marīci, Cyavana, and Ṛbhu—may they all make my morning auspicious.

14.s:
sanatkumāraḥ sanakaḥ sanandanaḥ sanātano 'pyāsuripiṅgalau ca /
sapta svarāḥ sapta rasātalāśca kurvantu sarve mama suprabhātam //
14.d:
सनत्कुमारः सनकः सनन्दनः सनातनो ऽप्यासुरिपिङ्गलौ च ।
सप्त स्वराः सप्त रसातलाश्च कुर्वन्तु सर्वे मम सुप्रभातम् ॥
14.m: May Sanatkumāra, Sanaka, Sanandana, and Sanātana, as well as Āsuri and Piṅgala, / the seven musical notes, and the seven Rasātalas—may they all make my morning auspicious.

14.s:
pṛthvī sagandhā sarasāstathā'paḥ sparśaśca vāyurjvalanaḥ satejāḥ /
nabhaḥ saśabdaṃ mahatā sahaiva yacchantu sarve mama suprabhātam //
14.d:
पृथ्वी सगन्धा सरसास्तथाऽपः स्पर्शश्च वायुर्ज्वलनः सतेजाः ।
नभः सशब्दं महता सहैव यच्छन्तु सर्वे मम सुप्रभातम् ॥
14.m: May the earth with its smell, and likewise water with its taste, touch and wind, fire with its light, / and space with its sound, together with the Mahat—may they all grant me an auspicious morning.

14.s:
saptārṇavāḥ sapta kulācalāśca saptarṣayo dvīpavarāśca sapta /
bhūrādi kṛtvā bhuvanāni sapta dadantu sarve mama suprabhātam //
14.d:
सप्तार्णवाः सप्त कुलाचलाश्च सप्तर्षयो द्वीपवराश्च सप्त ।
भूरादि कृत्वा भुवनानि सप्त ददन्तु सर्वे मम सुप्रभातम् ॥
14.m: May the seven oceans and the seven principal mountain ranges, the seven sages and the seven foremost continents, / and the seven worlds beginning with Bhūr—may they all give me an auspicious morning.

14.s:
itthaṃ prabhāte paramaṃ pavitraṃ paṭhet smaredvā śṛmuyācca bhaktyā /
duḥsvapnanāśo 'nagha suprabhātaṃ bhavecca satyaṃ bhagavatprasādāt //
14.d:
इत्थं प्रभाते परमं पवित्रं पठेत् स्मरेद्वा शृमुयाच्च भक्त्या ।
दुःस्वप्ननाशो ऽनघ सुप्रभातं भवेच्च सत्यं भगवत्प्रसादात् ॥
14.m: One who thus recites, remembers, or hears with devotion this supremely pure [hymn] at dawn / achieves the destruction of bad dreams, O sinless one, and an auspicious morning truly comes to be by the grace of the Lord.

14.s:
tataḥ samutthāya vicintayena dharmaṃ tathārthaṃ ca vihāya śayyām /
utthāya paścāddharirityudīrya gacchet tadotsargavidhiṃ hi kartum //
14.d:
ततः समुत्थाय विचिन्तयेन धर्मं तथार्थं च विहाय शय्याम् ।
उत्थाय पश्चाद्धरिरित्युदीर्य गच्छेत् तदोत्सर्गविधिं हि कर्तुम् ॥
14.m: Then, having arisen and left the bed, one should reflect on righteousness and wealth; / having stood up, and then having uttered 'Hari', one should indeed go to perform the rite of evacuation.

14.s:
na devagobrāhmaṇavahnimārge na rājamārge na catuṣpathe ca /
kuryādathotsargamapīha goṣṭhe pūrvāparāṃ caiva samāśrito gām //
14.d:
न देवगोब्राह्मणवह्निमार्गे न राजमार्गे न चतुष्पथे च ।
कुर्यादथोत्सर्गमपीह गोष्ठे पूर्वापरां चैव समाश्रितो गाम् ॥
14.m: Not on the path of gods, cows, Brahmins, or fire, nor on the royal highway, nor at a crossroads, / nor in a cow-pen here should one perform evacuation, facing east or west.

14.s:
tatastu śaucārthamupāharenmṛdaṃ gude trayaṃ pāṇitale ca sapta /
tathobhayoḥ pañca catustathaikāṃ liṅge tathaikāṃ mṛdamāhareta //
14.d:
ततस्तु शौचार्थमुपाहरेन्मृदं गुदे त्रयं पाणितले च सप्त ।
तथोभयोः पञ्च चतुस्तथैकां लिङ्गे तथैकां मृदमाहरेत ॥
14.m: Then, for purification, one should fetch earth: three [lumps] for the anus and seven for the left palm; / likewise five for both, and four, and one for the penis—one should bring the earth thus.

14.s:
nāntarjalādrākṣasa mūṣikasthalāt śaucāvaśiṣṭā śaraṇāt tathānyā /
valmīkamṛccaiva hi śaucanāya grāhya sadācāravidā nareṇa //
14.d:
नान्तर्जलाद्राक्षस मूषिकस्थलात् शौचावशिष्टा शरणात् तथान्या ।
वल्मीकमृच्चैव हि शौचनाय ग्राह्य सदाचारविदा नरेण ॥
14.m: Earth from within water, O Rākṣasa, from a mouse-hole, what remains after cleansing, from a house, or other such, / and earth from an anthill must [never] be taken for purification by a man who knows right conduct.

14.s:
udaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vāpi vidvān prakṣālya pādau bhuvi saṃniviṣṭaḥ /
samācamedadbhiraphenilābhirādau parimṛjya mukhaṃ dviradbhiḥ //
14.d:
उदङ्मुखः प्राङ्मुखो वापि विद्वान् प्रक्षाल्य पादौ भुवि संनिविष्टः ।
समाचमेदद्भिरफेनिलाभिरादौ परिमृज्य मुखं द्विरद्भिः ॥
14.m: Facing north or facing east, seated upon the ground, having washed his feet, the wise man / should sip water that is free of foam, having first wiped his mouth twice with water.

14.s:
tataḥ spṛśetkhāni śiraḥ kareṇa saṃdhyāmupāsīta tataḥ krameṇa /
keśāṃstu saṃśodhya ca dantadhāvanaṃ kṛtvā tathā darpaṇadarśanaṃ ca //
14.d:
ततः स्पृशेत्खानि शिरः करेण संध्यामुपासीत ततः क्रमेण ।
केशांस्तु संशोध्य च दन्तधावनं कृत्वा तथा दर्पणदर्शनं च ॥
14.m: Then he should touch the apertures [of the head] and the head with his hand, and then attend to twilight worship in proper order; / having cleaned his hair, cleaned his teeth, and looked into a mirror,

14.s:
kṛtvā śiraḥsnānamathāṅiḍkaṃ vā saṃpūjya toyena pitṝn sadevān /
homaṃ ca kṛtvālabhanaṃ śubhānāṃ kṛtvā bahirnirgamanaṃ praśastam //
14.d:
कृत्वा शिरःस्नानमथाङिड्कं वा संपूज्य तोयेन पितॄन् सदेवान् ।
होमं च कृत्वालभनं शुभानां कृत्वा बहिर्निर्गमनं प्रशस्तम् ॥
14.m: having bathed with his head or his limbs, and having worshipped the ancestors along with the gods with water, / and having performed the fire offering and touched auspicious things, going outside is praised.

14.s:
dūrvādadhisarpirathodakumbhaṃ dhenuṃ savatsāṃ vṛṣabhaṃ suvarṇam /
mṛdgomayaṃ svastikamakṣatāni lājāmadhu brāhmaṇakanyakāṃ ca //
14.d:
दूर्वादधिसर्पिरथोदकुम्भं धेनुं सवत्सां वृषभं सुवर्णम् ।
मृद्गोमयं स्वस्तिकमक्षतानि लाजामधु ब्राह्मणकन्यकां च ॥
14.m: Dūrvā grass, curd, clarified butter, a water jar, a cow with its calf, a bull, gold, / earth, cow dung, a svastika, unbroken grains, roasted grain, honey, and a Brahmin maiden,

14.s:
śvetāni puṣpāṇyatha śobhanāni hutāśanaṃ candamarkabimbam /
aśvatthavṛkṣaṃ ca samālabheta tatastu kuryānnijajātidharmam //
14.d:
श्वेतानि पुष्पाण्यथ शोभनानि हुताशनं चन्दमर्कबिम्बम् ।
अश्वत्थवृक्षं च समालभेत ततस्तु कुर्यान्निजजातिधर्मम् ॥
14.m: beautiful white flowers, fire, sandalwood, the orb of the sun, / and an aśvattha tree—these he should touch; and then he should perform the duties of his own caste.

14.s:
deśānuśiṣṭaṃ kula dharmamagryaṃ svagotradharmaṃ na hi saṃtyajet /
tenārthasiddhiṃ samupācareta nāsatpralāpaṃ na ca satyahīnam //
14.d:
देशानुशिष्टं कुल धर्ममग्र्यं स्वगोत्रधर्मं न हि संत्यजेत् ।
तेनार्थसिद्धिं समुपाचरेत नासत्प्रलापं न च सत्यहीनम् ॥
14.m: One should not abandon the duty of one's region, the prime duty of one's family, or the duty of one's own clan; / through that he should pursue the attainment of wealth, without false chatter and not lacking truth.

14.s:
na niṣṭhuraṃ nāgamaśāstrahīnaṃ vākyaṃ vadetsādhujanena yena /
nindyo bhavennaiva ca dharmaḥedī saṃgaṃ na cāsatsu nareṣu kuryāt //
14.d:
न निष्ठुरं नागमशास्त्रहीनं वाक्यं वदेत्साधुजनेन येन ।
निन्द्यो भवेन्नैव च धर्मःएदी संगं न चासत्सु नरेषु कुर्यात् ॥
14.m: He should not speak words that are harsh or devoid of the Āgamas and Śāstras, whereby / he would become censured by virtuous people, nor should he violate righteousness; and he should not keep company with wicked men.

14.s:
saṃdhyāsu varjyaṃ surataṃ divā ca sarvāsu yonīṣu parābalāsu /
āgāraśūnyeṣu mahītaleṣu rajasvalāsveva jaleṣu vīra //
14.d:
संध्यासु वर्ज्यं सुरतं दिवा च सर्वासु योनीषु पराबलासु ।
आगारशून्येषु महीतलेषु रजस्वलास्वेव जलेषु वीर ॥
14.m: Sexual intercourse is to be avoided during twilights and by day, with any [forbidden] wombs, with other men's women, / in empty houses, on the bare ground, with menstruating women, and in water, O hero.

14.s:
vṛthāṭanaṃ thā dānaṃ vṛthā ca paśumāraṇam /
na karttavyaṃ gṛhasthena vṛtā dāraparigraham //
14.d:
वृथाटनं था दानं वृथा च पशुमारणम् ।
न कर्त्तव्यं गृहस्थेन वृता दारपरिग्रहम् ॥
14.m: Aimless wandering, vain giving, and the pointless killing of animals, / and taking a wife in vain—these must not be done by a householder.

14.s:
vṛthāṭanānnityahānirvṛthādānāddhanakṣayaḥ /
vṛthā paśughnaḥ prāpnoti pātakaṃ narakapradam //
14.d:
वृथाटनान्नित्यहानिर्वृथादानाद्धनक्षयः ।
वृथा पशुघ्नः प्राप्नोति पातकं नरकप्रदम् ॥
14.m: From aimless wandering comes constant loss; from vain giving, the destruction of wealth; / one who kills an animal in vain incurs a sin that leads to hell.

14.s:
saṃtatyā hāniraślāghayā varṇasaṃkarato bhayam /
bhetavyaṃ ca bhavelloke vṛthādāraparigrahāt //
14.d:
संतत्या हानिरश्लाघया वर्णसंकरतो भयम् ।
भेतव्यं च भवेल्लोके वृथादारपरिग्रहात् ॥
14.m: Loss of lineage, dishonour, and fear from mixture of castes / must be feared in this world from taking a wife in vain.

14.s:
parasve paradāre ca na kāryā buddhiruttamaiḥ /
parasvaṃ narakāyaiva paradārāśca mṛtyave //
14.d:
परस्वे परदारे च न कार्या बुद्धिरुत्तमैः ।
परस्वं नरकायैव परदाराश्च मृत्यवे ॥
14.m: Noble men should never set their minds on another's property or another's wife; / another's property leads straight to hell, and another's wife leads to death.

14.s:
nekṣet parastriyaṃ nagnāṃ na saṃbhāṣena taskarān /
udkyādarśanaṃ sparśaṃ saṃbhāṣaṃ ca vivarjayet //
14.d:
नेक्षेत् परस्त्रियं नग्नां न संभाषेन तस्करान् ।
उद्क्यादर्शनं स्पर्शं संभाषं च विवर्जयेत् ॥
14.m: One should not look upon another's wife naked, nor converse with thieves; / looking upon, touching, and conversing with a menstruating woman must be avoided.

14.s:
naikāsane tathā stheyaṃ sodaryā parajāyayā /
tathaiva syānna mātuśca tathā svaduhitustvapi //
14.d:
नैकासने तथा स्थेयं सोदर्या परजायया ।
तथैव स्यान्न मातुश्च तथा स्वदुहितुस्त्वपि ॥
14.m: Likewise, one should not sit on the same seat with one's sister or another's wife; / in the same way, neither with one's mother nor with one's own daughter.

14.s:
na ca snāyīta vai nagno na śayīta kadācana /
digvāsaso 'pi na tathā paribhramaṇamiṣyate/ /
bhinnāsanabhājanādīn dūrataḥ parivarjayet //
14.d:
न च स्नायीत वै नग्नो न शयीत कदाचन ।
दिग्वाससो ऽपि न तथा परिभ्रमणमिष्यते। ।
भिन्नासनभाजनादीन् दूरतः परिवर्जयेत् ॥
14.m: And one should never bathe naked, nor ever sleep naked; / wandering about naked is also not approved; / one should completely avoid from afar broken seats, vessels, and the like.

14.s:
nandāsu nābhyaṅgamupācareta kṣauraṃ ca riktāsu jayāsu māṃsam /
pūrṇāsu yoṣitparivarjayeta bhadrāsu sarvāṇi samācareta //
14.d:
नन्दासु नाभ्यङ्गमुपाचरेत क्षौरं च रिक्तासु जयासु मांसम् ।
पूर्णासु योषित्परिवर्जयेत भद्रासु सर्वाणि समाचरेत ॥
14.m: One should not apply an oil bath on Nandā days, shaving on Riktā days, meat on Jayā days; / one should avoid women on Pūrṇā days; on Bhadrā days, one may do everything.

14.s:
nābhyaṅgamarke na ca bhūmiputre kṣauraṃ ca śukre ravije ca māṃsam /
budheṣu yoṣinna samācareta śeṣeṣu sarvāṇi sadaiva kuryāt //
14.d:
नाभ्यङ्गमर्के न च भूमिपुत्रे क्षौरं च शुक्रे रविजे च मांसम् ।
बुधेषु योषिन्न समाचरेत शेषेषु सर्वाणि सदैव कुर्यात् ॥
14.m: No oil bath on the day of the Sun (Sunday) or of the Son of the Earth (Tuesday), shaving on Friday, and meat on the day of the Son of the Sun (Saturday); / on the days of Mercury (Wednesday) one should not approach a woman; on the remaining days, one may always do everything.

14.s:
citrāsu haste śravaṇe ca tailaṃ kṣauraṃ viśākhāsvabhijitsuvarjyam /
mūle mṛge bhāgrapadāsu māṃsaṃ yoṣinmaghākṛttikayottarāsu //
14.d:
चित्रासु हस्ते श्रवणे च तैलं क्षौरं विशाखास्वभिजित्सुवर्ज्यम् ।
मूले मृगे भाग्रपदासु मांसं योषिन्मघाकृत्तिकयोत्तरासु ॥
14.m: Oil is to be avoided under Citrā, Hasta, and Śravaṇa; shaving under Viśākhā and Abhijit; / meat under Mūla, Mṛgaśīrṣa, and the Bhādrapadās; women under Maghā, Kṛttikā, and the Uttarās.

14.s:
sadaiva jarjyaṃ śayanamudakśirās tathā pratīcyāṃ rajanīcareśa /
bhuñjīta naiveha ca dakṣiṇāmukho na ca pratīcyāmabhibhojanīyam //
14.d:
सदैव जर्ज्यं शयनमुदक्शिरास् तथा प्रतीच्यां रजनीचरेश ।
भुञ्जीत नैवेह च दक्षिणामुखो न च प्रतीच्यामभिभोजनीयम् ॥
14.m: Sleeping with the head to the north is always to be avoided, as well as to the west, O lord of night-wanderers; / and one must never eat here facing south, nor is eating to be done facing west.

14.s:
devālayaṃ caityataruṃ catuṣpathaṃ vidyādhikaṃ cāpi guruṃ pradakṣiṇam /
mālyānnapānaṃ vasanāni yatnato nānyairdhṛtāṃścāpi hi dhārayed budhaḥ //
14.d:
देवालयं चैत्यतरुं चतुष्पथं विद्याधिकं चापि गुरुं प्रदक्षिणम् ।
माल्यान्नपानं वसनानि यत्नतो नान्यैर्धृतांश्चापि हि धारयेद् बुधः ॥
14.m: A temple, a sacred tree, a crossroads, one superior in knowledge, and a guru [are to be kept] to the right; / and a wise man should diligently not wear a garland, or take food, drink, or garments worn by others.

14.s:
snāyācchiraḥsnānatayā ca nityaṃ na kāraṇaṃ caiva vinā niśāsu /
grahoparāge svajanāpayāte muktvā ca janmarkṣagate śaśaṅke //
14.d:
स्नायाच्छिरःस्नानतया च नित्यं न कारणं चैव विना निशासु ।
ग्रहोपरागे स्वजनापयाते मुक्त्वा च जन्मर्क्षगते शशङ्के ॥
14.m: One should always bathe by pouring water over the head, and never at night without a cause, / except during an eclipse of a planet, upon the death of a kinsman, or when the moon enters one's birth star.

14.s:
nābhyaṅgitaṃ kāyamupaspṛśecca snāto na keśān vidhunīta cāpi /
gātrāṇi caivāmbarapāṇinā ca snāto vimṛjyād rajanīcareśa //
14.d:
नाभ्यङ्गितं कायमुपस्पृशेच्च स्नातो न केशान् विधुनीत चापि ।
गात्राणि चैवाम्बरपाणिना च स्नातो विमृज्याद् रजनीचरेश ॥
14.m: One should not touch a body that has been anointed with oil; once bathed, one should not shake out one's hair; / nor, having bathed, should one wipe one's limbs with the end of one's cloth, O lord of night-roamers.

14.s:
vasecca deśeṣu surājakeṣu susaṃhiteṣveva janeṣu nityam /
akrodhanā nyāyaparā amatsarāḥ kṛṣīvalā hyoṣadhayaśca yatra //
14.d:
वसेच्च देशेषु सुराजकेषु सुसंहितेष्वेव जनेषु नित्यम् ।
अक्रोधना न्यायपरा अमत्सराः कृषीवला ह्योषधयश्च यत्र ॥
14.m: One should always dwell in lands that have good rulers and united peoples, / where the cultivators are free from anger, devoted to justice, and without malice, and where medicinal herbs abound.

14.s:
na teṣu deśeṣu vaseta buddhimān sadā nṛpo daṇḍarucistvaśaktaḥ /
jano 'pi nityotsavabaddhavairaḥ sadā jigīṣuśca niśācarendra //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe caturdaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
14.d:
न तेषु देशेषु वसेत बुद्धिमान् सदा नृपो दण्डरुचिस्त्वशक्तः ।
जनो ऽपि नित्योत्सवबद्धवैरः सदा जिगीषुश्च निशाचरेन्द्र ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे चतुर्दशो ऽध्यायः
14.m:
A wise man should never dwell in lands where the king is fond of punishment but powerless, / or where the people are constantly hostile amidst festivals and ever bent on conquest, O lord of night-roamers.

Thus ends the fourteenth chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

15.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ /
yacca jarjyaṃ mahābāho sadādharmasthitairnaraiḥ /
yadbhojyaṃ ca samuddiṣṭaṃ kathayiṣyāmahe vayam //
15.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
यच्च जर्ज्यं महाबाहो सदाधर्मस्थितैर्नरैः ।
यद्भोज्यं च समुद्दिष्टं कथयिष्यामहे वयम् ॥
15.m: The sages said: / That which is to be avoided by men who abide constantly in righteousness, O mighty-armed one, / and that which is declared fit to be eaten, we shall now proclaim.

15.s:
bhojyamannaṃ paryuṣitaṃ snehāktāṃ cirasaṃbhṛtam /
asnehā vrīhayaḥ ślakṣṇā vikārāḥ payasastathā //
15.d:
भोज्यमन्नं पर्युषितं स्नेहाक्तां चिरसंभृतम् ।
अस्नेहा व्रीहयः श्लक्ष्णा विकाराः पयसस्तथा ॥
15.m: Food that is stale, if seasoned with oil and kept for a long time, may be eaten; / so too unctuous rice grains, and refined products of milk.

15.s:
śaśakaḥ śalyako godhā śvāvidho matsyakacchapau /
tadvad dvidalakādīni bhojyāni manurabravīt //
15.d:
शशकः शल्यको गोधा श्वाविधो मत्स्यकच्छपौ ।
तद्वद् द्विदलकादीनि भोज्यानि मनुरब्रवीत् ॥
15.m: The hare, the porcupine, the monitor lizard, the hedgehog, fish, and the tortoise— / likewise split pulses and the like—Manu declared fit to be eaten.

15.s:
maṇiratnapravālānāṃ tadvanmuktāphalasya ca /
śailadārumayānāṃ ca tṛṇamūlauṣadhānyapi //
15.d:
मणिरत्नप्रवालानां तद्वन्मुक्ताफलस्य च ।
शैलदारुमयानां च तृणमूलौषधान्यपि ॥
15.m: For gems, jewels, and coral, and likewise for pearls, / for objects made of stone and wood, and also grass, roots, and medicinal plants,

15.s:
śūrpadhānyājinānāṃ ca saṃhatānāṃ ca vāsasām /
valkalānāmaśeṣāṇāmambunā śuddhiriṣyate //
15.d:
शूर्पधान्याजिनानां च संहतानां च वाससाम् ।
वल्कलानामशेषाणामम्बुना शुद्धिरिष्यते ॥
15.m: for winnowing baskets, grains, animal skins, bundles of garments, / and all bark garments, purification is prescribed by water.

15.s:
sasnehānāmathoṣṇena tilakalkena vāriṇā /
kārpāsikānāṃ vastrāṇāṃ suddhiḥ syātsaha bhasmanā //
15.d:
सस्नेहानामथोष्णेन तिलकल्केन वारिणा ।
कार्पासिकानां वस्त्राणां सुद्धिः स्यात्सह भस्मना ॥
15.m: For oily things, purification is by hot water with sesame paste; / for cotton garments, purification is with water and ashes.

15.s:
nāgadantāsthiśṛṅgāṇāṃ takṣaṇācchuddhiriṣyate /
punaḥ pākena bhāṇḍānāṃ mṛnmayānāṃ ca medhyatā //
15.d:
नागदन्तास्थिशृङ्गाणां तक्षणाच्छुद्धिरिष्यते ।
पुनः पाकेन भाण्डानां मृन्मयानां च मेध्यता ॥
15.m: For ivory, bones, and horns, purification is prescribed by scraping; / and earthen vessels regain purity by being baked again in fire.

15.s:
śuci bhaikṣaṃ kāruhastaḥ paṇyaṃ yoṣinmukhaṃ tathā /
rathyāgatamavijñātaṃ dāsavargeṇa yatkṛtam //
15.d:
शुचि भैक्षं कारुहस्तः पण्यं योषिन्मुखं तथा ।
रथ्यागतमविज्ञातं दासवर्गेण यत्कृतम् ॥
15.m: Pure are alms, an artisan's hand, merchandise, and the mouth of a woman; / so too what is encountered on the road if its origin is unknown, and what is done by a group of slaves;

15.s:
vākpraśastaṃ cirātītamanekāntaritaṃ laghu /
ceṣṭitaṃ bālavṛddhānāṃ bālasya ca mukhaṃ śuci //
15.d:
वाक्प्रशस्तं चिरातीतमनेकान्तरितं लघु ।
चेष्टितं बालवृद्धानां बालस्य च मुखं शुचि ॥
15.m: what is approved by speech, what has happened long ago, what is separated by many intermediaries, light actions, / the movement of children and the elderly, and the mouth of a child are pure.

15.s:
karmāntāṅgāraśālāsu stanandhayasutāḥ striyaḥ /
vāgvipruṣo dvijendrāṇāṃ saṃtaptāścāmbubindavaḥ //
15.d:
कर्मान्ताङ्गारशालासु स्तनन्धयसुताः स्त्रियः ।
वाग्विप्रुषो द्विजेन्द्राणां संतप्ताश्चाम्बुबिन्दवः ॥
15.m: Pure are nursing women in workshops and charcoal sheds, / drops of saliva from the mouths of eminent twice-born, and drops of water heated [by fire].

15.s:
bhūmirviśudhyate khātadāhamārjanagokramaiḥ /
lepādullekhanāt sekād veśma saṃmārjanārjanāt //
15.d:
भूमिर्विशुध्यते खातदाहमार्जनगोक्रमैः ।
लेपादुल्लेखनात् सेकाद् वेश्म संमार्जनार्जनात् ॥
15.m: Ground is purified by excavation, burning, sweeping, and the treading of cows; / a house is purified by plastering, scraping, sprinkling, and sweeping.

15.s:
keśakīṭāvapanne 'nne goghrāte makṣikānvite /
mṛdambubhasmakṣārāṇi prakṣeptavyāni śuddhaye //
15.d:
केशकीटावपन्ने ऽन्ने गोघ्राते मक्षिकान्विते ।
मृदम्बुभस्मक्षाराणि प्रक्षेप्तव्यानि शुद्धये ॥
15.m: When food has been defiled by hair or insects, sniffed by a cow, or touched by flies, / earth, water, ashes, and alkaline water should be applied for its purification.

15.s:
audumbarāṇāṃ cāmlena kṣāreṇa trapusīsayoḥ /
bhasmāmbibhiśca kāṃsyānāṃ śuddhiḥ plāvodravasya ca //
15.d:
औदुम्बराणां चाम्लेन क्षारेण त्रपुसीसयोः ।
भस्माम्बिभिश्च कांस्यानां शुद्धिः प्लावोद्रवस्य च ॥
15.m: Copper vessels are purified with acid, tin and lead with alkaline substance, / bell-metal vessels with ashes and water, and liquid substances by being skimmed.

15.s:
amedhyāktasya mṛttoyairgandhāpaharaṇena ca /
anyeṣāmapi dravyāṇāṃ śuddhirgandhāpahārataḥ //
15.d:
अमेध्याक्तस्य मृत्तोयैर्गन्धापहरणेन च ।
अन्येषामपि द्रव्याणां शुद्धिर्गन्धापहारतः ॥
15.m: For what is smeared with impure matter, purification is by earth and water and the removal of the odor; / for other articles too, purification is effected by the removal of the odor.

15.s:
mātuḥ prasravaṇe vatsaḥ śakuniḥ phalapātane /
gardabho bhāravāhitve śvā mṛgagrahaṇe śuciḥ //
15.d:
मातुः प्रस्रवणे वत्सः शकुनिः फलपातने ।
गर्दभो भारवाहित्वे श्वा मृगग्रहणे शुचिः ॥
15.m: A calf is pure when its mother’s milk flows; a bird is pure when causing fruit to fall; / a donkey is pure while carrying a burden; a dog is pure when seizing game.

15.s:
rathyākardamatoyāni nāvaḥ pathi tṛṇāni ca /
mārutenaiva suddhyanti pakveṣṭakacitāni ca //
15.d:
रथ्याकर्दमतोयानि नावः पथि तृणानि च ।
मारुतेनैव सुद्ध्यन्ति पक्वेष्टकचितानि च ॥
15.m: Mud and water on a street, boats, and grass on a road, / and structures built of baked bricks are purified by the wind alone.

15.s:
śṛtaṃ droṇāḍhakasyānnamamedhyābhiplutaṃ bhavet /
agramuddhṛtya saṃtyājyaṃ śeṣasya prokṣaṇaṃ smṛtam //
15.d:
शृतं द्रोणाढकस्यान्नममेध्याभिप्लुतं भवेत् ।
अग्रमुद्धृत्य संत्याज्यं शेषस्य प्रोक्षणं स्मृतम् ॥
15.m: If cooked food measuring a droṇa or an āḍhaka is contaminated by impure matter, / the topmost part should be removed and thrown away; sprinkling with water is prescribed for the remainder.

15.s:
upavāsaṃ trirātraṃ vā dūṣitānnasya bhojane /
ajñāte jñātapūrve ca naiva śuddhirvidhīyate //
15.d:
उपवासं त्रिरात्रं वा दूषितान्नस्य भोजने ।
अज्ञाते ज्ञातपूर्वे च नैव शुद्धिर्विधीयते ॥
15.m: Fasting for one night or three nights is prescribed for eating defiled food / when done unknowingly; if done knowingly beforehand, no purification is prescribed.

15.s:
udakyāśvānanagnāṃśca sūtikāntyāvasāyinaḥ /
spṛṣṭvā snāyīta śaucārthaṃ tathaiva mṛtahāriṇaḥ //
15.d:
उदक्याश्वाननग्नांश्च सूतिकान्त्यावसायिनः ।
स्पृष्ट्वा स्नायीत शौचार्थं तथैव मृतहारिणः ॥
15.m: Having touched a menstruating woman, a dog, a naked person, a woman in childbed, or an outcaste, / one should bathe for purification, and likewise after touching bearers of a corpse.

15.s:
sasnehamasthi saṃspṛsya savāsāḥ snānamācaret /
ācamyaiva tu niḥsnehaṃ gāmālabhyārkamīkṣya ca //
15.d:
सस्नेहमस्थि संस्पृस्य सवासाः स्नानमाचरेत् ।
आचम्यैव तु निःस्नेहं गामालभ्यार्कमीक्ष्य च ॥
15.m: Having touched a bone with fat, one must bathe with one's clothes on; / but having touched a fatless bone, one is purified merely by sipping water, touching a cow, and looking at the sun.

15.s:
na laṅghayetpurīṣāsṛkṣṭhīvanodvarttanāni ca /
gṛhāducchiṣṭaviṇmūtre pādāmbhāṃsi kṣiped bahiḥ //
15.d:
न लङ्घयेत्पुरीषासृक्ष्ठीवनोद्वर्त्तनानि च ।
गृहादुच्छिष्टविण्मूत्रे पादाम्भांसि क्षिपेद् बहिः ॥
15.m: One must not step over feces, blood, spittle, or cosmetic pastes; / one should cast out from the house leftover food, feces, urine, and foot-washing water.

15.s:
pañcapiṇḍānanuddhatya na snāyāt paravāriṇi /
snāyīta devakhāteṣu sarohadasaritsu ca //
15.d:
पञ्चपिण्डाननुद्धत्य न स्नायात् परवारिणि ।
स्नायीत देवखातेषु सरोहदसरित्सु च ॥
15.m: Without lifting up five lumps of earth, one should not bathe in water belonging to another; / one may bathe in tanks dug by the gods, in natural lakes, pools, and rivers.

15.s:
nodyānādau vikāleṣu prājñastiṣṭhet kadācana /
nālaped janavidviṣṭaṃ vīrahīnāṃ tathā striyam //
15.d:
नोद्यानादौ विकालेषु प्राज्ञस्तिष्ठेत् कदाचन ।
नालपेद् जनविद्विष्टं वीरहीनां तथा स्त्रियम् ॥
15.m: A wise man should never stay in gardens and the like at twilight; / he should not converse with a person hated by people, nor with a woman destitute of husband and son.

15.s:
devatāpitṛsacchāstrayajñavedādinindakaiḥ /
kṛtvā tu sparśamālāpaṃ śuddhyater'kāvalokanāt //
15.d:
देवतापितृसच्छास्त्रयज्ञवेदादिनिन्दकैः ।
कृत्वा तु स्पर्शमालापं शुद्ध्यतेर्ऽकावलोकनात् ॥
15.m: Having touched or spoken with revilers of deities, ancestors, virtuous scriptures, sacrifices, or the Vedas, / one is purified by gazing upon the sun.

15.s:
abhojyāḥ sūtikāṣaṇḍhamārjārākhuśvakukkuṭāḥ /
patitāpaviddhanagnāścāṇḍālādyadhamāśca ye //
15.d:
अभोज्याः सूतिकाषण्ढमार्जाराखुश्वकुक्कुटाः ।
पतितापविद्धनग्नाश्चाण्डालाद्यधमाश्च ये ॥
15.m: Unfit to be eaten from are: a woman in childbed, an impotent man, a cat, a mouse, a dog, a rooster, / an outcaste, an abandoned person, a naked person, and the lowest men, such as a Cāṇḍāla.

15.s:
sukeśiruvāca /
bhavadbhiḥ kīrtitābhojyā ya ete sūtikādayaḥ /
amīṣāṃ śrotumicchāmi tattvato lakṣaṇāni hi //
15.d:
सुकेशिरुवाच ।
भवद्भिः कीर्तिताभोज्या य एते सूतिकादयः ।
अमीषां श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतो लक्षणानि हि ॥
15.m: Sukeśin said: / These persons—the woman in childbed and the rest—have been declared by you to be unfit to eat from; / I wish to hear their characteristics in accordance with reality.

15.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ /
brāhmaṇī brāhmaṇasyaiva yāvarodhatvamāgatā /
tāvubhau sūtiketyuktau tayorannaṃ vigarhitam //
15.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
ब्राह्मणी ब्राह्मणस्यैव यावरोधत्वमागता ।
तावुभौ सूतिकेत्युक्तौ तयोरन्नं विगर्हितम् ॥
15.m: The sages said: / A Brahmin woman who has become the concubine of a Brahmin— / both of them are called 'a woman in childbed'; food from both of them is condemned.

15.s:
na juhotyucite kāle na snāti na dadāti ca /
pitṛdevārcanāddhīnaḥ sa ṣaṇḍhaḥ parigīyate //
15.d:
न जुहोत्युचिते काले न स्नाति न ददाति च ।
पितृदेवार्चनाद्धीनः स षण्ढः परिगीयते ॥
15.m: He who does not offer oblations at the proper time, does not bathe, does not give gifts, / and is devoid of worship to ancestors and deities, is proclaimed to be an impotent man.

15.s:
dambhārthaṃ japate yaśca tapyate yajate tathā /
na paratrārthamudyakto sa mārjāraḥ prakīrtitiḥ //
15.d:
दम्भार्थं जपते यश्च तप्यते यजते तथा ।
न परत्रार्थमुद्यक्तो स मार्जारः प्रकीर्तितिः ॥
15.m: He who recites mantras, practices austerities, and offers sacrifices merely for ostentation, / and is not intent on the hereafter, is declared to be a cat.

15.s:
vibhave sati naivātti na dadāti juhoti ca /
tamāhurākhuṃ tasyānnaṃ bhuktvā kṛcchreṇa suddhyati //
15.d:
विभवे सति नैवात्ति न ददाति जुहोति च ।
तमाहुराखुं तस्यान्नं भुक्त्वा कृच्छ्रेण सुद्ध्यति ॥
15.m: He who, having wealth, neither eats, nor gives, nor offers oblations, / is called a mouse; having eaten his food, one is purified by the kṛcchra penance.

15.s:
yaḥ pareṣāṃ hi marmāṇi nikṛntanniva bhāṣate /
nityaṃ paraguṇadveṣī sa śvāna iti kathyate //
15.d:
यः परेषां हि मर्माणि निकृन्तन्निव भाषते ।
नित्यं परगुणद्वेषी स श्वान इति कथ्यते ॥
15.m: He who speaks as if cutting through the vitals of others / and is constantly envious of the virtues of others, is called a dog.

15.s:
sabhāgatānāṃ yaḥ sabhyaḥ pakṣapātaṃ samāśrayet /
tamāhuḥ kukkuṭaṃ devāstasyāpyannaṃ vigarhitam //
15.d:
सभागतानां यः सभ्यः पक्षपातं समाश्रयेत् ।
तमाहुः कुक्कुटं देवास्तस्याप्यन्नं विगर्हितम् ॥
15.m: A member of an assembly who shows partiality toward those who have come to the assembly / is called a rooster by the gods; his food also is condemned.

15.s:
svagharmaṃ yaḥ sutsṛjya paradharmaṃ samāśrayet /
anāpadi sa vidvadbhiḥ patitaḥ parikīrtyate //
15.d:
स्वघर्मं यः सुत्सृज्य परधर्मं समाश्रयेत् ।
अनापदि स विद्वद्भिः पतितः परिकीर्त्यते ॥
15.m: He who abandons his own duty and takes up the duty of another, / except in times of distress, is proclaimed by the wise to be an outcaste.

15.s:
devatyāgī pitṛtyāgī gurubhaktyaratastathā /
gobrāhmaṇastrīvadhakṛdapaviddhaḥ sa kīrtyate //
15.d:
देवत्यागी पितृत्यागी गुरुभक्त्यरतस्तथा ।
गोब्राह्मणस्त्रीवधकृदपविद्धः स कीर्त्यते ॥
15.m: He who abandons the gods, abandons the ancestors, and takes no delight in devotion to his guru, / and who slays cows, Brahmins, or women, is proclaimed to be an abandoned person.

15.s:
yeṣāṃ kule na vedo 'sti na sāstraṃ naiva ca vratam /
te nagnāḥ kīrtitāḥ sadbhis teṣāmannaṃ vigarhitam //
15.d:
येषां कुले न वेदो ऽस्ति न सास्त्रं नैव च व्रतम् ।
ते नग्नाः कीर्तिताः सद्भिस् तेषामन्नं विगर्हितम् ॥
15.m: Those in whose family there is neither Veda, nor scripture, nor observance— / they are declared by the virtuous to be naked; their food is condemned.

15.s:
āśārtānāmadātā ca dātuśca pratiṣedhakaḥ /
śaraṇāgataṃ yastyajati sa cāṇḍālo 'dhamo naraḥ //
15.d:
आशार्तानामदाता च दातुश्च प्रतिषेधकः ।
शरणागतं यस्त्यजति स चाण्डालो ऽधमो नरः ॥
15.m: He who gives nothing to those who come seeking hope, and prevents a giver from giving, / and he who abandons one who has sought refuge, is a Cāṇḍāla, the lowest of men.

15.s:
yo bāndhavaiḥ parityaktaḥ sādhubhirbrāhmaṇairapi /
kuṇḍāśī yaśca tasyānnaṃ bhuktvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret //
15.d:
यो बान्धवैः परित्यक्तः साधुभिर्ब्राह्मणैरपि ।
कुण्डाशी यश्च तस्यान्नं भुक्त्वा चान्द्रायणं चरेत् ॥
15.m: He who has been cast out by his relatives, by virtuous people, and by Brahmins, / and he who eats the food of an adulteress's son—having eaten his food, one should perform the cāndrāyaṇa penance.

15.s:
yo nityakarmaṇo hāniṃ kuryānnaimittikasya ca /
bhuktvānnaṃ tasya śuddhyeta trirātropoṣito naraḥ //
15.d:
यो नित्यकर्मणो हानिं कुर्यान्नैमित्तिकस्य च ।
भुक्त्वान्नं तस्य शुद्ध्येत त्रिरात्रोपोषितो नरः ॥
15.m: He who neglects regular rites and occasional rites— / having eaten his food, a man is purified by fasting for three nights.

15.s:
gaṇakasya niṣādasya gaṇikābhiṣajostathā /
kadaryasyāpi śuddhyeta trirātropoṣito naraḥ //
15.d:
गणकस्य निषादस्य गणिकाभिषजोस्तथा ।
कदर्यस्यापि शुद्ध्येत त्रिरात्रोपोषितो नरः ॥
15.m: After eating the food of an astrologer, a Niṣāda, a courtesan, a physician, / or a miser, a man is purified by fasting for three nights.

15.s:
nityasya karmaṇo hāniḥ kevalaṃ mṛtajanmasu /
na tu naimittikocchedaḥ karttavyo hi kathañcana //
15.d:
नित्यस्य कर्मणो हानिः केवलं मृतजन्मसु ।
न तु नैमित्तिकोच्छेदः कर्त्तव्यो हि कथञ्चन ॥
15.m: The cessation of regular rites occurs only upon deaths and births; / but the cessation of occasional rites should never be done under any circumstances.

15.s:
jāte putre pituḥ snānaṃ sacailasya vidhīyate /
mṛte ca sarvabandhūnāmityāha bhagavān bhṛguḥ //
15.d:
जाते पुत्रे पितुः स्नानं सचैलस्य विधीयते ।
मृते च सर्वबन्धूनामित्याह भगवान् भृगुः ॥
15.m: When a son is born, bathing with clothes on is prescribed for the father; / and when a person dies, [it is prescribed] for all relatives—so declared the venerable Bhṛgu.

15.s:
pretāya salilaṃ deyaṃ bahirdagdhvā tu gotrajaiḥ /
prame 'hni caturthe vā saptame vāsthisaṃcayam //
15.d:
प्रेताय सलिलं देयं बहिर्दग्ध्वा तु गोत्रजैः ।
प्रमे ऽह्नि चतुर्थे वा सप्तमे वास्थिसंचयम् ॥
15.m: Water should be offered to the deceased by kinsmen after burning [the corpse] outside; / the gathering of the bones should be done on the first, the fourth, or the seventh day.

15.s:
ūrddhvaṃ saṃcayanātteṣāmaṅgasparśo vidhīyate /
sodakaistu kriyā kāryā saṃśuddhaistu sapiṇḍajaiḥ //
15.d:
ऊर्द्ध्वं संचयनात्तेषामङ्गस्पर्शो विधीयते ।
सोदकैस्तु क्रिया कार्या संशुद्धैस्तु सपिण्डजैः ॥
15.m: Touching of their limbs is ordained after the collection [of bones]; / but the rites should be performed with water by the sapindas who have become purified.

15.s:
viṣodbandhanaśastrāmbuvahnipātamṛteṣu ca /
bāle pravrāji saṃnyāse deśāntaramṛte tathā //
15.d:
विषोद्बन्धनशस्त्राम्बुवह्निपातमृतेषु च ।
बाले प्रव्राजि संन्यासे देशान्तरमृते तथा ॥
15.m: And in the case of those who died from poison, hanging, weapons, water, or falling into fire, / or an infant, an ascetic, an ochre-robed renouncer, and likewise one who died in a distant country,

15.s:
sadyaḥ śaucaṃ bhavedvīra taccāpyuktaṃ caturvidham /
garbhasrāve tadevoktaṃ pūrṇakālena cetare //
15.d:
सद्यः शौचं भवेद्वीर तच्चाप्युक्तं चतुर्विधम् ।
गर्भस्रावे तदेवोक्तं पूर्णकालेन चेतरे ॥
15.m: immediate purity occurs, O hero; and that is also declared to be fourfold. / In the case of a miscarriage, that same [period] is declared, but for others, by the full time.

15.s:
brahmaṇānāmahorātraṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ dinatrayama /
ṣaḍrātraṃ caiva vaiśyānāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ dvādaśāhnikam //
15.d:
ब्रह्मणानामहोरात्रं क्षत्रियाणां दिनत्रयम ।
षड्रात्रं चैव वैश्यानां शूद्राणां द्वादशाह्निकम् ॥
15.m: A night and day for Brahmins, three days for Kṣatriyas, / six nights indeed for Vaiśyas, and twelve days for Śūdras;

15.s:
daśadvādaśamāsārddhamāsasaṃkhyairdiṃśca taiḥ /
svāḥ svāḥ karmakriyāḥ kuryuḥ sarve varṇā yathākrāmam //
15.d:
दशद्वादशमासार्द्धमाससंख्यैर्दिंश्च तैः ।
स्वाः स्वाः कर्मक्रियाः कुर्युः सर्वे वर्णा यथाक्रामम् ॥
