15.m: and by those days, numbered by ten, twelve, a half-month, and a month, / all the varṇas should perform their respective rites in due order.

15.s:
pretamuddisya karttavyamekoddiṣṭaṃ vidhānataḥ /
sapiṇḍīkaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ prete āvatsarānnaraiḥ //
15.d:
प्रेतमुद्दिस्य कर्त्तव्यमेकोद्दिष्टं विधानतः ।
सपिण्डीकरणं कार्यं प्रेते आवत्सरान्नरैः ॥
15.m: The ekoddiṣṭa rite should be performed according to the rule, with reference to the departed; / men should perform the sapiṇḍīkaraṇa rite for the departed within a year.

15.s:
tataḥ pitṛtvamāpanne darśapūrṇādibhiḥ subhaiḥ /
prīṇanaṃ tasya karttavyaṃ yathā śrutinidarśanāt //
15.d:
ततः पितृत्वमापन्ने दर्शपूर्णादिभिः सुभैः ।
प्रीणनं तस्य कर्त्तव्यं यथा श्रुतिनिदर्शनात् ॥
15.m: Then, once he has attained the state of an ancestor, his propitiation / should be performed on auspicious [occasions] such as the new moon and full moon, in accordance with the direction of the Veda.

15.s:
piturarthaṃ samuddiśya bhūmidānādikaṃ svayam /
kuryādyenāsya suprītāḥ pitaro yānti rākṣasa //
15.d:
पितुरर्थं समुद्दिश्य भूमिदानादिकं स्वयम् ।
कुर्याद्येनास्य सुप्रीताः पितरो यान्ति राक्षस ॥
15.m: Designating it for the sake of the father, one should oneself make gifts of land and the like, / by which his ancestors depart well pleased, O Rākṣasa.

15.s:
yad yadiṣṭatamaṃ kiñcid yaccāsya dayitaṃ gṛhe /
tattad guṇavate deyaṃ tadevākṣayamicchatā //
15.d:
यद् यदिष्टतमं किञ्चिद् यच्चास्य दयितं गृहे ।
तत्तद् गुणवते देयं तदेवाक्षयमिच्छता ॥
15.m: Whatever is most desirable, and whatever is dear to him in the house, / all that should be given to a virtuous person by one desiring that very [gift] to be inexhaustible.

15.s:
adhyetavyā trayī nityaṃ bhāvyaṃ ca viduṣā sadā /
dharmato dhanamāhāryaṃ yaṣṭavyaṃ cāpi śaktitaḥ //
15.d:
अध्येतव्या त्रयी नित्यं भाव्यं च विदुषा सदा ।
धर्मतो धनमाहार्यं यष्टव्यं चापि शक्तितः ॥
15.m: The triple Veda should be studied daily, and one should always be a learned man; / wealth should be acquired righteously, and sacrifice should be made according to one's power.

15.s:
yaccāpi kurvato nātmā jugupsāmeti rākṣasa /
tat karttavyamaśaṅkena yanna gopyaṃ mahājane //
15.d:
यच्चापि कुर्वतो नात्मा जुगुप्सामेति राक्षस ।
तत् कर्त्तव्यमशङ्केन यन्न गोप्यं महाजने ॥
15.m: And in doing which one's inner self does not feel reproach, O Rākṣasa, / that should be done without hesitation—that which is not to be concealed among the multitude.

15.s:
evamācarato loke puruṣasya gṛhe sataḥ /
dharmārthakāmasaṃprāptiḥ paratreha ca śobhanam //
15.d:
एवमाचरतो लोके पुरुषस्य गृहे सतः ।
धर्मार्थकामसंप्राप्तिः परत्रेह च शोभनम् ॥
15.m: For a man living in the house who conducts himself thus in the world, / there is attainment of dharma, wealth, and desire, and good both in the next world and here.

15.s:
eṣa dūddeśataḥ prokto gṛsthāśrama uttamaḥ /
vānaprasthāśramaṃ dharmaṃ pravakṣyāmo 'vadhāryatām //
15.d:
एष दूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो गृस्थाश्रम उत्तमः ।
वानप्रस्थाश्रमं धर्मं प्रवक्ष्यामो ऽवधार्यताम् ॥
15.m: This excellent householder stage of life has been briefly declared; / we shall proclaim the dharma of the forest-dweller stage of life—let it be understood.

15.s:
apatyasaṃtatiṃ dṛṣṭvā prājño dehasya cānatim /
vānaprasthāśramaṃ dharmaṃ pravakṣyāmo 'vadhāryatām //
15.d:
अपत्यसंततिं दृष्ट्वा प्राज्ञो देहस्य चानतिम् ।
वानप्रस्थाश्रमं धर्मं प्रवक्ष्यामो ऽवधार्यताम् ॥
15.m: Seeing an unbroken line of offspring and the stooping of his body, / a wise man [should enter the forest-dweller stage]—we shall proclaim the dharma of the forest-dweller stage of life; let it be understood.

15.s:
tatrāraṇyopabhogaiśca tapobhiścātmakarṣaṇam /
bhūmau śayyā brahmacaryaṃ pitṛdevātithikriyā //
15.d:
तत्रारण्योपभोगैश्च तपोभिश्चात्मकर्षणम् ।
भूमौ शय्या ब्रह्मचर्यं पितृदेवातिथिक्रिया ॥
15.m: There, through the forest's provisions and ascetic practices, there is the emaciation of oneself, / lying on the ground, celibacy, rites for ancestors, gods, and guests,

15.s:
homastriṣavaṇaṃ snānaṃ jaṭāvalkaladhāraṇam /
vanyasnehaniṣevitvaṃ vānaprasthavidhistvayam //
15.d:
होमस्त्रिषवणं स्नानं जटावल्कलधारणम् ।
वन्यस्नेहनिषेवित्वं वानप्रस्थविधिस्त्वयम् ॥
15.m: the fire sacrifice, bathing at the three junctures of the day, wearing matted hair and bark garments, / and relying on forest unctions: this is the rule for the forest-dweller.

15.s:
sarvasaṅgaparityāgo brahmacaryamamānitā /
jitendriyatvamāvāse naikasmin vasatiściram //
15.d:
सर्वसङ्गपरित्यागो ब्रह्मचर्यममानिता ।
जितेन्द्रियत्वमावासे नैकस्मिन् वसतिश्चिरम् ॥
15.m: Abandonment of all attachment, celibacy, absence of pride, / mastery of the senses, and not dwelling long in a single habitation;

15.s:
ananārambhastathāhāro bhaikṣānnaṃ nātikopitā /
ātmajñānāvabodhecchā tathā cātmāvabodhanam //
15.d:
अननारम्भस्तथाहारो भैक्षान्नं नातिकोपिता ।
आत्मज्ञानावबोधेच्छा तथा चात्मावबोधनम् ॥
15.m: abstaining from undertakings, food obtained as alms, lack of excessive anger, / desire for comprehension of knowledge of the Self, and indeed comprehension of the Self;

15.s:
caturthe tvāśrame dharmā asmābhiste prakīrtitāḥ /
varṇadharmāṇi cānyāni niśāmaya niśācara //
15.d:
चतुर्थे त्वाश्रमे धर्मा अस्माभिस्ते प्रकीर्तिताः ।
वर्णधर्माणि चान्यानि निशामय निशाचर ॥
15.m: the dharmas in the fourth stage of life have thus been proclaimed to you by us; / and hear the other duties of the varṇas, O night-roamer!

15.s:
gārhasthyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ ca vānaprasthaṃ trayāśramāḥ /
kṣatriyasyāpi kathitā ye cācārā dvijasya hi //
15.d:
गार्हस्थ्यं ब्रह्मचर्यं च वानप्रस्थं त्रयाश्रमाः ।
क्षत्रियस्यापि कथिता ये चाचारा द्विजस्य हि ॥
15.m: Householder life, celibate studenthood, and forest-dwelling: three stages of life / are declared also for the Kṣatriya, as are the practices of the twice-born.

15.s:
vaikhānasatvaṃ gārhasthyamāśramadvitayaṃ viśaḥ /
gārhasthyayamuttamaṃ tvekaṃ śūdrasya kṣaṇadācara //
15.d:
वैखानसत्वं गार्हस्थ्यमाश्रमद्वितयं विशः ।
गार्हस्थ्ययमुत्तमं त्वेकं शूद्रस्य क्षणदाचर ॥
15.m: The state of the hermit and householder life are the two stages of life for the Vaiśya; / but only the excellent householder life is for the Śūdra, O night-roamer.

15.s:
svāni varṇāśramoktāni dharmāṇīha na hāpayet /
yo hāpayati tasyāsau parikupyati bhāskaraḥ //
15.d:
स्वानि वर्णाश्रमोक्तानि धर्माणीह न हापयेत् ।
यो हापयति तस्यासौ परिकुप्यति भास्करः ॥
15.m: One should not abandon one's own dharmas declared for varṇa and stage of life in this world; / against him who abandons them, the Sun becomes exceedingly enraged.

15.s:
kupitaḥ kulanāśāya īśvaro rogavṛddhaye /
bhānurvai yatate tasya narasya kṣaṇadācara //
15.d:
कुपितः कुलनाशाय ईश्वरो रोगवृद्धये ।
भानुर्वै यतते तस्य नरस्य क्षणदाचर ॥
15.m: Enraged, the lord, the Sun, strives indeed / for the destruction of the family and increase of diseases of that man, O night-roamer.

15.s:
tasmāt svaradharmaṃ na hi saṃtyajeta na hāpayeccāpi hi nātmavaṃśam /
yaḥ saṃtyajeccāpi nijaṃ hi dharmaṃ tasmai prakupyeta divākarastu //
15.d:
तस्मात् स्वरधर्मं न हि संत्यजेत न हापयेच्चापि हि नात्मवंशम् ।
यः संत्यजेच्चापि निजं हि धर्मं तस्मै प्रकुप्येत दिवाकरस्तु ॥
15.m: Therefore, one must not abandon one's own dharma, nor indeed should one cause one's lineage to perish; / for against him who abandons his own dharma, the Sun becomes enraged.

15.s:
pulastya uvāca /
ityevamukto munibhiḥ sukeśī praṇamya tān brahmanidhīn maharṣīn /
jagāma cotpatya puraṃ svakīyaṃ muhurmuhurdharmamavekṣamāṇaḥ //
15.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
इत्येवमुक्तो मुनिभिः सुकेशी प्रणम्य तान् ब्रह्मनिधीन् महर्षीन् ।
जगाम चोत्पत्य पुरं स्वकीयं मुहुर्मुहुर्धर्ममवेक्षमाणः ॥
15.m: Pulastya said: / Addressed thus by the sages, Sukeśin, having bowed down to those great sages, treasures of sacred lore, / flew up and went to his own city, continually reflecting upon dharma.

16.s:
pulastya uvāca /
tataḥ sukeśirdevarṣe gatvā svapuramuttamam /
samhūyābravīt sarvān rākṣasān dhārmikaṃ vacaḥ //
16.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
ततः सुकेशिर्देवर्षे गत्वा स्वपुरमुत्तमम् ।
सम्हूयाब्रवीत् सर्वान् राक्षसान् धार्मिकं वचः ॥
16.m: Pulastya said: / Then Sukeśin, O divine sage, having gone to his excellent city, / summoned all the Rākṣasas and spoke righteous words:

16.s:
ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ śaucamindriyasaṃyamaḥ /
dānaṃ dayā ca kṣāntiśva brahmacaryamamānitā //
16.d:
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयं शौचमिन्द्रियसंयमः ।
दानं दया च क्षान्तिश्व ब्रह्मचर्यममानिता ॥
16.m: “Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, purity, restraint of the senses, / generosity, compassion, patience, celibacy, absence of pride,

16.s:
śubhā satyā ca madhurā vāṅ nityaṃ satkriyā ratiḥ /
sadācāraniṣevitvaṃ paralokapradāyakāḥ //
16.d:
शुभा सत्या च मधुरा वाङ् नित्यं सत्क्रिया रतिः ।
सदाचारनिषेवित्वं परलोकप्रदायकाः ॥
16.m: auspicious, true, and sweet speech, constant delight in good deeds, / and adherence to righteous conduct are the bestowers of the other world.

16.s:
ityūcurmunayo mahyaṃ dharmamādyaṃ purātanam /
sohamājñāpaye sarvān kriyatāmavikalpataḥ //
16.d:
इत्यूचुर्मुनयो मह्यं धर्ममाद्यं पुरातनम् ।
सोहमाज्ञापये सर्वान् क्रियतामविकल्पतः ॥
16.m: Thus the sages proclaimed to me the primeval, ancient dharma; / so I command all of you: let it be performed without doubt!”

16.s:
pulastya uvāca /
tataḥ sukeśivacanāt sarva eva niśācarāḥ /
trayodaśāṅgaṃ te dharma cakrurmuditamānasāḥ //
16.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
ततः सुकेशिवचनात् सर्व एव निशाचराः ।
त्रयोदशाङ्गं ते धर्म चक्रुर्मुदितमानसाः ॥
16.m: Pulastya said: / Then, at the word of Sukeśin, all the night-roamers indeed / practiced that thirteenfold dharma with delighted minds.

16.s:
tataḥ pravṛddhiṃ sutarāmagacchanta niśācarāḥ /
putrapautrārthasaṃyuktāḥ sadāṭārasamanvitāḥ //
16.d:
ततः प्रवृद्धिं सुतरामगच्छन्त निशाचराः ।
पुत्रपौत्रार्थसंयुक्ताः सदाटारसमन्विताः ॥
16.m: Then the night-roamers attained exceedingly great prosperity, / endowed with sons, grandsons, and wealth, and possessed of good conduct.

16.s:
tajjayotistejasteṣāṃ rākṣasānaṃ mahātmanām /
gantuṃ nāśaktuvan sūryo nakṣatrāṇi na candramāḥ //
16.d:
तज्जयोतिस्तेजस्तेषां राक्षसानं महात्मनाम् ।
गन्तुं नाशक्तुवन् सूर्यो नक्षत्राणि न चन्द्रमाः ॥
16.m: Past the shining brilliance of those noble Rākṣasas, / the sun, the constellations, and the moon were unable to pass.

16.s:
tatastribhuvane brahman niśācarapuro 'bhavat /
divā candrasya sadṛśaḥ kṣaṇadāyāṃ ca sūryavat //
16.d:
ततस्त्रिभुवने ब्रह्मन् निशाचरपुरो ऽभवत् ।
दिवा चन्द्रस्य सदृशः क्षणदायां च सूर्यवत् ॥
16.m: Then throughout the three worlds, O Brahmin, the city of the night-roamers became / like the moon by day, and like the sun at night.

16.s:
na jñāyate gatirvyomni bhāskarasya tato 'mbare /
śaśaṅkamiti tejastvādamanyanta purottamam //
16.d:
न ज्ञायते गतिर्व्योम्नि भास्करस्य ततो ऽम्बरे ।
शशङ्कमिति तेजस्त्वादमन्यन्त पुरोत्तमम् ॥
16.m: Because of that, the course of the Sun in the sky was not recognized in the firmament; / they thought that excellent city was the moon on account of its brilliance.

16.s:
svaṃ vikāsaṃ vimuñcanti niśāmiti vyacintayan /
kamalākareṣu kamalā mitramityavagamya hi /
rātrau vikasitā brahman vibhūtiṃ dātumīpsavaḥ //
16.d:
स्वं विकासं विमुञ्चन्ति निशामिति व्यचिन्तयन् ।
कमलाकरेषु कमला मित्रमित्यवगम्य हि ।
रात्रौ विकसिता ब्रह्मन् विभूतिं दातुमीप्सवः ॥
16.m: Thinking it was night, [day-blooming flowers] shed their bloom; / and realizing that their friend [the sun] was there, O Brahmin, the lotuses in lotus ponds / bloomed at night, wishing to bestow beauty.

16.s:
kauśikā rātrisamayaṃ buddhvā niragaman kila /
tān vāyasāstadā jñātvā divā nighnanti kauśikān //
16.d:
कौशिका रात्रिसमयं बुद्ध्वा निरगमन् किल ।
तान् वायसास्तदा ज्ञात्वा दिवा निघ्नन्ति कौशिकान् ॥
16.m: The owls, perceiving it to be night-time, came forth, indeed; / recognizing them, crows then slew those owls by day.

16.s:
snātakāstvāpagāsveva snānajapyaparāyaṇāḥ /
ākaṇṭhamagnāstiṣṭhanti rātrau jñātvātha vāsaram //
16.d:
स्नातकास्त्वापगास्वेव स्नानजप्यपरायणाः ।
आकण्ठमग्नास्तिष्ठन्ति रात्रौ ज्ञात्वाथ वासरम् ॥
16.m: And the snātakas, dedicated to bathing and muttered prayers in the rivers, / remained submerged up to the neck, thinking the night to be day.

16.s:
na vyayujyanta cakraāśca tadā vai puradarśane /
manmānāstu divasamidamuccairbruvanti ca //
16.d:
न व्ययुज्यन्त चक्रआश्च तदा वै पुरदर्शने ।
मन्मानास्तु दिवसमिदमुच्चैर्ब्रुवन्ति च ॥
16.m: And the cakravāka birds were not separated then at the sight of the city; / thinking it to be day, they said loudly:

16.s:
nūnaṃ kāntāvihīnena kenaciccakrapattriṇā /
utsṛṣṭaṃ jīvitaṃ śūnye phūtkṛtya saritastaṭe //
16.d:
नूनं कान्ताविहीनेन केनचिच्चक्रपत्त्रिणा ।
उत्सृष्टं जीवितं शून्ये फूत्कृत्य सरितस्तटे ॥
16.m: “Surely, by some cakravāka bird bereft of his beloved, / life was abandoned in solitude, shrieking on the riverbank!

16.s:
tato 'nukṛpayāviṣṭo vivasvāstīvraraśmibhiḥ /
saṃtāpayañjagat sarvaṃ nāstameti kathañcana //
16.d:
ततो ऽनुकृपयाविष्टो विवस्वास्तीव्ररश्मिभिः ।
संतापयञ्जगत् सर्वं नास्तमेति कथञ्चन ॥
16.m: Filled with compassion for him, Vivasvat, / scorching the whole world with fierce rays, does not set by any means!”

16.s:
anye vadanti cakraāhvo nṛnaṃ kaścin mṛto bhavet /
tatkāntayā tapastaptaṃ bhartṛśokārttayā bata //
16.d:
अन्ये वदन्ति चक्रआह्वो नृनं कश्चिन् मृतो भवेत् ।
तत्कान्तया तपस्तप्तं भर्तृशोकार्त्तया बत ॥
16.m: Others said: “Surely some male cakravāka must have died; / alas, by his beloved wife, tormented by grief for her husband, austerity was performed!

16.s:
ārādhitastu bhagavāṃstapasā vai divākaraḥ /
tenāsau śaśinirjetā nāstameti ravirdhruvam //
16.d:
आराधितस्तु भगवांस्तपसा वै दिवाकरः ।
तेनासौ शशिनिर्जेता नास्तमेति रविर्ध्रुवम् ॥
16.m: The blessed Sun was indeed propitiated by her austerity; / therefore, that sun, vanquisher of the moon, certainly does not set!”

16.s:
yajvino homaśālāsu saha ṛtvigbhiradhvare /
prāvarttayanta karmāṇi rātrāvapi mahāmune //
16.d:
यज्विनो होमशालासु सह ऋत्विग्भिरध्वरे ।
प्रावर्त्तयन्त कर्माणि रात्रावपि महामुने ॥
16.m: In the sacrifice halls, sacrificers together with the officiating priests / carried on the rites of the sacrifice even at night, O great sage.

16.s:
mahābhāgavatāḥ pūjāṃ viṣṇoḥ kurvanti bhaktitaḥ /
ravau śaśini caivānye brahmaṇo 'nye harasya ca //
16.d:
महाभागवताः पूजां विष्णोः कुर्वन्ति भक्तितः ।
रवौ शशिनि चैवान्ये ब्रह्मणो ऽन्ये हरस्य च ॥
16.m: The great devotees performed worship of Viṣṇu with devotion; / others to the sun and to the moon, and others to Brahmā and to Hara.

16.s:
kāminaścāpyamanyanta sādhu candramasā kṛtam /
yadiyaṃ rajanī ramyā kṛtā satatakaumudī //
16.d:
कामिनश्चाप्यमन्यन्त साधु चन्द्रमसा कृतम् ।
यदियं रजनी रम्या कृता सततकौमुदी ॥
16.m: And lovers thought: “It is well done by the moon / that this delightful night has been made into continuous moonlight!”

16.s:
anye 'bruvaṃllokagururasmābhiścakrabhṛd vaśī /
nirvyājena mahāgandhairarcitaḥ kusumaiḥ śubhaiḥ //
16.d:
अन्ये ऽब्रुवंल्लोकगुरुरस्माभिश्चक्रभृद् वशी ।
निर्व्याजेन महागन्धैरर्चितः कुसुमैः शुभैः ॥
16.m: Others said: “By us the teacher of the worlds, the self-controlled wielder of the discus, / has been unfeignedly worshipped with great perfumes and auspicious flowers!”

16.s:
saha lakṣmyā mahāyogī nabhasyādicaturṣvapi /
aśūnyaśayanā nāma dvitīyā sarvakāmadā //
16.d:
सह लक्ष्म्या महायोगी नभस्यादिचतुर्ष्वपि ।
अशून्यशयना नाम द्वितीया सर्वकामदा ॥
16.m: Together with Lakṣmī, the Great Yogin [was worshipped] in the four [months] beginning with Nabhasya; / the second [tithi], named Aśūnyaśayanā, grants all desires.

16.s:
tenāsau bhagavān prītaḥ prādācchayanamuttamam /
aśūnyaṃ ca mahābhogairanastamitaśekharam //
16.d:
तेनासौ भगवान् प्रीतः प्रादाच्छयनमुत्तमम् ।
अशून्यं च महाभोगैरनस्तमितशेखरम् ॥
16.m: Pleased by this, the Blessed One granted an excellent couch / that is never empty, [filled] with great pleasures, its crown never sinking into darkness.

16.s:
anaye 'bruvan dhruvaṃ devyā rohiṇyāśaśinaḥ kṣayam /
dṛṣṭvā taptaṃ tapo ghoraṃ rudrārādhanakāmyayā //
16.d:
अनये ऽब्रुवन् ध्रुवं देव्या रोहिण्याशशिनः क्षयम् ।
दृष्ट्वा तप्तं तपो घोरं रुद्राराधनकाम्यया ॥
16.m: Others said: "Surely, when the goddess Rohiṇī saw the moon’s decline, / she performed severe asceticism desiring to propitiate Rudra.

16.s:
puṇyāyāmakṣayāṣṭamyāṃ vedoktavidhinā svayam /
tuṣṭena śaṃbhunā dattaṃ varaṃ cāsyai yadṛcchayā //
16.d:
पुण्यायामक्षयाष्टम्यां वेदोक्तविधिना स्वयम् ।
तुष्टेन शंभुना दत्तं वरं चास्यै यदृच्छया ॥
16.m: On the holy Akṣayāṣṭamī, according to the rule prescribed in the Veda, by herself; / and Śambhu, being pleased, granted her a boon freely."

16.s:
anye 'bruvan candramasā dhruvamārādhito hariḥ /
vrateneha tvakhaṇḍena tenākhaṇḍaḥ śaśī divi //
16.d:
अन्ये ऽब्रुवन् चन्द्रमसा ध्रुवमाराधितो हरिः ।
व्रतेनेह त्वखण्डेन तेनाखण्डः शशी दिवि ॥
16.m: Others said: "Surely the moon propitiated Hari / with an unbroken observance in this world; therefore the moon is unbroken in heaven."

16.s:
anye 'bravañchaśāṅkena dhruvaṃ rakṣā kṛtātmanaḥ /
padadvayaṃ samabhyarcya viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ //
16.d:
अन्ये ऽब्रवञ्छशाङ्केन ध्रुवं रक्षा कृतात्मनः ।
पदद्वयं समभ्यर्च्य विष्णोरमिततेजसः ॥
16.m: Others said: "The moon surely achieved his own protection / having worshipped the two feet of Viṣṇu of boundless splendor.

16.s:
tenāsau dīptimāṃścandraḥ paribhūya divākaram /
asmākamānandakaro divā tapati sūryavat //
16.d:
तेनासौ दीप्तिमांश्चन्द्रः परिभूय दिवाकरम् ।
अस्माकमानन्दकरो दिवा तपति सूर्यवत् ॥
16.m: By virtue of that, this radiant moon, having surpassed the sun, / bringing us joy, shines by day like the sun.

16.s:
lakṣyate kāraṇairanyairbahubhiḥ satyameva hi /
śaśaṅkanirjitaḥ sūryo na vibhāti yathā purā //
16.d:
लक्ष्यते कारणैरन्यैर्बहुभिः सत्यमेव हि ।
शशङ्कनिर्जितः सूर्यो न विभाति यथा पुरा ॥
16.m: Indeed, from many other signs it is seen to be truly so: / conquered by the moon, the sun does not shine as before.

16.s:
yathāmī kamalāḥ ślakṣṇā raṇadbhṛṅgaṇāvṛtāḥ /
vikacāḥ pratibhāsante jātaḥ sūryodayo dhruvam //
16.d:
यथामी कमलाः श्लक्ष्णा रणद्भृङ्गणावृताः ।
विकचाः प्रतिभासन्ते जातः सूर्योदयो ध्रुवम् ॥
16.m: Just as these delicate lotuses, surrounded by swarms of humming bees, / appear blossomed, surely the sunrise has taken place.

16.s:
yathā cāmī vibhāsanti vikacāḥ kumudākarāḥ /
ato vijñāyate candra uditaśca pratāpavān //
16.d:
यथा चामी विभासन्ति विकचाः कुमुदाकराः ।
अतो विज्ञायते चन्द्र उदितश्च प्रतापवान् ॥
16.m: And just as these beds of night-lotuses shine in full bloom, / therefore it is known that the mighty moon has also risen."

16.s:
evaṃ saṃbhāṣatāṃ tatra sūryo vākyānī nārada /
amanyata kimetaddhi loko vakti śubhāśubham //
16.d:
एवं संभाषतां तत्र सूर्यो वाक्यानी नारद ।
अमन्यत किमेतद्धि लोको वक्ति शुभाशुभम् ॥
16.m: As they were speaking such words there, O Nārada, / the sun considered: "What is this auspicious and inauspicious thing that the people say?"

16.s:
evaṃ saṃcintya bhagavān dadhyau dhyānaṃ divākaraḥ /
āsamantājjagad grastaṃ trailokyaṃ rajanīcaraiḥ //
16.d:
एवं संचिन्त्य भगवान् दध्यौ ध्यानं दिवाकरः ।
आसमन्ताज्जगद् ग्रस्तं त्रैलोक्यं रजनीचरैः ॥
16.m: Thinking thus, the blessed sun entered into meditation: / [and saw that] the world, the three worlds on all sides, had been seized by night-wanderers.

16.s:
tatastu bhagavāñjñātvā tedajaso 'pyasahiṣṇutām /
niśācarasya vṛddhiṃ tāmacintayata yogavit //
16.d:
ततस्तु भगवाञ्ज्ञात्वा तेदजसो ऽप्यसहिष्णुताम् ।
निशाचरस्य वृद्धिं तामचिन्तयत योगवित् ॥
16.m: Then the Blessed One, knower of yoga, having perceived their intolerance of his radiance / and that increase of the night-wanderer, reflected.

16.s:
tato 'jñāsīcca tān sarvān sadācāraratāñśucīn /
devabrāhmaṇapūjāsu saṃsaktān dharmasaṃyutān //
16.d:
ततो ऽज्ञासीच्च तान् सर्वान् सदाचाररताञ्शुचीन् ।
देवब्राह्मणपूजासु संसक्तान् धर्मसंयुतान् ॥
16.m: And then he recognized that all of them were devoted to righteous conduct, pure, / intent on worshiping the gods and Brahmins, and endowed with virtue.

16.s:
tatastu rakṣaḥkṣayakṛt timiradvipakesarī /
mahāṃśunakharaḥ sūryastadvighātamacintayat //
16.d:
ततस्तु रक्षःक्षयकृत् तिमिरद्विपकेसरी ।
महांशुनखरः सूर्यस्तद्विघातमचिन्तयत् ॥
16.m: Then the sun, destroyer of demons, a lion to the elephant of darkness, / whose claws were his great rays, thought of a way to obstruct them.

16.s:
jñātavāṃśca tataśchidraṃ rākṣasānāṃ divaspatiḥ /
svadharmavicyutirnāma sarvadharmavighātakṛt //
16.d:
ज्ञातवांश्च ततश्छिद्रं राक्षसानां दिवस्पतिः ।
स्वधर्मविच्युतिर्नाम सर्वधर्मविघातकृत् ॥
16.m: And then the lord of the sky perceived a flaw among the rākṣasas: / namely, departure from one's own duty, which destroys all virtue.

16.s:
tataḥ krodhābhibhūtena bhānunā ripubhedibhiḥ /
bhānubhī rākṣasapuraṃ tad dṛṣṭaṃ ca yathaicchayā //
16.d:
ततः क्रोधाभिभूतेन भानुना रिपुभेदिभिः ।
भानुभी राक्षसपुरं तद् दृष्टं च यथैच्छया ॥
16.m: Then, overcome with anger, the sun looked upon that city of rākṣasas / as he pleased with his rays that pierce enemies.

16.s:
sa bhānunā tadā dṛṣṭaḥ krodhādhmātena catruṣā /
nipapātāmbarād bhraṣṭaḥ kṣīṇapuṇya iva grahaḥ //
16.d:
स भानुना तदा दृष्टः क्रोधाध्मातेन चत्रुषा ।
निपपाताम्बराद् भ्रष्टः क्षीणपुण्य इव ग्रहः ॥
16.m: Looked upon then by the sun who was swollen with anger in enmity, / it fell, tumbling from the sky like a planet whose merit is exhausted.

16.s:
patamānaṃ samālokya puraṃ śālakaṭaṅkaṭaḥ /
namo bhavāya śarvāya idamuccairudīrayat //
16.d:
पतमानं समालोक्य पुरं शालकटङ्कटः ।
नमो भवाय शर्वाय इदमुच्चैरुदीरयत् ॥
16.m: Seeing the city falling, Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa / loudly uttered this: "Homage to Bhava, to Śarva!"

16.s:
tamākranditamākarṇya cāraṇā gaganecarāḥ /
hā deti cukruśuḥ sarve harabhaktaḥ patatyasau //
16.d:
तमाक्रन्दितमाकर्ण्य चारणा गगनेचराः ।
हा देति चुक्रुशुः सर्वे हरभक्तः पतत्यसौ ॥
16.m: Hearing that cry, the sky-wandering Cāraṇas / all cried out, "Alas! Alas! This devotee of Hara is falling!"

16.s:
taccāraṇavacaḥ śarvaḥ śrutavān sarvago 'vyayaḥ /
śrutvā saṃcintayāmāsa kenāsau pātyate bhuvi //
16.d:
तच्चारणवचः शर्वः श्रुतवान् सर्वगो ऽव्ययः ।
श्रुत्वा संचिन्तयामास केनासौ पात्यते भुवि ॥
16.m: Śarva, the omnipresent and imperishable, heard that utterance of the Cāraṇas; / having heard it, he wondered: "By whom is he being thrown down to the earth?"

16.s:
jñātavān devapatinā sahasrakiraṇena tat /
pātitaṃ rākṣasapuraṃ tataḥ kruddhastrilocanaḥ //
16.d:
ज्ञातवान् देवपतिना सहस्रकिरणेन तत् ।
पातितं राक्षसपुरं ततः क्रुद्धस्त्रिलोचनः ॥
16.m: He learned that the city of the rākṣasas had been brought down / by the thousand-rayed lord of the gods; then the three-eyed one was enraged.

16.s:
kruddhastu bhagavantaṃ taṃ bhānumantamapaśyata /
dṛṣṭamātrastriṇetreṇa nipapāta tato 'mabarāt //
16.d:
क्रुद्धस्तु भगवन्तं तं भानुमन्तमपश्यत ।
दृष्टमात्रस्त्रिणेत्रेण निपपात ततो ऽमबरात् ॥
16.m: Enraged, he looked upon the blessed sun; / as soon as he was seen by the three-eyed god, [the sun] fell from the sky.

16.s:
gaganāt sa paribhraṣṭaḥ pathi vāyuniṣevite /
yadṛcchayā nipatito yantramukto yathopalaḥ //
16.d:
गगनात् स परिभ्रष्टः पथि वायुनिषेविते ।
यदृच्छया निपतितो यन्त्रमुक्तो यथोपलः ॥
16.m: Fallen from the sky into the path frequented by the wind, / he plunged at random like a stone cast from a catapult.

16.s:
tato vāyupathānmuktaḥ kiṃśukojjvalavigrahaḥ /
nipapātāntarikṣāt sa vṛtaḥ kinnaracāraṇaiḥ //
16.d:
ततो वायुपथान्मुक्तः किंशुकोज्ज्वलविग्रहः ।
निपपातान्तरिक्षात् स वृतः किन्नरचारणैः ॥
16.m: Then, loosed from the wind’s path, his form radiant like the kiṃśuka blossom, / he fell from the intermediate space, surrounded by Kinnaras and Cāraṇas.

16.s:
cāraṇerveṣṭito bhānuḥ pravibhātyambarāt patan /
arddhapakvaṃ yathā tālāt phalaṃ kapibhirāvṛtam //
16.d:
चारणेर्वेष्टितो भानुः प्रविभात्यम्बरात् पतन् ।
अर्द्धपक्वं यथा तालात् फलं कपिभिरावृतम् ॥
16.m: Surrounded by Cāraṇas, the sun falling from the sky shone / like a half-ripe fruit falling from a palmyra tree, covered with monkeys.

16.s:
tatastu ṛṣayo 'bhyetya pratyūcurbhānumālinam /
nipatasva harikṣetre yadi śreyo 'bhivāñchasi //
16.d:
ततस्तु ऋषयो ऽभ्येत्य प्रत्यूचुर्भानुमालिनम् ।
निपतस्व हरिक्षेत्रे यदि श्रेयो ऽभिवाञ्छसि ॥
16.m: Then the sages approached and said to the sun: / "Fall down into the sacred ground of Hari, if you desire welfare!"

16.s:
tato 'vravīt patanneva vivasvāṃstāṃstapodhanān /
kiṃ tat kṣetraṃ hareḥ puṇyaṃ vadadhvaṃ śīghrameva me //
16.d:
ततो ऽव्रवीत् पतन्नेव विवस्वांस्तांस्तपोधनान् ।
किं तत् क्षेत्रं हरेः पुण्यं वदध्वं शीघ्रमेव मे ॥
16.m: Then the sun, even as he was falling, spoke to those rich in asceticism: / "What is that holy sacred ground of Hari? Tell me at once!"

16.s:
tamūcurmunayaḥ sūryaṃ śṛṇu kṣetraṃ mahāphalam /
sāmprataṃ vāsudevasya bhāvi tacchaṅkarasya ca //
16.d:
तमूचुर्मुनयः सूर्यं शृणु क्षेत्रं महाफलम् ।
साम्प्रतं वासुदेवस्य भावि तच्छङ्करस्य च ॥
16.m: The sages said to the sun: "Hear about the sacred ground that yields great fruit; / at present it belongs to Vāsudeva, and in the future it will belong to Śaṅkara.

16.s:
yogaśāyinamārabhya yāvat keśavadarśanam /
etat kṣetraṃ hareḥ puṇyaṃ nāmnā vārāṇasī purī //
16.d:
योगशायिनमारभ्य यावत् केशवदर्शनम् ।
एतत् क्षेत्रं हरेः पुण्यं नाम्ना वाराणसी पुरी ॥
16.m: Beginning from the Sleeping Yogin up to the sight of Keśava, / this holy sacred ground of Hari is the city named Vārāṇasī."

16.s:
tacchrutvā bhagavān bhānurbhavanetrāgnitāpitaḥ /
varaṇāyāstathaivāsyāstvantare nipapāta ha //
16.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान् भानुर्भवनेत्राग्नितापितः ।
वरणायास्तथैवास्यास्त्वन्तरे निपपात ह ॥
16.m: Hearing that, the blessed sun, scorched by the fire of Bhava’s eye, / fell down between the Varaṇā and the Asī.

16.s:
tataḥ pradahyati tanau nimajyāsyāṃ lulad raviḥ /
varaṇāyāṃ samabhyetya nyamajjata yathecchayā //
16.d:
ततः प्रदह्यति तनौ निमज्यास्यां लुलद् रविः ।
वरणायां समभ्येत्य न्यमज्जत यथेच्छया ॥
16.m: Then, as his body burned, plunging into this [Asī], the rolling sun / reached the Varaṇā and submerged himself as he pleased.

16.s:
bhuyo 'siṃ varaṇāṃ bhūyo bhūyo 'pi varaṇāmasim /
lulaṃstriṇetravahnyārtto bhramate 'lātacakravat //
16.d:
भुयो ऽसिं वरणां भूयो भूयो ऽपि वरणामसिम् ।
लुलंस्त्रिणेत्रवह्न्यार्त्तो भ्रमते ऽलातचक्रवत् ॥
16.m: Rolling again into the Asī, again into the Varaṇā, again into the Asī, and into the Varaṇā, / tormented by the fire of the three-eyed god, he wandered like a firebrand's circle.

16.s:
etasminnantare brahman ṛṣayo yakṣarākṣasāḥ /
nāgā vidyādharāścāpi pakṣiṇo 'psarasastathā //
16.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे ब्रह्मन् ऋषयो यक्षराक्षसाः ।
नागा विद्याधराश्चापि पक्षिणो ऽप्सरसस्तथा ॥
16.m: In the meantime, O Brahmin, the sages, yakṣas, rākṣasas, / nāgas, vidyādharas, birds, and apsarases,

16.s:
yāvanto bhāskararathe bhūtapretādayaḥ sthitāḥ /
tāvanto brahmasadanaṃ gatā vedayituṃ mune //
16.d:
यावन्तो भास्कररथे भूतप्रेतादयः स्थिताः ।
तावन्तो ब्रह्मसदनं गता वेदयितुं मुने ॥
16.m: as many bhūtas, pretas, and others as stood on the chariot of the sun, / all went to the abode of Brahmā to inform him, O sage.

16.s:
tato brahma surapatiḥ suraiḥ sārdha samabhyagātaṭ /
ramyaṃ maheśvarāvāsaṃ mandaraṃ ravikāraṇāt //
16.d:
ततो ब्रह्म सुरपतिः सुरैः सार्ध समभ्यगातट् ।
रम्यं महेश्वरावासं मन्दरं रविकारणात् ॥
16.m: Then Brahmā, along with the gods and the lord of the gods, went / to Mandara, the delightful abode of Maheśvara, on account of the sun.

16.s:
gatvā dṛṣṭvā ca deveśaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śūlapāṇinam /
prasādya bhāskarārthāya vārāṇasyāmupānayat //
16.d:
गत्वा दृष्ट्वा च देवेशं शङ्करं शूलपाणिनम् ।
प्रसाद्य भास्करार्थाय वाराणस्यामुपानयत् ॥
16.m: Having gone and seen the lord of gods, Śaṅkara, who holds the trident in his hand, / and having propitiated him on behalf of the sun, he brought him to Vārāṇasī.

16.s:
tato divākaraṃ bhūyaḥ pāṇinādāya śaṅkaraḥ /
kṛtvā nāmāsya loleti rathamāropayat punaḥ //
16.d:
ततो दिवाकरं भूयः पाणिनादाय शङ्करः ।
कृत्वा नामास्य लोलेति रथमारोपयत् पुनः ॥
16.m: Then Śaṅkara took the sun once more by the hand, / gave him the name Lola, and placed him back on his chariot.

16.s:
āropite dinakare brahmābhyetya sukeśinam /
sabāndhavaṃ sanagaraṃ punarāropayad divi //
16.d:
आरोपिते दिनकरे ब्रह्माभ्येत्य सुकेशिनम् ।
सबान्धवं सनगरं पुनरारोपयद् दिवि ॥
16.m: When the sun had been placed [on his chariot], Brahmā went to Sukeśin / and placed him back in the sky along with his relatives and his city.

16.s:
samāropya sukeśiṃ ca pariṣvajya ca śaṅkaram /
praṇamya keśavaṃ devaṃ vairājaṃ svagṛhaṃ gataḥ //
16.d:
समारोप्य सुकेशिं च परिष्वज्य च शङ्करम् ।
प्रणम्य केशवं देवं वैराजं स्वगृहं गतः ॥
16.m: Having re-established Sukeśin and embraced Śaṅkara, / and having bowed to the divine Keśava, he went to his own Vairāja abode.

16.s:
evaṃ purā nārada bhāskareṇa puraṃ sukeśerbhuvi sannipātitam /
divākaro bhūmitale bhavena kṣiptastu dṛṣṭyā na ca saṃpradagdhaḥ //
16.d:
एवं पुरा नारद भास्करेण पुरं सुकेशेर्भुवि सन्निपातितम् ।
दिवाकरो भूमितले भवेन क्षिप्तस्तु दृष्ट्या न च संप्रदग्धः ॥
16.m: Thus of old, O Nārada, the city of Sukeśin was cast down to earth by the sun; / but the sun, thrown down to the surface of the earth by Bhava with his gaze, was not consumed.

16.s:
āropito bhṛmitalād bhavena bhūyo 'pi bhānuḥ pratibhāsanāya /
svayaṃbhuvā cāpi niśācarendras tvāropitaḥ khe sapuraḥ sabandhuḥ //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
16.d:
आरोपितो भृमितलाद् भवेन भूयो ऽपि भानुः प्रतिभासनाय ।
स्वयंभुवा चापि निशाचरेन्द्रस् त्वारोपितः खे सपुरः सबन्धुः ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे षोडशो ऽध्यायः
16.m:
The sun was placed up from the earth again by Bhava in order to shine; / and by the Self-born one, the lord of night-wanderers was also raised to the sky with his city and relatives.

Thus ends the sixteenth chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

17.s:
nārada uvāca /
yānetān bhagavān prāha kāmibhiḥ śaśinaṃ prati /
ārādhanāya devābhyāṃ harīśābhyāṃ vadasva tān //
17.d:
नारद उवाच ।
यानेतान् भगवान् प्राह कामिभिः शशिनं प्रति ।
आराधनाय देवाभ्यां हरीशाभ्यां वदस्व तान् ॥
17.m: Nārada said: / "Those observances which your reverence mentioned, performed by lovers toward the moon / for the worship of the two gods Hari and Īśa—tell me about them."

17.s:
pulastya uvāca/ /
śṛṇuṣva kāmibhiḥ proktān vratān puṇyān kalipriya /
ārādhanāya śarvasya keśavasya ca dhīmataḥ //
17.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच। ।
शृणुष्व कामिभिः प्रोक्तान् व्रतान् पुण्यान् कलिप्रिय ।
आराधनाय शर्वस्य केशवस्य च धीमतः ॥
17.m: Pulastya said: / "Listen, O lover of strife, to the holy observances spoken of by lovers / for the propitiation of Śarva and the wise Keśava.

17.s:
yadā tvāṣāḍhī saṃyāti vrajate cottarāyaṇam /
tadā svapiti deveśo bhogibhoge śriyaḥ patiḥ //
17.d:
यदा त्वाषाढी संयाति व्रजते चोत्तरायणम् ।
तदा स्वपिति देवेशो भोगिभोगे श्रियः पतिः ॥
17.m: When the full moon of Āṣāḍha arrives and the northward course of the sun begins, / then the lord of the gods, the husband of Śrī, sleeps upon the coils of the serpent.

17.s:
pratisupte vibhau tasmin devagandharvaguhyakāḥ /
devānāṃ mātaraścāpi prasuptāścāpyanukramāt //
17.d:
प्रतिसुप्ते विभौ तस्मिन् देवगन्धर्वगुह्यकाः ।
देवानां मातरश्चापि प्रसुप्ताश्चाप्यनुक्रमात् ॥
17.m: When that all-pervading lord has gone to sleep, the gods, gandharvas, guhyakas, / and the mothers of the gods also fall asleep in succession.

17.s:
nārada uvāca/ /
kathayasva kurādīnāṃ śayane vidhimuttamam /
sarvamanukrameṇaiva puraskṛtya janārdanam //
17.d:
नारद उवाच। ।
कथयस्व कुरादीनां शयने विधिमुत्तमम् ।
सर्वमनुक्रमेणैव पुरस्कृत्य जनार्दनम् ॥
17.m:
Nārada said:
Tell [me] the supreme rule for the lying down of the gods and the others,
all in proper sequence, placing Janārdana first.

17.s:
pulastya uvāca /
mithunābhigate sūrye śuklapakṣe tapodhana /
ekādaśyāṃ jagatsvāmī śayanaṃ parikalpayet //
17.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
मिथुनाभिगते सूर्ये शुक्लपक्षे तपोधन ।
एकादश्यां जगत्स्वामी शयनं परिकल्पयेत् ॥
17.m:
Pulastya said:
When the sun enters Gemini, on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight, O rich in asceticism,
the Lord of the World should prepare his couch.

17.s:
śeṣāhibhogaparyaṅkaṃ kṛtvā saṃpūjya keśavam /
kṛtvopavītakaṃ caiva samyaksaṃpūjya vai dvijān //
17.d:
शेषाहिभोगपर्यङ्कं कृत्वा संपूज्य केशवम् ।
कृत्वोपवीतकं चैव सम्यक्संपूज्य वै द्विजान् ॥
17.m:
Having made a couch of the coils of the serpent Śeṣa and having worshipped Keśava,
and having made a sacred thread, and having properly honoured the twice-born,

17.s:
anujñānaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaśca dvādaśyāṃ prayataḥ śuciḥ /
labdhvā pītāmbaradharaḥ svasti nidrāṃ samānayet //
17.d:
अनुज्ञानं ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च द्वादश्यां प्रयतः शुचिः ।
लब्ध्वा पीताम्बरधरः स्वस्ति निद्रां समानयेत् ॥
17.m:
and having obtained permission from the Brahmins on the twelfth day, restrained and pure,
clad in yellow garments, he should bring on auspicious sleep.

17.s:
trayodaśyāṃ tataḥ kāmaḥ svapate śayane śubhe /
kadambānāṃ sugandhānāṃ kusumaiḥ parikalpite //
17.d:
त्रयोदश्यां ततः कामः स्वपते शयने शुभे ।
कदम्बानां सुगन्धानां कुसुमैः परिकल्पिते ॥
17.m:
Then, on the thirteenth day, Kāma sleeps on a beautiful bed
prepared with fragrant kadamba flowers.

17.s:
caturdaśyāṃ tato yakṣāḥ svapanti sukhaśītale /
sauvarṇapaṅkajakṛte sukhāstīrṇopadhānake //
17.d:
चतुर्दश्यां ततो यक्षाः स्वपन्ति सुखशीतले ।
सौवर्णपङ्कजकृते सुखास्तीर्णोपधानके ॥
17.m:
Then, on the fourteenth day, the Yakṣas sleep on a pleasantly cool [bed]
made of golden lotuses, with a comfortably spread pillow.

17.s:
paurmamāsyāmumānāthaḥ svapate carmasaṃstare /
vaiyāghre ca jaṭābhāraṃ samudgranthyānyacarmaṇā //
17.d:
पौर्ममास्यामुमानाथः स्वपते चर्मसंस्तरे ।
वैयाघ्रे च जटाभारं समुद्ग्रन्थ्यान्यचर्मणा ॥
17.m:
On the full-moon day, the Lord of Umā sleeps on a layer of skins,
[namely] a tiger skin, having bound his mass of matted hair with another skin.

17.s:
tato divākaro rāśiṃ saṃprayāti ca karkaṭam /
tato 'marāṇāṃ rajanī bhavate dakṣiṇāyanam //
17.d:
ततो दिवाकरो राशिं संप्रयाति च कर्कटम् ।
ततो ऽमराणां रजनी भवते दक्षिणायनम् ॥
17.m:
Then the sun enters the sign of Cancer;
thereupon begins the night of the immortals, the southern course [of the sun].

17.s:
brahmā pratipadi tathā nīlotpalamaye 'nagha /
talpe svapiti lokānāṃ darśayan mārgamuttamam //
17.d:
ब्रह्मा प्रतिपदि तथा नीलोत्पलमये ऽनघ ।
तल्पे स्वपिति लोकानां दर्शयन् मार्गमुत्तमम् ॥
17.m:
On the first lunar day Brahmā likewise, O sinless one,
sleeps on a bed made of blue lotuses, showing the supreme path to the worlds.

17.s:
viśvakarmā dvitīyāyāṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ gireḥ sutā /
vināyakaścurthyā tu pañcamyāmapi dharmarāṭ //
17.d:
विश्वकर्मा द्वितीयायां तृतीयायां गिरेः सुता ।
विनायकश्चुर्थ्या तु पञ्चम्यामपि धर्मराट् ॥
17.m:
Viśvakarman [sleeps] on the second day; the daughter of the mountain on the third;
Vināyaka on the fourth; and the King of Dharma on the fifth;

17.s:
ṣaṣṭhyāṃ skandaḥ prasvapiti saptamyāṃbhagavān raviḥ /
kātyāyanī tathāṣṭamyāṃ navamyāṃ kamalālayā //
17.d:
षष्ठ्यां स्कन्दः प्रस्वपिति सप्तम्यांभगवान् रविः ।
कात्यायनी तथाष्टम्यां नवम्यां कमलालया ॥
17.m:
Skanda falls asleep on the sixth; the blessed Sun on the seventh;
likewise Kātyāyanī on the eighth; the Lotus-dweller [Lakṣmī] on the ninth;

17.s:
daśamyāṃ bhujagendrāśca svapante vāyubhojanāḥ /
ekādaśyāṃ tu kṛṣṇāyāṃ sādhyā brahman svapanti ca //
17.d:
दशम्यां भुजगेन्द्राश्च स्वपन्ते वायुभोजनाः ।
एकादश्यां तु कृष्णायां साध्या ब्रह्मन् स्वपन्ति च ॥
17.m:
and the kings of serpents, who feed on air, sleep on the tenth;
and on the eleventh day of the dark fortnight, O Brahmin, the Sādhyas sleep.

17.s:
eṣa kramaste gadito nabhādau svapane mune /
svapatsu tatra deveṣu prāvṛṭkālaḥ samāyayau //
17.d:
एष क्रमस्ते गदितो नभादौ स्वपने मुने ।
स्वपत्सु तत्र देवेषु प्रावृट्कालः समाययौ ॥
17.m:
This order of sleeping has been told to you, beginning with [the month of] Nabhas, O sage;
while the gods were sleeping there, the rainy season arrived.

17.s:
kaṅkāḥ samaṃ balākābhirārohanti nagottamān /
vāyasāścāpi survanti nīḍāni ṛṣipuṅgava /
vāyasāśca svapantyete ṛtau garbhabharālasāḥ //
17.d:
कङ्काः समं बलाकाभिरारोहन्ति नगोत्तमान् ।
वायसाश्चापि सुर्वन्ति नीडानि ऋषिपुङ्गव ।
वायसाश्च स्वपन्त्येते ऋतौ गर्भभरालसाः ॥

17.s:
yasyāṃ tithyāṃ prasvapiti viśvakarmā prajāpatiḥ /
dvitīyā sā śubhā puṇyā aśūnyaśayanoditā //
17.d:
यस्यां तिथ्यां प्रस्वपिति विश्वकर्मा प्रजापतिः ।
द्वितीया सा शुभा पुण्या अशून्यशयनोदिता ॥
17.m:
The lunar day on which the creator Viśvakarman falls asleep—
that second day is auspicious, holy, and proclaimed as 'the un-empty couch' (aśūnyaśayana).

17.s:
tasyāṃ tithāvarcya hariṃ śrīvatsāṅkaṃ caturbhujam /
paryaṅkasthaṃ samaṃ lakṣmyā gandhapuṣpādibhirmune //
17.d:
तस्यां तिथावर्च्य हरिं श्रीवत्साङ्कं चतुर्भुजम् ।
पर्यङ्कस्थं समं लक्ष्म्या गन्धपुष्पादिभिर्मुने ॥
17.m:
Having worshipped Hari on that day—marked with the śrīvatsa, four-armed,
sitting on his couch together with Lakṣmī—with fragrant scents, flowers, and the like, O sage,

17.s:
tato devāya śayyāyāṃ phalāni prakṣipet kramāt /
surabhīṇī nivedyetthaṃ vijñāpyo madhusūdanaḥ //
17.d:
ततो देवाय शय्यायां फलानि प्रक्षिपेत् क्रमात् ।
सुरभीणी निवेद्येत्थं विज्ञाप्यो मधुसूदनः ॥
17.m:
one should then cast fruits one by one upon the bed for the god,
and, offering sweet-smelling [foods], Madhusūdana should thus be addressed:

17.s:
yathā hi lakṣmyā na viyujyase tvaṃ trivikramānanta jagannivāsa /
tathāstvaśūnyaṃ śayanaṃ sadaiva asmākameveha tava prasādāt //
17.d:
यथा हि लक्ष्म्या न वियुज्यसे त्वं त्रिविक्रमानन्त जगन्निवास ।
तथास्त्वशून्यं शयनं सदैव अस्माकमेवेह तव प्रसादात् ॥
17.m:
'Just as you are never separated from Lakṣmī, O Trivikrama, O Infinite One, O Abode of the Universe,
so let our couch always be un-empty here, through your grace.

17.s:
yathā tvaśūnyaṃ tava deva talpaṃ samaṃ hi lakṣmyā varadācyuteśa /
satyena tenāmitavīrya viṣṇo gārhasthyanāśo mama nāstu deva //
17.d:
यथा त्वशून्यं तव देव तल्पं समं हि लक्ष्म्या वरदाच्युतेश ।
सत्येन तेनामितवीर्य विष्णो गार्हस्थ्यनाशो मम नास्तु देव ॥
17.m:
Just as your bed, O god, is not empty, [shared] indeed with Lakṣmī, O giver of boons, O Acyuta, O Lord,
by that truth, O Viṣṇu of immeasurable valour, let there be no destruction of my householder's life, O god.'

17.s:
ityuccārya praṇamyeśaṃ prasādya ca punaḥ punaḥ /
naktāṃ bhuñjīta devarṣe tailakṣāravivarjitamaṭ //
17.d:
इत्युच्चार्य प्रणम्येशं प्रसाद्य च पुनः पुनः ।
नक्तां भुञ्जीत देवर्षे तैलक्षारविवर्जितमट् ॥
17.m:
Having spoken thus, having bowed to the Lord and having propitiated him again and again,
one should eat at night, O divine sage, free of oil and salt.

17.s:
dvitīye 'hni dvijāgryāya phalān dadyād vicakṣaṇaḥ /
lakṣmīdharaḥ prīyatāṃ me ityuccārya nivedayet //
17.d:
द्वितीये ऽह्नि द्विजाग्र्याय फलान् दद्याद् विचक्षणः ।
लक्ष्मीधरः प्रीयतां मे इत्युच्चार्य निवेदयेत् ॥
17.m:
On the second day, a wise person should give fruits to an eminent twice-born;
pronouncing 'May Lakṣmī's bearer be pleased with me', he should offer them.

17.s:
anena tu vidhānena cāturmāsyavrataṃ caret /
yāvad cavṛścikarāśisthaḥ pratibhāti divākaraḥ //
17.d:
अनेन तु विधानेन चातुर्मास्यव्रतं चरेत् ।
यावद् चवृश्चिकराशिस्थः प्रतिभाति दिवाकरः ॥
17.m:
According to this procedure one should perform the four-month observance,
as long as the sun shines situated in the sign of Scorpio.

17.s:
tato vibudhyanti surāḥ kramaśaḥ kramaśo mune /
tulāsther'ke hariḥ kāmaḥ śivaḥ paścādvibudhyate //
17.d:
ततो विबुध्यन्ति सुराः क्रमशः क्रमशो मुने ।
तुलास्थेर्ऽके हरिः कामः शिवः पश्चाद्विबुध्यते ॥
17.m:
Then the gods awaken one by one, O sage:
when the sun is in Libra, Hari [awakens], [then] Kāma, [and] Śiva awakens later.

17.s:
tatra dānaṃ dvitīyāyāṃ mūrttirlakṣmīdharasya tu /
saśayyāstaraṇopetā yathā vibhavamātmanaḥ //
17.d:
तत्र दानं द्वितीयायां मूर्त्तिर्लक्ष्मीधरस्य तु ।
सशय्यास्तरणोपेता यथा विभवमात्मनः ॥
17.m:
There, the gift on the second day is an image of the bearer of Lakṣmī,
provided with a bed and covering, according to one's own wealth.

17.s:
eṣa vratastu prathamaḥ proktastava mahāmune /
yasmiṃś cīrṇe viyogastu na bhavediha kasyacit //
17.d:
एष व्रतस्तु प्रथमः प्रोक्तस्तव महामुने ।
यस्मिंश् चीर्णे वियोगस्तु न भवेदिह कस्यचित् ॥
17.m:
This first observance has been declared to you, O great sage,
which, when performed, ensures that no separation will befall anyone here.

17.s:
nabhasye māsi ca tathā yā syātkṛṣṇāṣṭamī śubhā /
yuktā mṛgaśireṇaiva sā tu kālāṣṭamī smṛtā //
17.d:
नभस्ये मासि च तथा या स्यात्कृष्णाष्टमी शुभा ।
युक्ता मृगशिरेणैव सा तु कालाष्टमी स्मृता ॥
17.m:
And in the month of Nabhasya, that auspicious eighth day of the dark fortnight
conjoined with Mṛgaśiras is known as Kālāṣṭamī.

17.s:
tasyāṃ sarveṣu liṅgeṣu tithau svapiti śaṅkaraḥ /
vasate saṃnidhāne tu tatra pūjākṣayā smṛtā //
17.d:
तस्यां सर्वेषु लिङ्गेषु तिथौ स्वपिति शङ्करः ।
वसते संनिधाने तु तत्र पूजाक्षया स्मृता ॥
17.m:
On that lunar day, Śaṅkara sleeps in all liṅgas;
he resides in close proximity, and worship offered there is remembered as imperishable.

17.s:
tatra snāyīna vai vidvān gomūtreṇa jalena ca /
snātaḥ saṃpūjayet puṣpairdhattūrasya trilocanam //
17.d:
तत्र स्नायीन वै विद्वान् गोमूत्रेण जलेन च ।
स्नातः संपूजयेत् पुष्पैर्धत्तूरस्य त्रिलोचनम् ॥
17.m:
There the learned one should bathe with cow's urine and with water;
having bathed, he should worship the Three-Eyed One with flowers of dhattūra,

17.s:
dhūpaṃ kesaraniryāsaṃ naivedyaṃ madhusarpiṣī /
prīyatāṃ me virūpākṣastvityuccārya ca dakṣiṇām /
viprāya dadyānnaivedyaṃ sahiraṇyaṃ dvijottama //
17.d:
धूपं केसरनिर्यासं नैवेद्यं मधुसर्पिषी ।
प्रीयतां मे विरूपाक्षस्त्वित्युच्चार्य च दक्षिणाम् ।
विप्राय दद्यान्नैवेद्यं सहिरण्यं द्विजोत्तम ॥

17.s:
tadvadāśvayuje māsi upavāsī jitendriyaḥ /
navamyāṃ gomayasnānaṃ kuryātpūjāṃ tu paṅkajaiḥ /
dhūpayet sarjaniryāsaṃ naivedyaṃ madhumodakaiḥ //
17.d:
तद्वदाश्वयुजे मासि उपवासी जितेन्द्रियः ।
नवम्यां गोमयस्नानं कुर्यात्पूजां तु पङ्कजैः ।
धूपयेत् सर्जनिर्यासं नैवेद्यं मधुमोदकैः ॥

17.s:
kṛtopavāsastavaṣṭamyāṃ navamyāṃ snānamācaret /
prīyatāṃ me hiraṇyākṣo dakṣiṇā satilā smṛtā //
17.d:
कृतोपवासस्तवष्टम्यां नवम्यां स्नानमाचरेत् ।
प्रीयतां मे हिरण्याक्षो दक्षिणा सतिला स्मृता ॥
17.m:
Having fasted on the eighth, he should perform the bath on the ninth;
[saying] 'May the Golden-Eyed One be pleased with me'; the priestly gift is remembered to be with sesame.

17.s:
kārttike payasā snānaṃ karavīreṇa cārcanam /
dhupaṃ śrīvāsaniryāsaṃ naivedyaṃ madhupāyasam //
17.d:
कार्त्तिके पयसा स्नानं करवीरेण चार्चनम् ।
धुपं श्रीवासनिर्यासं नैवेद्यं मधुपायसम् ॥
17.m:
In Kārttika, bathing is with milk, and worship is with oleander;
incense is turpentine resin, and the food offering is milk-rice with honey.

17.s:
sanaivedyaṃ ca rajataṃ dātavyaṃ dānamagraje /
prīyatāṃ gavān sthāsuriti vācyamaniṣṭhuram //
17.d:
सनैवेद्यं च रजतं दातव्यं दानमग्रजे ।
प्रीयतां गवान् स्थासुरिति वाच्यमनिष्ठुरम् ॥
17.m:
And together with the food offering, silver should be given as a gift to an elder [Brahmin];
'May the enduring Lord be pleased' should be spoken gently.

17.s:
kṛtvopavāsamaṣṭamyāṃ navamyāṃ snānamācaret /
māsi mārgaśire snānaṃ dadhnārcā bhadrayā smṛtā //
17.d:
कृत्वोपवासमष्टम्यां नवम्यां स्नानमाचरेत् ।
मासि मार्गशिरे स्नानं दध्नार्चा भद्रया स्मृता ॥
17.m:
Having fasted on the eighth, he should perform the bath on the ninth;
in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, bathing is with curds, and worship is remembered [to be performed] with bhadrā;

17.s:
dhūpaṃ śrīvṛkṣaniryāsaṃ naivedyaṃ madhunodanam /
saṃnivedyā raktaśālirdakṣiṇā parikīrttitā /
namo 'stu prīyatāṃ śarvastviti vācyaṃ ca paṇḍitaiḥ //
17.d:
धूपं श्रीवृक्षनिर्यासं नैवेद्यं मधुनोदनम् ।
संनिवेद्या रक्तशालिर्दक्षिणा परिकीर्त्तिता ।
नमो ऽस्तु प्रीयतां शर्वस्त्विति वाच्यं च पण्डितैः ॥

17.s:
pauṣe snānaṃ ca haviṣā pūjā syāttagaraiḥ subhaiḥ /
dhūpo madhukaniryāso naivedyaṃ madhu śaṣkulī //
17.d:
पौषे स्नानं च हविषा पूजा स्यात्तगरैः सुभैः ।
धूपो मधुकनिर्यासो नैवेद्यं मधु शष्कुली ॥
17.m:
In Pauṣa, bathing should be with sacrificial butter, and worship with beautiful tagara flowers;
incense is madhuka resin, and the food offering is honeyed fried cake.

17.s:
samudgā dakṣiṇā proktā prīmanāya jagadguroḥ /
vācyaṃ namaste deveśa tryambaketi prakīrtayet //
17.d:
समुद्गा दक्षिणा प्रोक्ता प्रीमनाय जगद्गुरोः ।
वाच्यं नमस्ते देवेश त्र्यम्बकेति प्रकीर्तयेत् ॥
17.m:
A priestly gift accompanied by mung beans is declared for the pleasing of the Teacher of the World;
one should recite, 'Homage to you, O Lord of the gods, O Tryambaka!'

17.s:
māghe kuśodakasnānaṃ mṛgamadena cārcyanam /
dhūpaḥ padambaniryāso naivedyaṃ satilodanam //
17.d:
माघे कुशोदकस्नानं मृगमदेन चार्च्यनम् ।
धूपः पदम्बनिर्यासो नैवेद्यं सतिलोदनम् ॥
17.m:
In Māgha, bathing is with kuśa grass water, and worship is with musk;
incense is kadamba resin, and the food offering is boiled rice with sesame.

17.s:
payobhaktaṃ sanaivedyaṃ sarukmaṃ pratipādayet /
prīyatāṃ me mahādeva umāpatiritīrayet //
17.d:
पयोभक्तं सनैवेद्यं सरुक्मं प्रतिपादयेत् ।
प्रीयतां मे महादेव उमापतिरितीरयेत् ॥
17.m:
One should present boiled rice with milk together with the food offering and with gold;
one should utter: 'May the Great God, the Lord of Umā, be pleased with me.'

17.s:
evameva samuddiṣṭaṃ ṣaḍbhirmāsaistu pāraṇam /
pāraṇānte trinetrasya snapanaṃ kārayetkramāt //
17.d:
एवमेव समुद्दिष्टं षड्भिर्मासैस्तु पारणम् ।
पारणान्ते त्रिनेत्रस्य स्नपनं कारयेत्क्रमात् ॥
17.m:
In this very way, the breaking of the fast through six months has been stated;
at the conclusion of the fast-breaking, he should successively perform the bath of the Three-Eyed One.

17.s:
gorocanāyāḥ sahitā guḍena devaṃ samālabhya ca pūjayeta /
prīyasva dīno 'smi bhavantamīśa macchokanāśaṃ prakuruṣva yogyam //
17.d:
गोरोचनायाः सहिता गुडेन देवं समालभ्य च पूजयेत ।
प्रीयस्व दीनो ऽस्मि भवन्तमीश मच्छोकनाशं प्रकुरुष्व योग्यम् ॥
17.m:
Having anointed the god with gorocanā together with molasses, he should worship [him]:
'Be pleased, O Lord; I am afflicted; do you bring about the proper destruction of my sorrow!'

17.s:
tatastu phālgune māsiṃ kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ yatavrata /
upavāsaṃ samudītaṃ kartavyaṃ dvijasattama //
17.d:
ततस्तु फाल्गुने मासिं कृष्णाष्टम्यां यतव्रत ।
उपवासं समुदीतं कर्तव्यं द्विजसत्तम ॥
17.m:
Then in the month of Phālguna, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, O one of observed vows,
the fast proclaimed should be observed, O best of the twice-born.

17.s:
dvitīye 'hni tataḥ snānaṃ pañcagavyena kārayet /
pūjayetkundakusumairdhūpayet candanaṃ tvapi //
17.d:
द्वितीये ऽह्नि ततः स्नानं पञ्चगव्येन कारयेत् ।
पूजयेत्कुन्दकुसुमैर्धूपयेत् चन्दनं त्वपि ॥
17.m:
Then on the second day, he should perform the bath with the five products of the cow;
he should worship with kunda blossoms and also burn incense of sandalwood.

17.s:
naivedyaṃ saghṛtaṃ dadyāt tāmrapātre guḍodanam /
dakṣiṇāṃ ca dvijātibhyo naivedyasahitāṃ mune /
vāsoyugaṃ prīṇayecca rudramuccārya nāmataḥ //
17.d:
नैवेद्यं सघृतं दद्यात् ताम्रपात्रे गुडोदनम् ।
दक्षिणां च द्विजातिभ्यो नैवेद्यसहितां मुने ।
वासोयुगं प्रीणयेच्च रुद्रमुच्चार्य नामतः ॥

17.s:
caitre codumbaraphalaiḥ snānaṃ mandārakārcanam /
gugguluṃ mahiṣākhyaṃ ca ghṛtāktaṃ dhūpayed budhaḥ //
17.d:
चैत्रे चोदुम्बरफलैः स्नानं मन्दारकार्चनम् ।
गुग्गुलुं महिषाख्यं च घृताक्तं धूपयेद् बुधः ॥
17.m: In Caitra, a wise man should bathe with cluster fig fruits and worship with mandāra flowers, / and burn as incense mahiṣa-guggulu mixed with ghee.

17.s:
samodakaṃ tathā sarpiḥ prīṇanaṃ vinivedayet /
dakṣiṇā ca sanaivedyaṃ sṛgājinamudāhṛtam //
17.d:
समोदकं तथा सर्पिः प्रीणनं विनिवेदयेत् ।
दक्षिणा च सनैवेद्यं सृगाजिनमुदाहृतम् ॥
17.m: He should offer ghee along with water for propitiation, / and the priestly fee along with food-offerings is declared to be a deer-skin.

17.s:
nāṭyeśvara namaste 'stu idamuccārya nārada /
prīṇanaṃ devanāthāya kuryācchraddhāsamanvitaḥ //
17.d:
नाट्येश्वर नमस्ते ऽस्तु इदमुच्चार्य नारद ।
प्रीणनं देवनाथाय कुर्याच्छ्रद्धासमन्वितः ॥
17.m: Saying, ‘O Nāṭyeśvara, reverence to you!’, O Nārada, / endowed with faith, he should make the propitiation to the lord of the gods.

17.s:
vaiśākhe snānamuditaṃ sugandhakusumāmbhasā /
pūjanaṃ śaṅkarasyoktaṃ cūtamañjaribhirvibho //
17.d:
वैशाखे स्नानमुदितं सुगन्धकुसुमाम्भसा ।
पूजनं शङ्करस्योक्तं चूतमञ्जरिभिर्विभो ॥
17.m: In Vaiśākha, bathing with fragrant flower-water is prescribed; / the worship of Śaṅkara, O powerful one, is said to be with mango blossoms.

17.s:
dhūpaṃ sarjājyayuktaṃ ca naivedyaṃ saphalaṃ ghṛtam /
nāmajapyamapīśasya kālaghneti vipaścitā //
17.d:
धूपं सर्जाज्ययुक्तं च नैवेद्यं सफलं घृतम् ।
नामजप्यमपीशस्य कालघ्नेति विपश्चिता ॥
17.m: Incense mixed with sal resin and ghee, food-offerings with fruit and ghee, / and the name ‘Kālaghna’ of the Lord should be recited by the discerning one.

17.s:
jalakumbhān sanaivedyān brāhmaṇāya nivedayet /
sopavītān sahānnādyāṃstaccittaistatparāyaṇaiḥ //
17.d:
जलकुम्भान् सनैवेद्यान् ब्राह्मणाय निवेदयेत् ।
सोपवीतान् सहान्नाद्यांस्तच्चित्तैस्तत्परायणैः ॥
17.m: He should present water-pitchers along with food-offerings to a Brahmin, / accompanied by sacred threads and staple foods, their minds fixed on him, devoted to him.

17.s:
jyeṣṭhe snānaṃ cāmalakaiḥ pūjār'kakusumaistathā /
dhūpayettattrinetraṃ ca āyatyāṃ puṣṭikārakam //
17.d:
ज्येष्ठे स्नानं चामलकैः पूजार्ऽककुसुमैस्तथा ।
धूपयेत्तत्त्रिनेत्रं च आयत्यां पुष्टिकारकम् ॥
17.m: In Jyeṣṭha, bathing is with emblic myrobalans, and worship with arka blossoms; / he should fumigate the Three-eyed One with that which brings prosperity in the future.

17.s:
saktūṃśca saghṛtān deve dadhnāktān vinivedayet /
upānadyagalaṃ chatraṃ dānaṃ dadyācca bhaktimān //
17.d:
सक्तूंश्च सघृतान् देवे दध्नाक्तान् विनिवेदयेत् ।
उपानद्यगलं छत्रं दानं दद्याच्च भक्तिमान् ॥
17.m: He should present to the god roasted barley-meal with ghee and smeared with curd; / and full of devotion, he should give a pair of sandals and an umbrella as a gift.

17.s:
namaste bhaganetraghna pūṣṇo daśananāśana /
idamuccārayedbhaktyā prīṇanāya jagatpateḥ //
17.d:
नमस्ते भगनेत्रघ्न पूष्णो दशननाशन ।
इदमुच्चारयेद्भक्त्या प्रीणनाय जगत्पतेः ॥
17.m: ‘Reverence to you, O destroyer of Bhaga’s eyes, O destroyer of Pūṣan’s teeth!’ / He should recite this with devotion for the propitiation of the Lord of the universe.

17.s:
āṣāḍhe snānamuditaṃ śrīphalairarcanaṃ tathā /
dhattūrakusumaiḥ śuklairdhūpayet silhakaṃ tathā //
17.d:
आषाढे स्नानमुदितं श्रीफलैरर्चनं तथा ।
धत्तूरकुसुमैः शुक्लैर्धूपयेत् सिल्हकं तथा ॥
17.m: In Āṣāḍha, bathing is prescribed with bilva fruits, and likewise worship / with white dhattūra flowers; he should also burn olibanum as incense.

17.s:
naivedyāḥ saghṛtāḥ pūpāḥ dakṣiṇā saghṛtā yavāḥ /
namaste dakṣayajñaghna idamuccairudīrayet //
17.d:
नैवेद्याः सघृताः पूपाः दक्षिणा सघृता यवाः ।
नमस्ते दक्षयज्ञघ्न इदमुच्चैरुदीरयेत् ॥
17.m: The food-offerings are sweet cakes with ghee, the priestly fee is barley with ghee. / He should loudly proclaim: ‘Reverence to you, O destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice!’

17.s:
śrāvaṇe mṛgabhojyena snānaṃ kṛtvār'cayeddharam /
śrīvṛkṣapatraḥ saphalairdhūpaṃ dadyāt tathāgurum //
17.d:
श्रावणे मृगभोज्येन स्नानं कृत्वार्ऽचयेद्धरम् ।
श्रीवृक्षपत्रः सफलैर्धूपं दद्यात् तथागुरुम् ॥
17.m: In Śrāvaṇa, having bathed with wild rice, he should worship Hara; / with bilva leaves and fruits, and he should offer agallochum as incense.

17.s:
naivedyaṃ saghṛtaṃ dadyāt dadhi pūpān samodakān /
dadhyodanaṃ sakṛsaraṃ māṣadhānāḥ saśaṣkulīḥ //
17.d:
नैवेद्यं सघृतं दद्यात् दधि पूपान् समोदकान् ।
दध्योदनं सकृसरं माषधानाः सशष्कुलीः ॥
17.m: He should offer food with ghee: curd, sweet cakes together with modakas, / curd-rice mixed with kṛsara, parched black grams, and large cakes.

17.s:
dakṣiṇāṃ śvetavṛṣabhaṃ dhenuṃ ca kapilāṃ śubhām /
kanakaṃ rakkavasanaṃ pradadyād brāhmaṇāya hi /
gaṅgādhareti japtavyaṃ nāma śaṃbhośca paṇḍitaiḥ //
17.d:
दक्षिणां श्वेतवृषभं धेनुं च कपिलां शुभाम् ।
कनकं रक्कवसनं प्रदद्याद् ब्राह्मणाय हि ।
गङ्गाधरेति जप्तव्यं नाम शंभोश्च पण्डितैः ॥
17.m: As a priestly fee, he should give to a Brahmin a white bull, an auspicious tawny cow, / gold, and a dyed garment; / and the learned should repeat the name of Śambhu: ‘Gaṅgādhara’.

17.s:
amībhiḥ ṣaḍbhiraparairmāsaiḥ pāraṇamuttamam /
evaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ saṃpūjya ṣabhadhvajam /
akṣayān labhate kāmān maheśvaravaco yathā //
17.d:
अमीभिः षड्भिरपरैर्मासैः पारणमुत्तमम् ।
एवं संवत्सरं पूर्णं संपूज्य षभध्वजम् ।
अक्षयान् लभते कामान् महेश्वरवचो यथा ॥
17.m: With these six other months, the breaking of the fast is supreme; / thus having worshipped the Bull-bannered One for a full year, / one obtains imperishable desires, in accordance with Maheśvara’s word.

17.s:
idamuktaṃ vrataṃ puṇyaṃ sarvākṣayakaraṃ śubham /
svayaṃ rudraṇa devarṣe tattathā na tadanyathā //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
17.d:
इदमुक्तं व्रतं पुण्यं सर्वाक्षयकरं शुभम् ।
स्वयं रुद्रण देवर्षे तत्तथा न तदन्यथा ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे सप्तदशो ऽध्यायः
17.m:
This holy, auspicious observance, yielding imperishable reward in all things, / was spoken by Rudra himself, O divine seer; it is just so, and not otherwise.

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter in the glorious Vāmanapurāṇa.

18.s:
pulastya uvāca /
māsi cāśvayuje brahman yadā padmaṃ jagatpateḥ /
nābhyā niryāti hi tadā deveṣvetānyatho 'bhavan //
18.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
मासि चाश्वयुजे ब्रह्मन् यदा पद्मं जगत्पतेः ।
नाभ्या निर्याति हि तदा देवेष्वेतान्यथो ऽभवन् ॥
18.m: Pulastya said: / In the month of Āśvina, O Brahmin, when the lotus / issued from the navel of the Lord of the universe, then among the gods these [trees] came into being.

18.s:
kandarpasya karāgre tu kadambaścārudarśanaḥ /
tena tasya parā prītiḥ kadambena vivarddhate //
18.d:
कन्दर्पस्य कराग्रे तु कदम्बश्चारुदर्शनः ।
तेन तस्य परा प्रीतिः कदम्बेन विवर्द्धते ॥
18.m: At the tip of Kandarpa’s hand was the lovely kadamba; / because of it, his supreme delight increases through the kadamba.

18.s:
yakṣāṇāmadhipasyāpi maṇibhadrasya nārada /
vaṭavṛkṣaḥ samabhavat tasmistasya yatiḥ sadā //
18.d:
यक्षाणामधिपस्यापि मणिभद्रस्य नारद ।
वटवृक्षः समभवत् तस्मिस्तस्य यतिः सदा ॥
18.m: For Maṇibhadra, the lord of the yakṣas, O Nārada, / the banyan tree arose; in it is his constant delight.

18.s:
maheśvarasya hṛdaye dhattūraviṭapaḥ śubhaḥ /
saṃjātaḥ sa ca śarvasya patikṛt tasya nityaśaḥ //
18.d:
महेश्वरस्य हृदये धत्तूरविटपः शुभः ।
संजातः स च शर्वस्य पतिकृत् तस्य नित्यशः ॥
18.m: In the heart of Maheśvara, the auspicious dhattūra shrub / sprang up; and it constantly pleases Śarva.

18.s:
brahmaṇo madhyato dehāñjāto marakataprabhaḥ /
kha daraḥ kaṇṭakī śreyānabhavadviśvakarmaṇaḥ //
18.d:
ब्रह्मणो मध्यतो देहाञ्जातो मरकतप्रभः ।
ख दरः कण्टकी श्रेयानभवद्विश्वकर्मणः ॥
18.m: From the middle of Brahmā’s body sprang the acacia, shining like emerald; / the thorny, auspicious [tree] belonged to Viśvakarman.

18.s:
girijāyāḥ karatale kundasulmastvajāyata /
gaṇādhipasya kumbhastho rājate sindhuvārakaḥ //
18.d:
गिरिजायाः करतले कुन्दसुल्मस्त्वजायत ।
गणाधिपस्य कुम्भस्थो राजते सिन्धुवारकः ॥
18.m: In the palm of Girijā’s hand, a kunda bush was born; / the sindhuvāraka tree shines on the brow of the Lord of Gaṇas.

18.s:
yamasya kṣiṇe pārśve pālāśo dakṣiṇottare /
kṛṣṇodumbarako rudrājjātaḥ kṣomakaro vṛṣaḥ //
18.d:
यमस्य क्षिणे पार्श्वे पालाशो दक्षिणोत्तरे ।
कृष्णोदुम्बरको रुद्राज्जातः क्षोमकरो वृषः ॥
18.m: On Yama’s right side arose the palāśa, on the north-east [another]; / from Rudra arose the black cluster fig, the bull that brings delight.

18.s:
skandasya bandhujīvastu raveraśvattha eva ca /
kātyāyanayāḥ śamījātābilvo lakṣmāyāḥ kare 'bhavat //
18.d:
स्कन्दस्य बन्धुजीवस्तु रवेरश्वत्थ एव च ।
कात्यायनयाः शमीजाताबिल्वो लक्ष्मायाः करे ऽभवत् ॥
18.m: The bandhujīva belonged to Skanda, and the aśvattha to the Sun; / the śamī was born of Kātyāyanī, and the bilva arose in the hand of Lakṣmī.

18.s:
nāgānāṃ pataye brahmañcharastambo vyajāyata /
vāsukervistṛte pucche pṛṣṭhe dūrvā sitāsitā //
18.d:
नागानां पतये ब्रह्मञ्छरस्तम्बो व्यजायत ।
वासुकेर्विस्तृते पुच्छे पृष्ठे दूर्वा सितासिता ॥
18.m: For the lord of serpents, O Brahmin, a reed clump was born; / on Vāsuki’s broad tail and on his back grew white and dark dūrvā grass.

18.s:
sādhyānāṃ hṛdaye jāto vṛkṣo haritacandanaḥ /
evaṃ jāteṣu sarveṣu tena tat ratirbhavet //
18.d:
साध्यानां हृदये जातो वृक्षो हरितचन्दनः ।
एवं जातेषु सर्वेषु तेन तत् रतिर्भवेत् ॥
18.m: In the heart of the Sādhyas was born the green sandalwood tree; / when all these had arisen in this way, there would be delight through each.

18.s:
tatra ramye śubhe kāle yā śuklaikādaśī bhavet /
tasyāṃ saṃpūjayed viṣṇuṃ tena khaṇḍo 'sya pūryate //
18.d:
तत्र रम्ये शुभे काले या शुक्लैकादशी भवेत् ।
तस्यां संपूजयेद् विष्णुं तेन खण्डो ऽस्य पूर्यते ॥
18.m: At that charming, auspicious time, on whichever bright eleventh lunar day it falls, / he should worship Viṣṇu on it; thereby his deficiency is made whole.

18.s:
puṣṣaiḥ putraiḥ phalairvāpi gandhavarṇarasnvitaiḥ /
oṣadhībhiśca mukhyābhiryāvatsyāccharadāgamaḥ //
18.d:
पुष्षैः पुत्रैः फलैर्वापि गन्धवर्णरस्न्वितैः ।
ओषधीभिश्च मुख्याभिर्यावत्स्याच्छरदागमः ॥
18.m: With flowers, leaves, or fruits endowed with fragrance, color, and taste, / and with the foremost medicinal herbs, until the arrival of autumn,

18.s:
ghṛtaṃ tilā brīhiyavā hiraṇyakankādi yat /
maṇimuktāpravālāni vastrāṇi vividhāni ca //
18.d:
घृतं तिला ब्रीहियवा हिरण्यकन्कादि यत् ।
मणिमुक्ताप्रवालानि वस्त्राणि विविधानि च ॥
18.m: ghee, sesame, rice, barley, gold, ornaments, and so forth, / jewels, pearls, corals, and diverse garments,

18.s:
rasāni svādukaṭvamlakaṣāyalavaṇāni ca /
tiktāni ca nivedyāni tānyakhaṇḍāni yāni hi //
18.d:
रसानि स्वादुकट्वम्लकषायलवणानि च ।
तिक्तानि च निवेद्यानि तान्यखण्डानि यानि हि ॥
18.m: tastes—sweet, pungent, sour, astringent, salty, / and bitter—whatever whole [articles] are to be offered,

18.s:
tatpūjārthaṃ pradātavyaṃ keśavāya mahātmane /
yadā saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇamakhaṇḍaṃ bhavate gṛhe //
18.d:
तत्पूजार्थं प्रदातव्यं केशवाय महात्मने ।
यदा संवत्सरं पूर्णमखण्डं भवते गृहे ॥
18.m: should be presented for his worship to the great-souled Keśava, / so that a full year in the house becomes complete and unbroken.

18.s:
kṛtopavāso devarṣe dvitīye 'hani saṃyataḥ /
snānena tena snāyīta yenākhaṇḍaṃ hi vatsaram //
18.d:
कृतोपवासो देवर्षे द्वितीये ऽहनि संयतः ।
स्नानेन तेन स्नायीत येनाखण्डं हि वत्सरम् ॥
18.m: Having observed a fast, O divine seer, restrained on the second day, / he should bathe with that bath by which the year indeed becomes unbroken.

18.s:
siddhārtakaistilairvāpi tenaivodvartanaṃ smṛtam /
haviṣā padmanābhasya snānameva samācaret /
home tadeva gaditaṃ dāne śaktirnijā dvija //
18.d:
सिद्धार्तकैस्तिलैर्वापि तेनैवोद्वर्तनं स्मृतम् ।
हविषा पद्मनाभस्य स्नानमेव समाचरेत् ।
होमे तदेव गदितं दाने शक्तिर्निजा द्विज ॥
18.m: Anointing is prescribed with white mustard or sesame seeds; / he should perform the bath of Padmanābha with clarified butter; / in the oblation, that very thing is declared; in giving, one’s own capacity [is the rule], O twice-born.

18.s:
pūjayetātha kusumaiḥ pādādārabhya keśavam /
dhūpayed vividhaṃ dhūpaṃ yena syād vatsaraṃ param //
18.d:
पूजयेताथ कुसुमैः पादादारभ्य केशवम् ।
धूपयेद् विविधं धूपं येन स्याद् वत्सरं परम् ॥
18.m: He should then worship Keśava with flowers beginning from the feet; / he should burn various incense, so that the year may be supreme.

18.s:
hiraṇyaratnavāsobhiḥ pūjayeta jagad gurum /
rāgakhāṇḍavacoṣyāṇi haviṣyāṇi nivedayet //
18.d:
हिरण्यरत्नवासोभिः पूजयेत जगद् गुरुम् ।
रागखाण्डवचोष्याणि हविष्याणि निवेदयेत् ॥
18.m: He should worship the Guru of the universe with gold, gems, and garments; / he should offer spiced condiments, suckable foods, and sacrificial fare.

18.s:
tataḥ saṃpūjya deveśaṃ padmanābhaṃ jagad gurum /
vijñāpayenmuniśreṣṭha mantreṇānena suvrata //
18.d:
ततः संपूज्य देवेशं पद्मनाभं जगद् गुरुम् ।
विज्ञापयेन्मुनिश्रेष्ठ मन्त्रेणानेन सुव्रत ॥
18.m: Then, having worshipped the Lord of gods, Padmanābha, the Guru of the universe, / he should make request, O best of sages, with this mantra, O one of good vows:

18.s:
namo 'stu te padmanābha padmādhava mahādyute /
dharmārthakāmamokṣaṇi tvakhaṇḍāni bhavantu me //
18.d:
नमो ऽस्तु ते पद्मनाभ पद्माधव महाद्युते ।
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षणि त्वखण्डानि भवन्तु मे ॥
18.m: ‘Reverence be to you, O Padmanābha, O Padmādhava, O one of great splendor! / May righteousness, wealth, desire, and liberation be unbroken for me!

18.s:
vikāsipadmapatrākṣa yathākhaṇḍosi sarvataḥ /
tena satyena dharmādya akhaṇḍāḥ santu keśava //
18.d:
विकासिपद्मपत्राक्ष यथाखण्डोसि सर्वतः ।
तेन सत्येन धर्माद्य अखण्डाः सन्तु केशव ॥
18.m: O one whose eyes are like blossoming lotus leaves, just as you are unbroken in all ways, / by that truth, may righteousness and the rest be unbroken, O Keśava!’

18.s:
evaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ sopavāso jitendriyaḥ /
aghaṇḍaṃ pārayed brahman vrataṃ vai sarvavastuṣu //
18.d:
एवं संवत्सरं पूर्णं सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः ।
अघण्डं पारयेद् ब्रह्मन् व्रतं वै सर्ववस्तुषु ॥
18.m: Fastened thus for a full year, with subdued senses, / he should complete the unbroken observance in all things, O Brahmin.

18.s:
asmiṃścīrṇe vrataṃ vyaktaṃ parituṣyanti devatāḥ /
dharmārthakāmamokṣādyāstvakṣayāḥ saṃbhavanti hi //
18.d:
अस्मिंश्चीर्णे व्रतं व्यक्तं परितुष्यन्ति देवताः ।
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाद्यास्त्वक्षयाः संभवन्ति हि ॥
18.m: When this observance has been performed, clearly the deities are thoroughly pleased; / righteousness, wealth, desire, and liberation indeed become imperishable.

18.s:
etāni te mayoktāni vratānyuktāni kāmibhiḥ /
prakṣyāmyadhunā tvetadvaiṣṇavaṃ pañjaraṃ śubham //
18.d:
एतानि ते मयोक्तानि व्रतान्युक्तानि कामिभिः ।
प्रक्ष्याम्यधुना त्वेतद्वैष्णवं पञ्जरं शुभम् ॥
18.m: These observances desired by seekers have been told to you by me; / I shall now declare to you this auspicious armor of Viṣṇu.

18.s:
namo namaste govinda cakraṃ gṛhya sudarśanam /
prācyāṃ rakṣasva māṃ viṣṇo tvāmāhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
18.d:
नमो नमस्ते गोविन्द चक्रं गृह्य सुदर्शनम् ।
प्राच्यां रक्षस्व मां विष्णो त्वामाहं शरणं गतः ॥
18.m: ‘Reverence, reverence to you, O Govinda! Taking up the Sudarśana discus, / protect me in the east, O Viṣṇu! I have gone to you for refuge!

18.s:
gadāṃ kaumodakīṃ gṛhya padmanābhāmitadyute /
yāmyāṃ rakṣasva māṃ viṣṇo tvamāhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
18.d:
गदां कौमोदकीं गृह्य पद्मनाभामितद्युते ।
याम्यां रक्षस्व मां विष्णो त्वमाहं शरणं गतः ॥
18.m: Taking up the Kaumodakī mace, O Padmanābha of boundless splendor, / protect me in the south, O Viṣṇu! I have gone to you for refuge!

18.s:
halamādāya saunandaṃ namaste puraṣottama /
pratīcyāṃ rakṣa me viṣṇo bhavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
18.d:
हलमादाय सौनन्दं नमस्ते पुरषोत्तम ।
प्रतीच्यां रक्ष मे विष्णो भवन्तं शरणं गतः ॥
18.m: Taking up the plough Saunanda, reverence to you, O Puruṣottama! / Protect me in the west, O Viṣṇu! I have gone to you for refuge!

18.s:
musalaṃ śātanaṃ gṛhya puṇḍarīkākṣa rakṣa māma /
uttarasyāṃ jagannātha bhavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
18.d:
मुसलं शातनं गृह्य पुण्डरीकाक्ष रक्ष माम ।
उत्तरस्यां जगन्नाथ भवन्तं शरणं गतः ॥
18.m: Taking up the pestle Śātana, O Lotus-eyed One, protect me! / In the north, O Lord of the universe, I have gone to you for refuge!’

18.s:
śārṅgamādāya ca dhanurastraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ hare /
namaste rakṣa rakṣaghna aiśānyāṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
18.d:
शार्ङ्गमादाय च धनुरस्त्रं नारायणं हरे ।
नमस्ते रक्ष रक्षघ्न ऐशान्यां शरणं गतः ॥
18.m: Taking the Śārṅga bow and the missile Nārāyaṇa, O Hari, / homage to you; protect [me], O destroyer of monsters! In the northeast I have gone to [you for] refuge.

18.s:
pāñcajanyaṃ mahāśaṅkhamantarbodhyaṃ ca paṅkajam /
pragṛhay rakṣa māṃ viṣṇo āgneyyāṃ yajñasūkara //
18.d:
पाञ्चजन्यं महाशङ्खमन्तर्बोध्यं च पङ्कजम् ।
प्रगृहय् रक्ष मां विष्णो आग्नेय्यां यज्ञसूकर ॥
18.m: Taking the Pāñcajanya, the great conch, and the lotus that opens from within, / protect me in the southeast, O Viṣṇu, O sacrificial boar!

18.s:
carma sūryaśataṃ gṛhya khaṅgaṃ candramasaṃ tathā /
nairṛtyāṃ māṃ ca rakṣasva divyamūrte nṛkesarin //
18.d:
चर्म सूर्यशतं गृह्य खङ्गं चन्द्रमसं तथा ।
नैरृत्यां मां च रक्षस्व दिव्यमूर्ते नृकेसरिन् ॥
18.m: Taking the shield shining like a hundred suns and the sword brilliant as the moon, / protect me in the southwest, O deity of divine form, O man-lion!

18.s:
vaijayantīṃ pragṛhya tvaṃ śrīvatsaṃ kaṇṭhabhūṣaṇam /
vāyavyāṃ rakṣa māṃ deva aśvaśīrṣa namo 'stu te //
18.d:
वैजयन्तीं प्रगृह्य त्वं श्रीवत्सं कण्ठभूषणम् ।
वायव्यां रक्ष मां देव अश्वशीर्ष नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
18.m: Bearing the Vaijayantī [garland] and the Śrīvatsa on your neck, / protect me in the northwest, O god, O horse-headed one; homage be to you!

18.s:
vainateyaṃ samāruhya antarikṣe janārdana /
māṃ tvaṃ rakṣājita sadā namaste tvaparājati //
18.d:
वैनतेयं समारुह्य अन्तरिक्षे जनार्दन ।
मां त्वं रक्षाजित सदा नमस्ते त्वपराजति ॥
18.m: Mounting the son of Vinatā in the sky, O Janārdana, / protect me always, O unconquered one; homage to you, O undefeated one!

18.s:
viśālākṣaṃ samāruhya rakṣa māṃ tvaṃ rasātale /
akūpāra namastubhyaṃ mahāmoha namo 'stu te //
18.d:
विशालाक्षं समारुह्य रक्ष मां त्वं रसातले ।
अकूपार नमस्तुभ्यं महामोह नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
18.m: Mounting Viśālākṣa, protect me in Rasātala; / homage to you, O tortoise; homage be to you, O great delusion!

18.s:
karaśīrṣāṅghrarveṣu tathāṣṭabāhupañjaram /
kṛtvā rakṣasva māṃ deva namaste puruṣottama //
18.d:
करशीर्षाङ्घ्रर्वेषु तथाष्टबाहुपञ्जरम् ।
कृत्वा रक्षस्व मां देव नमस्ते पुरुषोत्तम ॥
18.m: Having made an armor of eight arms over my hands, head, and feet, / protect me, O god; homage to you, O supreme spirit!

18.s:
etaduktaṃ bhagavatā vaiṣṇavaṃ pañjaraṃ mahat /
purā rakṣārthamīśena kātyāyanyā dvijottama //
18.d:
एतदुक्तं भगवता वैष्णवं पञ्जरं महत् ।
पुरा रक्षार्थमीशेन कात्यायन्या द्विजोत्तम ॥
18.m: This great armor of Viṣṇu was spoken by the Lord / in ancient times to Kātyāyanī for the sake of protection, O best of the twice-born,

18.s:
nāśayāmāsa sā yatra dānavaṃ mahiṣāsuram /
namaraṃ raktabījaṃ ca tathānyān surakaṇṭakān //
18.d:
नाशयामास सा यत्र दानवं महिषासुरम् ।
नमरं रक्तबीजं च तथान्यान् सुरकण्टकान् ॥
18.m: where she destroyed the Dānava Mahiṣāsura, / Namara, Raktabīja, and other thorns to the gods.

18.s:
nārada uvāca /
kāsau kātyāyānī nāma yacā jaghne mahiṣāsuram /
namaraṃ raktabījaṃ ca tathānyān kurakaṇṭakān //
18.d:
नारद उवाच ।
कासौ कात्यायानी नाम यचा जघ्ने महिषासुरम् ।
नमरं रक्तबीजं च तथान्यान् कुरकण्टकान् ॥
18.m: Nārada said: / Who is this one named Kātyāyanī, who slew Mahiṣāsura, / Namara, Raktabīja, and other thorns to the gods?

18.s:
kaścasau mahiṣo nāma kule jātaśca kasya saḥ /
kaścāsau raktabījākhyo namaraḥ kasya cātmajaḥ /
etadvistaratastāta yathāvad vaktumarhasiḥ //
18.d:
कश्चसौ महिषो नाम कुले जातश्च कस्य सः ।
कश्चासौ रक्तबीजाख्यो नमरः कस्य चात्मजः ।
एतद्विस्तरतस्तात यथावद् वक्तुमर्हसिः ॥
18.m: And who is this named Mahiṣa, and in whose family was he born? / And who is this named Raktabīja, and whose son was Namara? / You ought to tell this in full, dear friend, just as it happened.

18.s:
pulastya uvāca/ /
śrūyatāṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm /
sarvadā varadā durgā yeyaṃ kātyāyanī mune //
18.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच। ।
श्रूयतां संप्रवक्ष्यामि कथां पापप्रणाशिनीम् ।
सर्वदा वरदा दुर्गा येयं कात्यायनी मुने ॥
18.m: Pulastya said: / Listen, I will tell the story that destroys sin, / of this Durgā who always grants boons, who is Kātyāyanī, O sage.

18.s:
purāsuravarau raudrau jagatkṣobhakarāvubhau /
rambhaścaiva karambhaś ca dvāvāstāṃ sumābalau //
18.d:
पुरासुरवरौ रौद्रौ जगत्क्षोभकरावुभौ ।
रम्भश्चैव करम्भश् च द्वावास्तां सुमाबलौ ॥
18.m: Formerly there were two formidable best of asuras, who both agitated the world: / Rambha and Karambha, both possessing very great strength.

18.s:
tāvaputrau ca devarṣe putrārthaṃ tepatustapaḥ /
bahūn varṣagaṇān daityau sthitau pañcanade jale //
18.d:
तावपुत्रौ च देवर्षे पुत्रार्थं तेपतुस्तपः ।
बहून् वर्षगणान् दैत्यौ स्थितौ पञ्चनदे जले ॥
18.m: The two of them, sonless, O divine sage, performed austerity for the sake of a son; / for many groups of years the two Daityas stood in the waters of Pañcanada.

18.s:
tatraiko jalamadhyastho dvitīyo 'pyagnipañcamī /
karambhaścaiva rambhaśca yakṣaṃ mālapaṭaṃ prati //
18.d:
तत्रैको जलमध्यस्थो द्वितीयो ऽप्यग्निपञ्चमी ।
करम्भश्चैव रम्भश्च यक्षं मालपटं प्रति ॥
18.m: There one stood in the middle of the water, and the second was in the midst of five fires, / Karambha and Rambha, facing the yakṣa Mālavaṭa.

18.s:
ekaṃ mimagnaṃ salile grāharūpeṇa vāsavaḥ /
caraṇābhyāṃ samādāya nijaghāna yathecchayā //
18.d:
एकं मिमग्नं सलिले ग्राहरूपेण वासवः ।
चरणाभ्यां समादाय निजघान यथेच्छया ॥
18.m: Vāsava, in the form of a crocodile, seized one who was submerged in the water / by both feet and killed him as he pleased.

18.s:
tato bhrātari naṣṭe ca rambhaḥ kopapariplutaḥ /
vahnau svaśīrṣaṃ saṃkṣidya hotumaiccan mahābalaḥ //
18.d:
ततो भ्रातरि नष्टे च रम्भः कोपपरिप्लुतः ।
वह्नौ स्वशीर्षं संक्षिद्य होतुमैच्चन् महाबलः ॥
18.m: Then, when his brother was destroyed, Rambha, overcome with anger, / wishing to cut off his own head, desired to offer it into the fire, having great strength.

18.s:
tataḥ pragṛhya keśeṣu khaṅgaṃ ca ravisaprabham /
chettukāmo nijaṃ śīrṣaṃ vahninā pratiṣedhitaḥ //
18.d:
ततः प्रगृह्य केशेषु खङ्गं च रविसप्रभम् ।
छेत्तुकामो निजं शीर्षं वह्निना प्रतिषेधितः ॥
18.m: Then, grasping his hair and a sword blazing like the sun, / wishing to cut off his own head, he was restrained by the fire.

18.s:
uktaśca mā daityavara nāśayātmānamātmanā /
dustarā paravadhyāpi svavadhyāpyatidustarā //
18.d:
उक्तश्च मा दैत्यवर नाशयात्मानमात्मना ।
दुस्तरा परवध्यापि स्ववध्याप्यतिदुस्तरा ॥
18.m: And he was told: "Do not destroy yourself by your own hand, O best of Daityas! / Even death by another is hard to overcome, but death by oneself is exceedingly hard to overcome.

18.s:
yacca prārthayase vīra taddadāmi yathepsitam /
mā mriyasva mṛtasyeha naṣṭā bhavati vai kathā //
18.d:
यच्च प्रार्थयसे वीर तद्ददामि यथेप्सितम् ।
मा म्रियस्व मृतस्येह नष्टा भवति वै कथा ॥
18.m: And whatever you ask for, O hero, I will give that just as desired; / do not die, for when one is dead here, his story is indeed lost."

18.s:
tato 'bravīd vaco rambho varaṃ cenme dadāsi hi /
trailokyavijayī putraḥ syānme tvattejasādhikaḥ //
18.d:
ततो ऽब्रवीद् वचो रम्भो वरं चेन्मे ददासि हि ।
त्रैलोक्यविजयी पुत्रः स्यान्मे त्वत्तेजसाधिकः ॥
18.m: Then Rambha spoke [these] words: "If you are indeed giving me a boon, / let my son be a conqueror of the three worlds, greater than you in splendor,

18.s:
ajeyo daivataiḥ sarvaiḥ pubhirdaityaiśca pāvaka /
mahābalo vāyuriva kāmarūpī kṛtāstravit //
18.d:
अजेयो दैवतैः सर्वैः पुभिर्दैत्यैश्च पावक ।
महाबलो वायुरिव कामरूपी कृतास्त्रवित् ॥
18.m: unconquerable by all gods, men, and Daityas, O fire, / possessing great strength like the wind, changing shape at will, and skilled in missiles!"

18.s:
taṃ provāca kavirbrahman bāñamevaṃ bhaviṣyati /
yasyāṃ cittaṃ samālambi kariṣyasi tataḥ sutaḥ //
18.d:
तं प्रोवाच कविर्ब्रह्मन् बाञमेवं भविष्यति ।
यस्यां चित्तं समालम्बि करिष्यसि ततः सुतः ॥
18.m: The wise one said to him, O Brahmin: "Indeed, it shall be so. / On whatever [female] you set your mind, from her will be a son."

18.s:
ityevamukto devena vahninā dānavo yayau /
draṣṭuṃ mālavaṭaṃ yakṣaṃ yakṣaiśca parivāritam //
18.d:
इत्येवमुक्तो देवेन वह्निना दानवो ययौ ।
द्रष्टुं मालवटं यक्षं यक्षैश्च परिवारितम् ॥
18.m: Thus spoken to by the divine fire, the Dānava went / to see the yakṣa Mālavaṭa surrounded by yakṣas.

18.s:
teṣāṃ padmanidhistatra vasate nānyacetanaḥ /
gajaśca mahiṣāścāśvā gāvo 'jāvipariplutāḥ //
18.d:
तेषां पद्मनिधिस्तत्र वसते नान्यचेतनः ।
गजश्च महिषाश्चाश्वा गावो ऽजाविपरिप्लुताः ॥
18.m: Their Padmanidhi dwells there, with mind on nothing else; / and elephants, buffaloes, horses, cows, goats, and sheep abound.

18.s:
tān dṛṣṭvaiva tadā cakre bhāvaṃ dānavapārthivaḥ /
mahiṣyāṃ rūpayuktāyāṃ trihāyaṇyāṃ tapodhana //
18.d:
तान् दृष्ट्वैव तदा चक्रे भावं दानवपार्थिवः ।
महिष्यां रूपयुक्तायां त्रिहायण्यां तपोधन ॥
18.m: As soon as he saw them, the king of Dānavas directed his passion / toward a beautiful three-year-old female buffalo, O ascetic.

18.s:
sā samāgācca daityaindraṃ kāmayantī tarasvinī /
sa cāpi gamanaṃ cakre bhavitavyapracoditaḥ //
18.d:
सा समागाच्च दैत्यैन्द्रं कामयन्ती तरस्विनी ।
स चापि गमनं चक्रे भवितव्यप्रचोदितः ॥
18.m: She came to the lord of Daityas, desiring him, swift-paced, / and he too made union, impelled by destiny.

18.s:
tasyāṃ samabhavad garbhastāṃ pragṛhyātha dānavaḥ /
pātālaṃ praviveśātha tataḥ svabhavanaṃ gataḥ //
18.d:
तस्यां समभवद् गर्भस्तां प्रगृह्याथ दानवः ।
पातालं प्रविवेशाथ ततः स्वभवनं गतः ॥
18.m: Conception took place in her; then, taking her, the Dānava / entered Pātāla and then went to his own abode.

18.s:
dṛṣṭaśca dānavaiḥ sarvaiḥ parityaktaśca bandhubhiḥ /
akāryakāraketyevaṃ bhṛyo mālavaṭaṃ gataḥ //
18.d:
दृष्टश्च दानवैः सर्वैः परित्यक्तश्च बन्धुभिः ।
अकार्यकारकेत्येवं भृयो मालवटं गतः ॥
18.m: Seen by all the Dānavas and abandoned by his kin / with the words, "He is a perpetrator of an improper act," he went back to Mālavaṭa.

18.s:
sāpi tenaiva patinā mahiṣī cārudarśanā /
samaṃ jagāma tat puṇyaṃ yakṣamaṇḍalamuttamam //
18.d:
सापि तेनैव पतिना महिषी चारुदर्शना ।
समं जगाम तत् पुण्यं यक्षमण्डलमुत्तमम् ॥
18.m: She too, the beautiful female buffalo, along with that husband, / went together to that sacred, excellent circle of yakṣas.

18.s:
tatastu vasatastasya śyāmā sā suṣuve mune /
ajījanat sutaṃ śubhraṃ mahiṣaṃ kāmarūpiṇam //
18.d:
ततस्तु वसतस्तस्य श्यामा सा सुषुवे मुने ।
अजीजनत् सुतं शुभ्रं महिषं कामरूपिणम् ॥
18.m: Then, as he dwelt there, that dark-skinned one gave birth, O sage; / she brought forth a bright son, a buffalo changing shape at will.

18.s:
etāmṛtumatīṃ jātāṃ mahiṣo 'nyo dadarśa ha /
sā cābhyagād ditivaraṃ rakṣantī śīlamātmanaḥ //
18.d:
एतामृतुमतीं जातां महिषो ऽन्यो ददर्श ह ।
सा चाभ्यगाद् दितिवरं रक्षन्ती शीलमात्मनः ॥
18.m: When she entered her season, another male buffalo saw her, / and she ran toward the best of Diti's line, guarding her own virtue.

18.s:
tamunnāmitanāsaṃ ca mahiṣaṃ vīkṣya dānavaḥ /
khaṅga niṣkṛṣya tarasā mahiṣaṃ samupādravat //
tenāpi daityastīkṣṇābhyāṃ śṛṅgābhyāṃ hṛdi tāḍitaḥ /
nirbhinnahṛdayo bhūmau nipapāta mamāra ca / /
18.d:
तमुन्नामितनासं च महिषं वीक्ष्य दानवः ।
खङ्ग निष्कृष्य तरसा महिषं समुपाद्रवत् ॥
तेनापि दैत्यस्तीक्ष्णाभ्यां शृङ्गाभ्यां हृदि ताडितः ।
निर्भिन्नहृदयो भूमौ निपपात ममार च । ।
18.m:
Seeing that male buffalo with lifted nose, the Dānava / drew his sword and rushed swiftly at the male buffalo.

Struck in the heart by him with his two sharp horns,
the Daitya, with his heart pierced, fell to the ground and died.

18.s:
18.63 mṛte bhartari sā śyāmā yakṣāṇāṃ śaraṇaṃ gatā /
rakṣitā guhyakaiḥ sādhvī nivārya mahiṣaṃ tataḥ //
18.d:
18.63 मृते भर्तरि सा श्यामा यक्षाणां शरणं गता ।
रक्षिता गुह्यकैः साध्वी निवार्य महिषं ततः ॥
18.m:
Her husband dead, the youthful woman sought the protection of the yakṣas;
the virtuous lady, protected by the guhyakas, then drove away the buffalo.

18.s:
tato nivārito yakṣairhayārirmadanāturaḥ /
nipapāta saro divyaṃ tato daityai'bhavanmṛtaḥ //
18.d:
ततो निवारितो यक्षैर्हयारिर्मदनातुरः ।
निपपात सरो दिव्यं ततो दैत्यैऽभवन्मृतः ॥
18.m: Then, warded off by the yakṣas, the enemy of horses, tormented by desire, / fell into a divine lake, and then the Daitya became dead.

18.s:
namaro nāma vikhyāto mahābalaparākramaḥ /
yakṣānāśritya tasthau sa kālayan śvāpadān mun //
18.d:
नमरो नाम विख्यातो महाबलपराक्रमः ।
यक्षानाश्रित्य तस्थौ स कालयन् श्वापदान् मुन् ॥
18.m: Renowned by the name Namara, endowed with great strength and prowess, / he stayed relying on the yakṣas, chasing wild beasts, O sage.

18.s:
sa ca daityeśvaro yakṣairmālavaṭapurassaraiḥ /
citāmāropitaḥ sā ca śyāmā taṃ cāruhat patim //
18.d:
स च दैत्येश्वरो यक्षैर्मालवटपुरस्सरैः ।
चितामारोपितः सा च श्यामा तं चारुहत् पतिम् ॥
18.m: And that lord of Daityas was placed on the funeral pyre by the yakṣas, led by Mālavaṭa, / and that dark-skinned woman ascended it with her husband.

18.s:
tato 'gnimadhyāduttasthau puruṣo raudradarśanaḥ /
vyadrāvayat sa tān yakṣān khaṅgapāṇirbhayaṅkaraḥ //
18.d:
ततो ऽग्निमध्यादुत्तस्थौ पुरुषो रौद्रदर्शनः ।
व्यद्रावयत् स तान् यक्षान् खङ्गपाणिर्भयङ्करः ॥
18.m: Then from the middle of the fire arose a man of terrifying appearance; / with sword in hand, fearsome, he routed those yakṣas.

18.s:
tato hatāstu mahiṣāḥ sarva eva mahātmanā /
ṛte saṃrakṣitāraṃ hi mahiṣaṃ rambhanandanam //
18.d:
ततो हतास्तु महिषाः सर्व एव महात्मना ।
ऋते संरक्षितारं हि महिषं रम्भनन्दनम् ॥
18.m: Then all the male buffaloes were slain by that great-souled one, / except the protector, the buffalo born of Rambha.

18.s:
sa nāmataḥ smṛto daityo raktabījo mahāmun /
yo 'jayat sarvato devān sendrarudrārkamārutān //
18.d:
स नामतः स्मृतो दैत्यो रक्तबीजो महामुन् ।
यो ऽजयत् सर्वतो देवान् सेन्द्ररुद्रार्कमारुतान् ॥
18.m: That Daitya is remembered by the name Raktabīja, O great sage, / who conquered on every side the gods, including Indra, Rudra, the sun, and the winds.

18.s:
evaṃ prabhāvā danupuṅgavāste tejo 'dhikastatra babhau hayāriḥ /
rājye 'bhiṣiktaśca mahāsurendrairvinirjitaiḥ śambaratārakādyaiḥ //
18.d:
एवं प्रभावा दनुपुङ्गवास्ते तेजो ऽधिकस्तत्र बभौ हयारिः ।
राज्ये ऽभिषिक्तश्च महासुरेन्द्रैर्विनिर्जितैः शम्बरतारकाद्यैः ॥
18.m: Of such power were those bulls among Danu's sons; there the enemy of horses shone with superior majesty, / and he was consecrated into kingship by the great lords of asuras who had been vanquished, Śambara, Tāraka, and others.

18.s:
aśaknuvadbhiḥ sahitaiśca devaiḥ salokapālaiḥ sahutāśabhāskaraiḥ /
sthānāni tyaktāni śaśīndrabhāskarairdharmaśca dūre pratiyojitaśca //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe aṣṭādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
18.d:
अशक्नुवद्भिः सहितैश्च देवैः सलोकपालैः सहुताशभास्करैः ।
स्थानानि त्यक्तानि शशीन्द्रभास्करैर्धर्मश्च दूरे प्रतियोजितश्च ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे अष्टादशो ऽध्यायः
18.m:
By the gods unable [to withstand him], together with the world-protectors, with the fire and the sun, / their abodes were abandoned by the moon, Indra, and the sun, and righteousness was cast far away.

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

19.s:
pulastya uvāca /
tatastu devā mahiṣema nirjitāḥ sthānāni saṃtyajya savāhanāyudhāḥ /
jagmuḥ puraskṛtya ricāmahaṃ te draṣṭuṃ tadā cakradharaṃ śriyaḥ patim //
19.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
ततस्तु देवा महिषेम निर्जिताः स्थानानि संत्यज्य सवाहनायुधाः ।
जग्मुः पुरस्कृत्य रिचामहं ते द्रष्टुं तदा चक्रधरं श्रियः पतिम् ॥
19.m: Pulastya said: / Then the gods, vanquished by Mahiṣa, abandoning their abodes with their vehicles and weapons, / placing the Grandfather at their head, went to see the wielder of the discus, the husband of Śrī.

19.s:
gatvā tvapaśyaṃśca mithaḥ surottamau sthitau khagendrāsanaśaṅkarau hi /
dṛṣṭāvā praṇamyaiva ca siddisādhakau nyavedayaṃstanmahiṣādiceṣṭitam //
19.d:
गत्वा त्वपश्यंश्च मिथः सुरोत्तमौ स्थितौ खगेन्द्रासनशङ्करौ हि ।
दृष्टावा प्रणम्यैव च सिद्दिसाधकौ न्यवेदयंस्तन्महिषादिचेष्टितम् ॥
19.m: Going there, they saw the two foremost gods, seated together: / Viṣṇu on Garuḍa and Śaṅkara, fulfillers of all aims; and having bowed down, they reported that conduct of Mahiṣa and the others:

19.s:
prabho 'śvisūryendvanilāgnivedhasāṃ jaleśaśakrādiṣu cādhikārān /
ākramya nākāttu nirākṛtā vayaṃ kṛtāvanisthā mahiṣāsureṇa //
19.d:
प्रभो ऽश्विसूर्येन्द्वनिलाग्निवेधसां जलेशशक्रादिषु चाधिकारान् ।
आक्रम्य नाकात्तु निराकृता वयं कृतावनिस्था महिषासुरेण ॥
19.m: “O Lords, Mahiṣāsura has usurped the domains / of the Aśvins, Sūrya, Candra, Vāyu, Agni, Brahmā, Varuṇa, Indra, and the rest; / and having driven us from heaven, he has reduced us to living on the earth.

19.s:
etad bhavantau śaraṇāgatānāṃ śrutvā vaco brūta hitaṃ surāṇām /
na ced vrajāmo 'dya rasātalaṃ hi saṃkālyamānā yudhi dānavena //
19.d:
एतद् भवन्तौ शरणागतानां श्रुत्वा वचो ब्रूत हितं सुराणाम् ।
न चेद् व्रजामो ऽद्य रसातलं हि संकाल्यमाना युधि दानवेन ॥
19.m: Having heard this plea of the gods who have fled to you for refuge, declare our welfare; / otherwise, being driven in battle by the Dānava, we must go today to Rasātala.”

19.s:
itthaṃ murāriḥ saha śaṅkareṇa śrutvā vaco viplutacetasastān /
dṛṣṭvātha cakre sahasaiva kopaṃ kālāgnikalpo hariravyayātmā //
19.d:
इत्थं मुरारिः सह शङ्करेण श्रुत्वा वचो विप्लुतचेतसस्तान् ।
दृष्ट्वाथ चक्रे सहसैव कोपं कालाग्निकल्पो हरिरव्ययात्मा ॥
19.m: Having thus heard their speech, Murāri, together with Śaṅkara, seeing them distraught in mind, / suddenly flared with rage—Hari of imperishable self, like the fire of cosmic dissolution.

19.s:
tato 'nukopānmadhusūdanasya saśaṅkarasyāpi pitāmahasya /
tathaiva śakrādiṣu daivateṣu maharddhi tejo vadanād viniḥsutam //
19.d:
ततो ऽनुकोपान्मधुसूदनस्य सशङ्करस्यापि पितामहस्य ।
तथैव शक्रादिषु दैवतेषु महर्द्धि तेजो वदनाद् विनिःसुतम् ॥
19.m: Then, following the anger of Madhusūdana, / of Śaṅkara, and also of Pitāmaha, / as well as of Indra and the gods, a brilliant light of great power issued from their mouths.

19.s:
taccaikatāṃ parvatakūṭasannibhaṃ jagāma tejaḥ pravarāśram mune /
kātyāyanasyāpratimasya tena maharṣiṇā teja upākṛtaṃ ca //
19.d:
तच्चैकतां पर्वतकूटसन्निभं जगाम तेजः प्रवराश्रम् मुने ।
कात्यायनस्याप्रतिमस्य तेन महर्षिणा तेज उपाकृतं च ॥
19.m: That light, resembling a mountain peak, coalesced and went to the foremost hermitage, O sage, / of the matchless Kātyāyana; and by that great sage the light was received and magnified.

19.s:
tenārṣisṛṣṭena ca teja-sā vṛtaṃ jvalatprakāśārkasahasratulyam /
